ABOUT THE TEAM

The Hardware Engineering team designs and delivers the electromechanical systems that allow NEO to move, manipulate, and interact safely with the world. From structural components and precision mechanisms to complete robotic subsystems, the team owns hardware development from concept through production.

Working closely with electrical, controls, firmware, manufacturing, and robotics engineers, you'll help transform ambitious ideas into robust, manufacturable products that operate reliably in real-world environments.




YOUR CHARTER

Design and deliver lightweight, structurally optimized, highly integrated structures that enable NEO’s hands to perform reliably and be manufactured at scale.

You will design and develop structural components and assemblies that integrate actuators, electronics, mechanisms, sensors, wiring, and thermal hardware within extremely constrained mechanical envelopes.

You will use structural analysis, FEA, optimization, and physical testing to drive design decisions and develop hardware that balances stiffness, strength, mass, packaging, reliability, manufacturability, and cost.




KEY OUTCOMES

 - Design and release structural components and assemblies that meet performance, reliability, cost, and manufacturability requirements

 - Drive designs from concept through detailed design, prototyping, validation, and production release

 - Design for high-volume manufacturing and drive DFM, DFA, tolerance analysis, and cost optimization throughout development

 - Work closely with electrical, thermal, materials, test, and manufacturing teams to define interfaces and develop integrated mechanical solutions

 - Work directly with suppliers and manufacturing partners to resolve DFM issues, validate production processes, and support production ramp

 - Support hardware through production ramp and continuous improvement, identifying and resolving design, reliability, and manufacturing issues

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Power Systems team develops the electrical architectures and power electronics that enable NEO to operate safely, reliably, and efficiently. We design and integrate power conversion, distribution, motor drives, battery interfaces, and embedded electrical systems across the robot.



Our work spans high-frequency switching electronics, power integrity, electromagnetic compatibility, sensing, communication interfaces, and system-level electrical integration. We collaborate closely with Electrical Engineering, Firmware, Mechanical Engineering, Controls, and Systems Engineering to solve complex challenges associated with tightly integrated robotic hardware.



As NEO moves from development into scaled production, ensuring electromagnetic compatibility across interconnected electrical systems is critical to product performance, safety, reliability, and manufacturing readiness.




YOUR CHARTER

Own the EMI/EMC strategy and solve complex electromagnetic interference challenges across NEO's robotic platform.



As a Staff Electrical Engineer specializing in EMI/EMC, you will serve as the technical authority responsible for investigating, debugging, and resolving complex electromagnetic interference and compatibility issues across NEO's electrical systems.



You will lead system-level EMI/EMC investigations, identify interference sources and coupling mechanisms, develop mitigation strategies, and validate corrective actions through rigorous testing and quantitative measurements.



Working hands-on with electrical hardware, laboratory instrumentation, and fully integrated robotic systems, you will partner with engineering teams to improve grounding, shielding, filtering, PCB layout, cable routing, and system-level electrical integration.



You will establish EMI/EMC engineering standards, influence electrical architecture decisions, mentor engineers, and develop scalable validation methodologies that reduce development risk and improve reliability across the robotic platform.




KEY OUTCOMES

 - Lead EMI/EMC technical strategy, investigation, and resolution across PCB, subsystem, and complete robot levels.

 - Identify, characterize, and resolve conducted and radiated electromagnetic interference generated by switching power supplies, DC-DC converters, motor drives, battery management systems, chargers, and power distribution electronics.

 - Diagnose complex common-mode and differential-mode noise, ground loops, parasitic coupling, switching transients, and interference affecting sensitive electronic systems.

 - Develop and implement effective EMI mitigation strategies involving PCB layout, grounding architecture, shielding, filtering, cable routing, and component selection.

 - Establish repeatable EMI/EMC testing, troubleshooting, and validation methodologies that accelerate root-cause identification and corrective action.

 - Lead conducted and radiated emissions testing, electromagnetic immunity testing, ESD testing, and other relevant pre-compliance evaluations.

 - Validate corrective actions through quantitative measurements, documented test results, and before-and-after performance comparisons.

 - Drive system-level electrical integration improvements to prevent interference between power electronics, embedded controllers, sensors, and communication interfaces.

 - Lead external compliance testing efforts and resolve EMI/EMC failures identified during formal qualification.

 - Partner with Power Systems, Electrical Engineering, Firmware, Controls, Mechanical Engineering, and Systems Engineering teams to address complex cross-functional interference challenges.

 - Establish EMI/EMC design guidelines, validation standards, and engineering best practices that reduce late-stage redesigns and improve product readiness.

 - Provide technical leadership and mentorship to engineers across multiple hardware teams.




KEY COMPETENCIES

 - Deep expertise in electromagnetic interference, electromagnetic compatibility, conducted and radiated emissions, and electromagnetic coupling mechanisms.

 - Advanced understanding of grounding, shielding, filtering, PCB layout, return-current paths, and high-frequency electrical behavior.

 - Strong knowledge of switching power electronics, motor drives, DC-DC converters, power distribution, and parasitic effects.

 - Exceptional hands-on troubleshooting skills with the ability to systematically identify interference sources, coupling paths, and susceptible circuits.

 - Advanced proficiency with EMI/EMC laboratory instrumentation, including spectrum analyzers, EMI receivers, oscilloscopes, VNAs, LISNs, current probes, and near-field probes.

 - Strong analytical mindset with the ability to use first-principles reasoning, measurements, and structured experimentation to drive engineering decisions.

 - Ability to develop practical EMI mitigation solutions while balancing electrical performance, size, mass, thermal constraints, reliability, and manufacturing cost.

 - Proven ability to lead complex, cross-functional technical investigations and influence electrical system architecture.

 - Strong communication, technical leadership, and mentorship skills across multidisciplinary engineering teams.




MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

 - Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related technical discipline.

 - 7+ years of electrical engineering experience with significant hands-on responsibility for EMI/EMC design, testing, and troubleshooting.

 - Proven track record of leading complex EMI/EMC investigations and independently resolving system-level interference challenges in physical hardware.

 - Deep understanding of conducted and radiated emissions, electromagnetic coupling, grounding, shielding, filtering, and noise mitigation techniques.

 - Extensive hands-on experience using EMI receivers, spectrum analyzers, oscilloscopes, Vector Network Analyzers (VNAs), LISNs, near-field probes, current probes, and related laboratory instrumentation.

 - Experience using VNAs for antenna, chassis, or related electromagnetic characterization.

 - Strong knowledge of high-frequency switching circuits, power electronics, PCB layout, parasitic inductance, and return-current paths.

 - Experience troubleshooting EMI/EMC issues involving switched-mode power supplies, DC-DC converters, motor drives, or similar power electronics.

 - Demonstrated ability to develop EMI/EMC test strategies, reproduce complex interference problems, identify root causes, and validate corrective actions.

 - Experience leading EMI/EMC pre-compliance testing and supporting formal compliance evaluations.

 - Ability to analyze electrical schematics, review PCB layouts, and influence design and architecture improvements.

 - Demonstrated technical leadership, including driving cross-functional engineering initiatives, establishing best practices, or mentoring other engineers.

 - Strong analytical, problem-solving, documentation, and technical communication skills.




PREFERRED SKILLS

 - EMI/EMC experience with robotics, electric vehicles, industrial automation, aerospace, or other complex electromechanical systems.

 - Experience troubleshooting EMI generated by GaN or SiC switching power electronics.

 - Knowledge of CISPR, IEC 61000, FCC Part 15, and other applicable electromagnetic compatibility standards.

 - Experience with motor inverters, high-current battery systems, high-frequency power converters, and multi-board embedded electronics.

 - Experience troubleshooting interference affecting CAN, Ethernet, EtherCAT, and other high-speed or industrial communication interfaces.

 - Familiarity with electromagnetic simulation tools such as Ansys SIwave, HFSS, CST, or equivalent.

 - Experience developing system-level EMI/EMC strategies for complex integrated hardware products.

 - Experience with ESD, electrical fast transients (EFT), electromagnetic immunity, and related robustness testing.

 - Experience working directly with external EMC laboratories and leading regulatory qualification activities.

 - Experience developing EMI/EMC design guidelines, test methodologies, and engineering standards.

 - Experience operating in fast-paced hardware environments with rapid design iteration, frequent prototype builds, and complex system-level integration challenges.

About The Role

As a Senior Beamline Scientist/Engineer at Antares, you will lead the testing, commissioning, and experimental validation of particle accelerator systems supporting nuclear technology development. Working within system requirements and performance specifications established by technical leadership, you will develop and execute test plans, characterize beamline performance, and provide experimental results and technical recommendations that inform hardware development and engineering decisions.

This role combines experimental physics with hands-on test engineering. Working closely with nuclear, mechanical, electrical, controls, and radiation protection teams, you will support the integration and operation of ion sources, beam transport systems, vacuum infrastructure, diagnostics, and associated instrumentation. You will take ownership of test planning, execution, data analysis, and performance verification while contributing to hardware development and troubleshooting. As a senior individual contributor, you will independently lead experimental activities, establish repeatable testing methodologies, mentor teammates, and help ensure safe and reliable operation of experimental systems.

Job Responsibilities

 - Own the development and execution of beamline test plans, commissioning procedures, and experimental validation activities based on established system requirements and performance specifications.

 - Develop test methodologies, measurement techniques, and acceptance criteria in coordination with system engineering and technical leadership.

 - Support the design, development, and integration of beamline hardware, including ion sources, beam extraction and transport, focusing and steering elements, neutralizers, vacuum systems, diagnostics, and experimental fixtures.

 - Lead experimental characterization of beamline performance, including beam current, energy, spatial distribution, divergence, stability, and measurement uncertainty.

 - Perform or support beam optics, particle transport, plasma, and radiation transport simulations to inform experimental configurations, interpret results, and investigate performance discrepancies.

 - Develop and integrate test instrumentation, including beam diagnostics, detectors, data acquisition systems, and associated measurement hardware.

 - Support hardware assembly, alignment, installation, integration, and commissioning activities in collaboration with responsible engineering teams.

 - Collaborate with electrical and controls engineers to integrate power supplies, instrumentation, data acquisition, monitoring, and safety interlocks into experimental test systems.

 - Lead troubleshooting and root-cause investigations of beamline performance issues, instrumentation failures, and experimental anomalies, coordinating corrective actions with hardware development teams.

 - Analyze experimental data, assess measurement uncertainties, and document test results to evaluate system performance against established requirements.

 - Provide technical recommendations and experimental feedback to support beamline design improvements, hardware modifications, and system optimization.

 - Work with radiation protection and facility teams to develop test procedures, establish safe operating conditions, and support experimental readiness reviews.

 - Coordinate with vendors and external research facilities to support specialized testing, instrumentation development, and hardware qualification.

 - Maintain test documentation, calibration records, experimental procedures, and performance reports to ensure traceability and repeatability.

 - Mentor engineers and scientists in experimental methods, instrumentation, data analysis, and safe laboratory practices.

Basic Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in physics, nuclear engineering, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical discipline.

 - Five or more years of relevant experience in experimental physics, test engineering, accelerator systems, particle beamlines, or scientific instrumentation; relevant graduate research may count toward this experience.

 - Demonstrated experience developing and executing test plans, commissioning procedures, or experimental validation activities for complex scientific or engineering systems.

 - Strong understanding of experimental physics, particle interactions with matter, measurement techniques, and quantitative data analysis.

 - Hands-on experience integrating, operating, and troubleshooting scientific instrumentation, vacuum systems, detectors, power supplies, or data acquisition hardware.

 - Experience with experimental characterization, instrument calibration, measurement uncertainty, and performance verification.

 - Experience using scientific computing tools such as Python, MATLAB, or C++ for data analysis, simulation, automation, or instrument control.

 - Ability to apply first-principles calculations and computational modeling to experimental design, troubleshooting, and interpretation of measured performance.

 - Experience working within established laboratory safety procedures, including high-voltage, vacuum, radiation, or other relevant experimental hazards.

 - Ability to independently plan and execute experimental activities, investigate technical problems, and communicate results across multidisciplinary engineering teams.



Preferred Qualifications

 - Master's degree or Ph.D. in physics, nuclear engineering, accelerator physics, or a related discipline.

 - Experience testing, commissioning, or operating charged-particle accelerators, ion beam systems, neutral particle beams, or plasma-based ion sources.

 - Understanding of charged-particle beam physics, including beam extraction, electrostatic or magnetic focusing, beam transport, and neutralization techniques.

 - Experience with ultra-high-vacuum systems, high-voltage equipment, RF or microwave plasma systems, and associated instrumentation.

 - Experience with beam diagnostics, including Faraday cups, beam profile monitors, energy analyzers, or other charged-particle measurement systems.

 - Familiarity with particle optics or multiphysics simulation tools such as IBSimu, SIMION, COMSOL, or equivalent software.

 - Experience developing automated test systems, instrument control interfaces, or experimental data acquisition software.

 - Experience with hardware acceptance testing, subsystem qualification, commissioning, and performance verification.

 - Experience developing technical test reports, experimental procedures, and measurement uncertainty assessments.

Additional Requirements:

 - Ability to work long hours and weekends as necessary to support critical milestones

 - Ability to travel to customer and mission-relevant locations as needed.

 - Ability to obtain a Top Secret or Top Secret SCI clearance is preferred.

Location

 - We are located in Torrance, CA in a 322,000 square foot, brand new facility featuring large open spaces for team collaboration, R&D, and production, as well as easy access to the 405, 105, and 110 freeways. Our facility is in the heart of Los Angeles' vibrant emerging tech ecosystem alongside many other high growth startups and enterprises.





Culture

At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful:

 - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system

 - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle

 - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done”

 - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together

 - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption

About the Role

Antares is seeking a Licensing Lead to build and lead the organization responsible for obtaining regulatory authorizations for advanced microreactor deployments. Depending on experience and demonstrated scope, the position may be leveled as Licensing Lead, Licensing Manager, Licensing Senior Manager, or Director of Licensing. The selected leader will develop licensing and safety-basis strategies, build the team and operating model needed to execute them, and maintain accountability for authorization progress and outcomes across DOE, Department of War, and NRC deployment pathways.

The role will initially lead a team of approximately five people and is expected to develop the organization to 10-12 people over the next two years. The leader will oversee licensing products, safety-basis processes, regulatory engagements, schedules, budgets, risks, commitments, and cross-functional execution. Success will require close coordination with engineering, safety analysis, nuclear operations, quality, deployment, program management, customers, regulators, and government stakeholders. State and local permitting interfaces may also be included depending on the selected candidate's level and experience.



Roles and Responsibilities

 - Develop and maintain integrated licensing, authorization, safety-basis, and regulatory engagement strategies for DOE, Department of War, and NRC deployments.

 - Build, organize, mentor, and manage a licensing team.

 - Establish clear roles, interfaces, technical expectations, review standards, priorities, and accountability for licensing and safety-basis work.

 - Develop and manage licensing schedules, budgets, staffing plans, deliverables, milestones, metrics, risk registers, and executive reporting.

 - Oversee the preparation, review, approval, and implementation of license applications, authorization packages, safety documents, white papers, topical reports, technical briefs, and regulator responses.

 - Manage regulator comments, requests for additional information, commitments, decisions, owners, due dates, objective evidence, and closure status.

 - Translate applicable requirements and licensing positions into actionable design, analysis, testing, programmatic, operational, quality, and documentation requirements.

 - Lead regulator and stakeholder engagement planning and represent Antares in technical, programmatic, executive, customer, and government meetings.

 - Identify licensing and authorization risks early, develop alternative strategies, evaluate tradeoffs, and elevate decisions with clear recommendations.

 - Coordinate with engineering, safety analysis, operations, quality, deployment, mission, and legal teams to maintain integrated execution.

 - Establish scalable licensing processes, governance, tools, records, configuration control, performance indicators, and lessons-learned practices.

 - Provide leadership with accurate forecasts and clear assessments of progress, readiness, risk, resource needs, and authorization confidence.

 - Oversee state and local permitting interfaces when assigned based on role level or deployment needs.

Basic Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in engineering or another relevant technical discipline.

 - Demonstrated experience developing and implementing licensing, authorization, or safety-basis documentation in a regulated technical environment.

 - Evidence of carrying complex regulatory products through review, comment resolution, implementation, and successful application or authorization outcomes.

 - Ability to develop practical licensing strategies and convert them into integrated plans, deliverables, responsibilities, and measurable progress.

 - Strong technical judgment and the ability to evaluate competing approaches, uncertainties, precedents, and downstream consequences.

 - Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary work, develop personnel, resolve organizational interfaces, and maintain accountability for quality and schedule.

 - Excellent technical writing, executive communication, regulator engagement, and stakeholder-management skills.

 - Ability to operate effectively in an ambiguous, fast-paced environment while building durable processes and organizational capability.
   
   

Preferred Skills & Experience

 - Prior experience leading, managing, or developing a licensing or safety-basis team.

 - Successful experience with one or more DOE, Department of War, Army, NRC, commercial nuclear, advanced reactor, national laboratory, or comparable authorization pathways.

 - Experience developing organizational staffing plans, budgets, schedules, performance measures, and resource strategies.

 - Experience presenting regulatory strategy, progress, risk, and decision needs to executives, regulators, customers, and senior government leaders.

 - Experience establishing scalable licensing processes for multiple projects, sites, or deployments.

 - Familiarity with systems engineering, design control, safety analysis, nuclear quality assurance, configuration management, operations, and readiness processes.

About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array and parabolic ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.



Role: 

A satellite pass gives you a limited window to acquire the signal, track it as Doppler shifts the carrier frequency, and recover data as signal conditions change. As a DSP Engineer at Northwood, you’ll own the modem algorithms that make those links work on our next-generation radio platform.

You’ll take the modem from waveform definition and prototyping through real-time implementation on our in-house SDR and FPGA platform. You’ll decide how the signal-processing chain comes together, where each function runs, and how to measure performance under realistic channel conditions. You’ll work closely with RF, FPGA, and systems engineers to integrate your design and see how your algorithm choices translate into link performance across Northwood’s satellite ground network.


Responsibilities: 

 - Own the definition and development of modem algorithms end-to-end, from requirements through implementation and validation

 - Define waveform processing chains — synchronization, pulse shaping, equalization, and related signal-processing functions — for implementation on an in-house SDR platform or FPGA

 - Partition and implement modem signal-processing functions across FPGA logic and embedded/host-based compute, working within the existing hardware platform

 - Collaborate with RF, FPGA, and systems engineers to integrate modem algorithms into the end-to-end system and validate performance

 - Develop and run communication system tests to characterize modem performance under realistic channel impairments



Basic Qualifications: 

 - Bachelor's degree with 0-4 years of relevant experience in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field

 - Experience developing modems or waveform processing chains for SDR, wireless communications, radar, or similar RF systems

 - Strong understanding of digital communications theory: CCSDS waveforms, BPSK/QPSK/OQPSK, DVB-S2, carrier synchronization, pulse shaping, equalization, and Doppler effects

 - Demonstrated ability to carry waveform algorithms from analysis and prototyping through to a working implementation, rather than stopping at simulation

 - Working understanding of the complete signal chain and how modem design decisions interact with RF and hardware constraints

 - Experience with communication system testing and performance characterization



Preferred Qualifications: 

 - Experience with bit-equivalence verification through FPGAs

 - Familiarity with SDR frameworks such as GNU Radio

 - Experience with real-time signal processing

 - Systems programming skills in C++ or Rust, with Rust especially valued

 - Experience with beamforming, radar, or electronic warfare (EW) systems

ABOUT US

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Sierra was co-founded by Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/ who first met while working together at Google over 20 years ago. Bret currently serves as Chairman of the Board of Open AI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce and CTO of Facebook. Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Support our Sales, Marketing, and customer-facing teams, which might include:
   
   - Driving end-to-end GTM processes, including developing customer presentations, and delivering financial analyses to enable team success.
   
   - Analyzing, optimizing, and implementing sales territories and processes for a fast-growing sales team.
   
   - Building out prospecting programs and marketing campaigns, helping the sales team to drive net new demand
   
   - Help define and scale the playbook for how Sierra builds, evaluates, launches, and expands AI agents at large enterprises.
   
   - Work closely with account teams to identify whitespace, prioritize expansion opportunities, and build repeatable motions that convert post-sale momentum into durable revenue growth.

 - Work with Pricing, Legal, Operations, Sales, Agent Development & Finance teams to identify inefficiencies in current GTM operations and design scalable solutions to help Sierra scale.

 - Turn insight into action: Analyze complex datasets and translate findings into clear, executive-ready recommendations that drive high-leverage decisions.

 - Take on special projects and initiatives related to international expansion, pricing, marketing, legal, deal strategy

 - Serve as a versatile, proactive team player, taking on both foundational tasks and high-impact strategic initiatives that drive the GTM team’s success.

 - Leverage AI-native tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex to build lightweight internal systems, automate workflows, and create operational leverage.


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 4+ years of experience in revenue operations, sales operations, management consulting, corporate strategy, or business operations.

 - Proficiency in financial modeling and data analysis (e.g., Excel, Google Sheets); experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Looker, or Power BI).

 - A detail-oriented, methodical, and process-driven mentality that is focused on both accuracy and efficiency.

 - Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects, prioritize effectively, and meet deadlines.

 - A proactive mindset with the ability to navigate ambiguity, drive and execute initiatives, and deliver results in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex ideas and problems into straightforward, actionable recommendations, especially to executives.


EVEN BETTER…

 - SQL experience.

 - Familiarity with CRM platforms (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot) and marketing automation tools.

 - Previous 0-1 startup or operational experience.


OUR VALUES

 - Trust: We do the right thing, even when no one is looking, and even when it’s hard. When we screw up, we take accountability, fully and completely. We act in such a way that if all of our actions were completely visible to our customers, we would be proud.

 - Customer Obsession: Our entire business is designed to ensure every agent built on Sierra succeeds, and that we are accountable to our customers and their success. We do whatever it takes to make our customers successful, and we go the extra mile in how we show up as a partner with unreasonable hospitality.

 - Craftsmanship: A great company is the aggregation of thousands of things done well. As they say, “how you do anything is how you do everything”. Most important is craftsmanship in building agents that are so great that people thank them at the end of a call. That’s the standard.

 - Intensity: We operate with urgency, and we want to win. We are never complacent. We fight to win every deal, big or small, using the full force of the company. And when we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

 - Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We work hard, and turn on the afterburners when needed. But we pick up our parents at the airport when they’re visiting from out of town. We go to our kids’ events. And we show up for one another, in moments of celebration and hardship.

Ambrook helps American family-run businesses become more profitable and resilient.
From volatile markets to climate shifts, independent operators face mounting pressure. While sustainable investments often yield the best long-term returns, they require financial clarity and capital that fragmented legacy systems can’t provide.

We are rebuilding the financial infrastructure that real economy operators rely on. By replacing paperwork with modern tools for accounting, banking, and spending, Ambrook gives owners the data they need to prove viability to lenders and the next generation. We empower the stewards of land and labor to make confident investments in their future.

We’re a Series B startup backed by Lachy Groom, Thrive Capital, Dylan Field, Thomson Reuters Ventures, Cameron Ventures, and leaders at Notion, Gusto, and Vercel. We’re looking for team members to help us untangle the intersection of American industry, climate, and the economy.

The opportunity

Ambrook’s AI Platform engineers build the shared systems that make everyone at Ambrook faster: engineers, operators, and the teams shipping AI to our customers. You’ll own two closely linked areas:

 - AI platform: the frameworks, evals, harnesses, sandboxes, tool integrations, and interfaces that let any team build, deploy, and operate agents with confidence.

 - Internal tooling: the environments, workflows, and internal products that shape how Ambrook's commercial team runs the business.

We’re working toward a world where any team can request an agent, deploy it, run evals against it, and see the results on a dashboard. Getting there means solving hard problems:

 - how agents get safe, auditable access to tools and data

 - how can we share these tools safely and securely, with auditable access

 - how can we publish custom apps or agents to share with customers

 - how we know whether a change made an agent better or worse

 - how we trace and debug what an agent did

 - how coding agents and engineers work well together in our codebase

 - how we keep cost, latency, and reliability in check as usage grows

This is engineering work, not IT. You’ll treat the people who use what you build as customers: learn how they work, iterate quickly from real feedback, and hold the quality, security, and data-integrity standards a financial product requires. Our stack is mostly TypeScript on GCP.

You’ll decide which problems are worth solving, define the patterns other teams follow, and change how the whole company works.

Within 1 month you’ll…

 - Build a working mental model of how Ambrook builds software and uses AI today: internal agent workflows, customer-facing agentic features, developer workflows and tooling, and where each breaks down.

 - Build relationships with non-engineering teams to learn where friction slows them down, and where agents could remove it.

 - Ship a meaningful improvement to production that makes it faster, safer, or easier to build software or run an agent at Ambrook.

 - Turn those conversations into a prioritized view of the biggest platform opportunities.

Within 3 months you’ll…

 - Own a platform project from discovery through rollout and adoption, such as an agent configuration interface, a shared evaluation system, a sandboxed harness for running agent loops, or a major developer workflow improvement.

 - Stand up a repeatable way to evaluate agents, so teams measure quality before and after a change instead of relying on spot checks.

 - Give agent runs real observability, including tracing, cost, latency, and failure visibility, so teams can debug and improve what they ship.

 - Set the defaults for how agents at Ambrook get context, permissions, and review, and get other teams to adopt them.

Within 6 months you’ll…

 - Own the roadmap for AI platform and developer experience, informed by internal customer needs, where the field is heading, and Ambrook’s standards for quality, security, and auditability.

 - Expand shared infrastructure that supports both internal workflows and customer-facing agentic features, including reusable evals, harnesses, sandboxes, tool integrations, and operational tooling.

 - Make it possible for a team outside engineering to request, deploy, and evaluate an agent with minimal help.

 - Show a measurable change in how Ambrook builds, such as engineering velocity, agent quality, or hours given back to operational teams.

 - Raise the bar for how Ambrook ships AI, internal tools, and customer-facing prototypes through clear design, mentorship, and production ownership.

 

About you

 - You have senior or staff-level experience building production systems that other engineers and teams depend on, and you’ve worked hands-on with LLMs in production.

 - You’ve built infrastructure for agentic systems, such as evals, agent loops, harnesses, sandboxes, or tool integrations, not only individual agents.

 - You care about developer experience and have improved how a team builds, tests, or ships software.

 - You think rigorously about measuring AI quality and understand the limits of evals, LLM-as-judge, and offline testing.

 - You treat internal teams as customers. You learn how they work, build with empathy, and measure success by adoption.

 - You can move quickly while holding the reliability and quality standards that shared infrastructure requires.

 - You’re security-minded and treat agent permissions, data access, prompt injection, auditability, and failure modes as part of ordinary engineering work.

 - Bonus: Experience with coding agents in a production codebase, tool protocols like MCP, or running untrusted code in sandboxes.

 - Bonus: Experience building financial products or systems where auditability and data integrity matter.

About Amplify

Amplify helps teachers bring delight and rigor to students every day. Job Description Summary:

Amplify is seeking a strategic and experienced Manager of State Adoptions to lead our high-stakes statewide implementation efforts. In this pivotal, customer-facing individual contributor role, you will oversee the full lifecycle of state-level partnerships—ranging from "Full Statewide Implementations" (e.g., North Carolina, Louisiana, and Alaska) to complex "Opt-In Implementations" (e.g., Colorado and Connecticut).

You will serve as the primary strategic escalation point for state leaders and own the customer journey through the entire lifecycle, from launch through post-sale, ensuring a superior customer experience. Your expertise will ensure that state-specific nuances—from complex data enrollment to political stakeholder management—are handled with precision and empathy. You act as a trusted advisor and coach, mitigating risk and driving value to ensure our partners fully leverage Amplify’s suite of products.



Essential Responsibilities:

Account Ownership & Strategic State Success

 - Primary Point of Contact: Serve as the main point of contact for state-level implementations, owning the entire customer journey for your defined state book of business. Act as the accountable party for account success, retention, and renewal of high-stakes contracts.

 - Executive Stakeholder Engagement: Engage with and advise state leaders, district leaders, school admins, teachers, and other decision-makers. You will navigate complex or emotionally charged client relationships, acting as a stabilizing force during implementation challenges.

 - Strategic Planning: Regularly review plans, objectives, and initiatives to ensure they remain aligned with the evolving needs of States, Districts, Schools, Teachers, and Students. Develop advanced success plans that align with state goals to facilitate successful contract continuation. Cultivate robust partnerships with account leaders (instructional and technical) to develop long-term student achievement strategies and set multi-year goals.

 - Trusted Advisor: Act as a consultant and coach to state leaders, defining and measuring the realization of curriculum objectives. Serve as the primary point of contact, collaborating closely with internal teams to deliver a superior experience.

Implementation, Onboarding & Complex Project Orchestration

 - Complex Project Orchestration: Oversee and execute massive logistical hurdles specific to state contracts, including:
   
   - North Carolina: Managing quarterly complex invoicing, reading camps, and enrollment system updates.
   
   - Louisiana: Coordinating presence at the Teacher Leader Summit and managing biannual invoicing.
   
   - Connecticut: Overseeing contractor-managed Data Sharing Agreements (DSAs) and complex internal collaborations.

 - Project Management & Onboarding: Execute detailed project plans for implementations. Create and manage state tracking documents, implementation documents, and agendas for state-specific meetings to define project priorities, ensuring launch readiness and success. Track meeting notes and documentation meticulously. Oversee massive logistical hurdles specific to state contracts (e.g., managing complex invoicing in NC, coordinating Summit presence in LA, or overseeing DSAs in CT).

 - Risk Management: Proactively identify risks, political launch blockers, and contractual non-compliance issues; alert stakeholders and implement solutions or workarounds to keep projects on track.

 - Operational Excellence: Leverage project tracking tools for consistency; maintain knowledge of project status to communicate effectively with internal and external partners. Manage state-specific inboxes to ensure timely responses and update state-specific websites with relevant resources and announcements.

 - Resource Coordination: Coordinate the development of Professional Learning plans and involve product specialists as needed to meet state requirements. Provide 1:1 support and/or outreach to districts within the state as needed to ensure the "last mile" of adoption is successful.

Business Value & Data Analysis

 - Data & Technical Oversight: Drive the resolution of enrollment issues and data discrepancies, particularly in states without Master Data Management (MDO) or dedicated support structures.

 - Data-Driven Insights: Plan and prepare data for reviews, and support the presentation of data in person and/or in remote data review sessions. Review and analyze account data to understand usage trends, develop actionable insights, and navigate difficult reporting groups. Share these impact reviews with state leaders to inform ongoing curriculum strategy and drive ROI.

 - Contract & Revenue Management: Develop a deep understanding of customer contracts, including complex, non-standard invoicing schedules (quarterly vs. biannual), to ensure compliance and proactively make recommendations. Support renewal efforts and identify opportunities for upselling.

 - Health Monitoring: Accurately report and monitor the health of state engagements, partnering with internal teams on service level reporting to drive corrective action plans where needed.

Customer Enablement & Continuous Improvement

 - Webinar Strategy: Support state-specific webinars, including content creation and supporting/leading live webinar sessions to train and inform users.

 - Process Optimization: Continue to identify and leverage technology solutions to streamline and personalize interactions at all levels of State Contracts.

 - Feedback Loops: Collect and incorporate customer feedback by regularly soliciting input through surveys, interviews, and active listening. Use this feedback to refine processes, address risks, and enhance the overall customer experience.

Cross-Functional Strategy & Expertise

 - Escalation Resolution: Intervene when support tickets are slow or incorrect (e.g., Alaska) and troubleshoot internal roadblocks across Sales, Professional Development (PD), Customer Success (CS), and Product teams.

 - Internal Partnership: Partner with internal teams to support state implementations, resolve customer issues, and inform the approach to customer lifecycle processes.

 - Customized Reporting: Manage frequent and customized data requests, ensuring nuanced data reviews for state partners.

 - Event Strategy: Direct strategy for in-person support at key state events, such as Science of Reading (SoR) conventions and Teacher of the Year (TOY) data reviews.

 - Product Mastery: Maintain expertise across Amplify’s suite of products (focusing on Literacy and/or STEM) to advise state accounts across all curriculum needs.



Required Qualifications:

 - Education: Bachelor’s Degree or related work experience.

 - Experience: 1+ years of experience in Account Management or Customer Success, with a proven track record managing statewide implementations or large-scale district adoptions.

 - Data Fluency: Deep understanding of data enrollment systems, reporting groups, and Data Sharing Agreements (DSAs).

 - Escalation Management: Proven track record in handling high-stakes customer escalations and fostering positive resolutions.

 - Communication: Exceptional verbal, written, and presentation skills, with the ability to engage and influence stakeholders at all executive levels; ability to create detailed reports and meeting minutes.

 - Strategic & Project Management Skills: Strong strategic thinking, organizational skills, project management skills, and the ability to drive results independently in a fast-paced environment.

 - Independence: Resourcefulness, independent problem-solving ability, and comfort operating under ambiguity.

 - Financial Acumen: Experience reviewing and managing complex, non-standard invoicing schedules (quarterly vs. biannual).




Preferred Qualifications:

 - Industry Knowledge: Experience in education, school/district leadership, or educational publishing/technology.

 - Subject Matter: Background in Elementary Literacy and/or STEM; experience teaching or using Amplify products.

 - Technical Proficiency: Experience with Salesforce, Gainsight, and Google Suite.

Job Description Summary:

The IT Services Analyst helps maintain the stability, efficiency, and reliability of Amplify’s core enterprise applications. This role will investigate application issues by bringing together system data, user input, and operational trends; apply established practices to resolve problems; and recommend improvements or alternative solutions after identifying recurring causes or opportunities. Working with business and technical teams across all lines of business, this role will own assigned support and operational work, contribute to projects—including phases of larger initiatives—and help improve application adoption, reporting, integrations, and the evaluation of new enterprise applications, including emerging AI technologies.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Investigate and resolve application incidents and service requests, using sound judgment within established procedures and identifying root causes, business impact, and appropriate next steps.

 - Monitor and support third-party software applications, APIs, and system integrations; coordinate with systems administrators and other technical partners to diagnose issues and restore service.

 - Apply and interpret departmental application-support policies, procedures, and standards; identify when an issue requires an exception, escalation, or review of the current approach.

 - Review and reconcile information from application dashboards, system logs, operational reports, case trends, and usage data to identify data-quality concerns, performance issues, and operational risks.

 - Analyze recurring incidents, application usage, and support trends; recommend practical changes that reduce repeat problems and improve reliability, usability, or efficiency.

 - Support analysis of software adoption and license utilization, and present evidence-based recommendations for consolidations, tier changes, or other adjustments.

 - Maintain and improve operational reports, dashboards, supporting materials, and data validation practices; clearly explain findings to technical and non-technical audiences.

 - Gather business and operational needs and translate them into clear system, reporting, or process requirements in partnership with stakeholders.

 - Own assigned application-support projects and defined workstreams, including significant phases of greater efforts; evaluate options, coordinate dependencies, track outcomes, and surface risks or blockers.

 - Contribute to annual IT Services objectives by completing assigned deliverables and communicating progress, decisions, and dependencies in an Agile or other structured work environment.

 - Create and maintain support training materials, process guides, standard operating procedures, and end-user documentation.

 - Evaluate new, existing, and emerging AI technologies for relevant support or business use cases, documenting findings and partnering with stakeholders on appropriate next steps.

 - Work collaboratively across IT and business teams, adapting communication to the audience and constructively managing routine disagreements or competing needs.



Minimum Qualifications:

 - Demonstrated ability to independently evaluate support issues, select appropriate procedures, and resolve moderately complex problems within established practices, escalating issues that exceed defined authority or expertise.

 - 2 years of related experience in application support, technical support, systems support, or a related professional role; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.

 - Experience analyzing business requirements and translating them into technical solutions.

 - Experience troubleshooting technical issues, analyzing, and identifying process gaps and recommending solutions.

 - Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to compare information from multiple data sources and maintain data accuracy.

 - Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to explain technical information, findings, and recommendations to all levels of stakeholders, technical and non-technical audiences.

 - Experience working in a ticketing or service-management environment and managing multiple requests with competing priorities.

 - Experience creating or maintaining operational reports, dashboards, or other support materials.

 - Strong documentation skills, including the ability to turn technical processes into clear, user-friendly guides.

 - Experience using AI platforms such as Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, or Anthology.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Experience working in an Agile environment or supporting defined phases of cross-functional projects.

 - Experience working in or supporting the Educational Technology (EdTech) industry.

 - Familiarity with SaaS application integrations, APIs, or troubleshooting connected systems.

 - Proficiency with Google Workspace for support reporting and data validation.

 - Experience with support platforms or IT service tools such as Jira Service Management or Salesforce.

Our Inside Sales Representatives work with our small and medium-sized businesses and are responsible for expanding our network of service providers.  - Overcoming objections and negotiating solutions while building trust with service providers to understand their needs.

 - Coaching service providers how to effectively build life-long customers with the homeowners who submit service requests.

 - Researching service providers using internal notes, company websites, and other public information.
   
   - Prospecting is done for you! We assign you customers quickly. Leads are provided in our CRM (a proprietary system for Angi).

 - Guiding service providers through the background check authorization and approval process.

 - Meeting and exceeding required sales targets – you will be responsible for the amount of contract value sold biweekly.

 - Bachelor’s degree OR 2+ years of sales experience required

 - High School Diploma or GED required

 - Experience in sales, especially inside sales, is a plus

 - Motivation to exceed sales goals – you are not satisfied by doing the minimum, and you strive to be the best

 - Strong communication skills – building rapport quickly, active listening, and confidence in what you’re saying

 - Desire to contribute to the bottom line and recognize that a team is only as strong as the weakest player – you seek feedback and want to continuously improve

 - Ability to multi-task and work independently while paying attention to detail

 - Strong initiative to strive for continuous accuracy, quality, and timeliness of information

 - Talk on a phone headset for up to 8 hours per day

 - Proven computer aptitude including proficiency with Microsoft Office products

 - Individual Hardline High-speed internet connection

 - Able to provide proof you are at least 21 years of age

 - Veterans encouraged to apply!

Benefits & Compensation:

 - The compensation range for the position ranges from $40,000 - $78,000 per year between base salary and uncapped commission.
   
   - The base pay for the position is $19.23 per hour.
   
   - There is uncapped performance-based commission, with annual on-target base + commission earnings of $78,000 after 6 months of tenure.
   
   - For the first 6 months of tenure, the annual on-target base + commission earnings are $66,000.
   
   - The top 10% of reps in this position earn $160,000+.
   
   - There are ramping performance tiers and other incentives during the new hire training period.

 - Medical coverage with a company contribution to an HSA fund for qualified plans

 - Dental & vision coverage, pet discount plans

 - Retirement plan with company match (401K) through Charles Schwab

 - Generous PTO including sick, personal, vacation, volunteer time and paid holidays

 - Technical equipment (i.e. laptop) provided

 - This is a remote position and we are seeking candidates who permanently reside in the following states: Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, District of Columbia, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, Wisconsin or Wyoming. Lead Mission Integration Engineer, Payload I&T

Spacecraft represent the most pressing unmet need across the entire aerospace industry. As more launch vehicles come online and the cost to orbit decreases, more companies launching payloads to space continue to emerge.

For the first time in history, this influx of payload companies combined with reduced launch costs has resulted in a massive increase in need for commercial spacecraft platforms, known as satellite buses. These buses hold the payloads of our customers and are flown on launch vehicles.

Apex manufactures these satellite buses at scale using a combination of software, vertical integration, and hardware that is designed for manufacturing. Our spacecraft enable the future of society: ranging from earth observation to communications and more.

We’d love for you to join us on our mission of providing humankind access to the galaxy beyond our planet. 




ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Lead Payload Integration & Test Mission Integration Engineer, you will lead the team responsible for planning and executing customer payload integration and SV level test campaigns, turning our foundational spacecraft platform into the backbone of customer missions. You will be responsible for mentoring, tasking, and overall direction of the mission integration engineering team within the payload I&T specialty, serving as the primary technical liaison for complex SV level I&T. In this role, you will balance long term strategic integration planning with short term technical execution with a balance of roughly fifty percent management and fifty percent individual contributor work. We are looking for experienced engineers who are eager to solve complex mission integration challenges with a focus on practicality and scalability, and who thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced aerospace environment.



Responsibilities:

 - Lead, mentor, and develop a team of mission integration engineers within the payload I&T specialty, including hiring, onboarding, performance management, and career growth.

 - Set priorities, assign tasks, and balance workload across concurrent customer campaigns.

 - Serve as the team’s technical backstop: provide final technical review of test plans, procedures, and anomaly dispositions, and act as the escalation point for novel or high-risk integration challenges.

 - Own resource planning for I&T campaigns, including staffing, shift coverage, cleanroom and test facility needs, GSE, and schedule, in coordination with program management and operations.

 - Define and continuously improve standard integration and test processes, procedure templates, and lessons-learned practices so the team scales across programs and customers.

 - Lead and direct the team in planning space vehicle I&T campaigns, and drive execution on the cleanroom floor.

 - Serve as the primary technical liaison for complex SV-level I&T, leading customer technical engagements to develop bus-to-payload integration procedures

 - Own planning and oversee execution of SV-level environmental testing (random vibration, quasi-static load, TVAC) and functional testing, personally leading the highest-complexity or highest-risk test events.

 - Oversee propulsion loading operations for dynamic testing and launch, and ensure team members are trained and qualified for hazardous operations and compliant with safety requirements.

 - Ensure coupled loads analysis (CLA) and thermal analysis results are reviewed, challenged where needed, and incorporated into test planning, working directly with the analysis teams.

 - Support the launch engineering team in deploying to launch sites for launch vehicle integration, system checkouts, and launch rehearsals.

 - Review and approve customer-facing system-level documentation, including specifications, interface control documents, and integration procedures.

 - Own the team’s technical risk posture: identify, assess, and drive mitigation of risks across design, integration, test, and operations, and escalate to leadership as appropriate.

 - Support requirements analysis, verification, and validation to ensure I&T plans align with customer needs.

 - Represent the team in customer meetings, design reviews, and status updates, communicating clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, including senior leadership, and negotiating schedule, scope, and interface changes.



Requirements

 - Bachelor’s degree or higher in Aerospace, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering, or related field.

 - 8+ years of spacecraft or complex flight hardware integration and test experience, including hands-on experience planning and executing SV-level I&T campaigns.

 - 2+ years of formal leadership experience, such as a team lead, supervisor, or senior technical lead directing the work of other engineers, with demonstrated experience mentoring and developing engineers.

 - Proven track record of delivering spacecraft or payload through SV-level environmental testing (random vibration, quasi-static load, TVAC) and functional testing to launch readiness.

 - Strong understanding of space systems integration, test planning, and verification, including interpreting coupled loads and thermal analysis results to derive test levels and margins.

 - Experience leading customer or payload-provider technical engagements, including developing interface documentation and integration procedures, ideally with prime contractors or government entities.

 - Experience managing schedules and cross-functional coordination across multiple concurrent campaigns in a fast-paced environment.

 - Strong communication and organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize and adapt to shifting demands and to present concise technical content to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

 - Willingness to travel to launch sites and work in cleanroom and hazardous-operations environments, including extended or irregular hours during campaigns.

 - U.S. Person status is required, as this position needs access to export-controlled data.



Preferred

 - Experience with propulsion loading operations or other hazardous spacecraft ground operations, including safety and procedure authorship.

 - Experience with CubeSat, small satellite, or rideshare mission integration across multiple spacecraft or vehicle classes.

 - Previous spacecraft, launch vehicle, or payload engineering experience in leadership roles within satellite manufacturing or related aerospace industries.

 - Background in system-level FMEA, anomaly investigation, and reliability engineering methods.

 - Proficiency with Python or MATLAB for test data analysis and automation.

 - Familiarity with flight software, embedded systems, and space communications protocols.

This role reports to me. COMPANY OVERVIEW

Astera Neuro, part of the Astera Institute, is building the tools to decipher and ultimately write the neural codes behind perception, thought, behavior, and internal state. Since these tools don't yet exist, we're assembling a founding team of neuroscientists, computational scientists, and engineers to build them (hardware, software, and methods) and use them to study neural activity at unprecedented scale, with direct relevance to neurological and psychiatric disease. We do high-risk, high-reward science in a well-resourced, collaborative environment with competitive pay, and share our work openly under Astera's Open Science Policy.




POSITION SUMMARY

This role is hands-on and central to the operation of the research program. You will design and run positive-reinforcement training protocols for husbandry and procedural cooperation; implement enrichment and socialization programs designed with the veterinary and behavioral teams; perform daily behavioral and health observations; train animals for voluntary participation in research and veterinary procedures; and maintain the records that keep the program compliant. You will work under the guidance of the Lead Animal Trainer to learn our protocols and colony, with the expectation that you will grow into running training programs independently as your experience develops. The quality of your work directly shapes the welfare of the animals and the reliability of the science.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Design and deliver positive-reinforcement training programs for the NHP population per established SOPs, initially under the direction of the Lead Animal Trainer.

 - Train animals for voluntary cooperation with husbandry, veterinary, and research procedures (e.g., station training, targeting, injection/blood-draw cooperation).

 - Implement environmental enrichment and social-housing programs designed by the veterinary and behavioral teams.

 - Perform daily behavioral and health observations and report clinical, behavioral, or environmental abnormalities to the veterinary team promptly.

 - Track and document training progress, shaping plans, and behavioral milestones to support IACUC, USDA, and AAALAC compliance.

 - Assist veterinary, research, and behavioral teams with animal handling, transport, weighing, and procedural support as needed.

 - Contribute to the development and refinement of training SOPs, behavioral records, and enrichment practices as the program grows.


WHO YOU ARE

Bedrock Robotics, Inc. seeks a Hardware Engineer in San Francisco, CA responsible for designing, manufacturing, and testing its autonomous hardware systems, including high performance computer systems, sensors, controllers, interfaces to machines, and testing equipment.

This position will work with autonomous hardware systems installed on standard heavy construction machinery—excavators, bulldozers, and wheel loaders—to allow that equipment to perform earthmoving work on construction sites autonomously. In this context, “autonomous hardware systems” are the physical electronic components installed on a construction machine that allow it to operate without a human operator in the cab. They consist of: high-performance computer systems (ruggedized onboard computers mounted on the machine that perform the calculations required for autonomous operation); sensors (devices that allow the machine to perceive its surroundings, including cameras, radar, lidar, and GNSS); controllers and interfaces (electronic units that translate the computer's decisions into electrical signals that operate the machine's existing hydraulic, steering, and engine controls); and testing equipment (benches, fixtures, and instrumentation used to verify each of the above components before and after installation on a machine). Working together, these systems continuously collect sensor data, determine the machine's position and what is around it, calculate the path the machine should follow and the movements it should make, and then command the machine's controls to carry out those movements, performing the tasks a human operator would otherwise perform manually.

Specific duties include: (i) defining and designing hardware systems, including component-level architecture for autonomous machines and camera/optics design and performance; (ii) establishing and leading relationships and programs with external vendors to facilitate hardware manufacturing and delivery; (iii) supporting hardware system verification and validation, including working with safety teams to establish/tune requirements and performance metrics for components and systems; (iv) using industry standard tools and knowledge to test standards of hardware systems; and (v) writing reusable, high quality sensor data analysis and testing automation software.

This is a hybrid office-based/work-from-home position within the United States. The employee can work remotely from within the United States but must be able to work in the San Francisco office at least three (3) days per week.

Must have a bachelor’s degree (or foreign equivalent) in Electrical Engineering, Robotics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a directly related field plus five (5) years of progressively responsible, post-baccalaureate experience in designing, integrating, and validating electrical hardware systems.

Must have any experience with: (i) high performance computer systems, including x86 or ARM; (ii) robotics sensors stacks, including lidar, radar, camera, or GNSS; (iii) communication protocols and technologies, including CAN, LIN, J1939, FlexRay, or Ethernet; (iv) python or C++/C/Rust; and (v) standardization tools and organizations, including ISO, SAE, and ANSI.

Must be willing and able to travel regionally/nationally up to 15%, to visit hardware testing sites.

Experience can be concurrent.

About the role:

We're hiring an experienced software engineer to oversee security at Chalk. This is an opportunity to join us in-person as our first security engineer and make a large impact at a high growth start-up.

Senior Software Engineer - Data Warehousing & Transformation Ecosystem

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Connectors team is the bridge between ClickHouse and the broader data ecosystem. We build and maintain the integrations that make ClickHouse accessible to millions of developers, data practitioners and AI agents worldwide: data visualization plugins (Tableau, Power BI, Superset, Metabase), connectors for data frameworks (Apache Spark, Flink, Kafka Connect, Beam, Fivetran), transformation and orchestration tooling (dbt, Airflow, Dagster), and AI tooling.

Our work directly shapes how companies process massive datasets: real-time analytics platforms ingesting millions of events per second, observability systems monitoring global infrastructure, and the data warehouses and AI-powered applications redefining how teams work with data. We collaborate closely with the open-source community, internal teams, and enterprise users to ensure ClickHouse integrations set the standard for performance, reliability, and developer experience.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Software Engineer focused on the data warehousing ecosystem, you will own how ClickHouse plugs into the modern analytics-engineering toolchain. This role sits at the intersection of high-performance database engineering, developer experience, and production operations. You will build the integrations that let data teams use ClickHouse as the warehouse behind the tools they already run, and you will own how those integrations are deployed and operated at scale.

You will drive architecture, performance, and feature direction across four areas:

 - Transformation: dbt, across both the Python-based v1 adapter and the Rust-based v2 (Fusion) engine; SQLMesh

 - Semantic layer: dbt Semantic Layer / MetricFlow, Cube, Apache Ossie (formerly Open Semantic Interchange)

 - Schema and metadata management: schema evolution, model contracts, migration tooling, catalog integration

 - Orchestration: Apache Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, Temporal, and how transformation jobs run inside them (Astronomer Cosmos, dagster-dbt)

We are looking for someone who has run the transformation layer of a real data warehouse, not just written models in it. You have operated dbt and its orchestration for many teams: CI/CD, environments, scheduling, credentials, observability, and cost. You know what breaks at scale because you were the one paged for it. You know what it takes to maintain code that other teams’ pipelines depend on – ideally because you’ve contributed to the open-source data warehousing ecosystem yourself (dbt and its adapters, orchestration providers, semantic-layer tooling or similar). You bring that practitioner's insight into what we should build and why, and you turn it into robust, production-ready integrations and the deployment artifacts (container images, Helm charts, reference architectures) that make ClickHouse the natural choice when data teams design their next warehouse.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own and evolve dbt-clickhouse and related transformation adapters to enterprise-grade quality: correctness, performance, and reliability across dbt versions and engines

 - Design and build ClickHouse integrations for semantic-layer tooling (MetricFlow, Cube, Apache Ossie), making ClickHouse a first-class target for governed metrics consumed by BI tools and AI agents

 - Build and maintain orchestration integrations (Airflow provider, Dagster, Prefect) and the patterns for running transformation jobs inside them

 - Define how schema evolution, model contracts, and migrations work across the toolchain when ClickHouse is the warehouse

 - Own the production deployment and operations story for these integrations: container images, Helm charts, reference architectures, and runbooks for running transformation and orchestration workloads on Kubernetes against ClickHouse

 - Build and operate the Kubernetes-based CI, integration-test, and benchmark infrastructure

 - Engage actively with the open-source community: triage issues, support contributors, advocate for users, and shape the roadmap from real-world feedback

 - Collaborate with Product, Cloud, and core database teams to align integration work with broader priorities

 - Bring a practitioner's perspective to roadmap decisions, grounding prioritization in how data and analytics engineers actually operate a warehouse


ABOUT YOU

 - 7+ years of software development experience, including hands-on time as a Data Engineer, Analytics Engineer, or Data Platform Engineer

 - Deep dbt experience from both sides: you have run large dbt projects in production, and you understand how an adapter plugs into dbt-core

 - You have built or operated an internal data platform that served multiple teams: CI/CD for transformation projects, orchestration, environment promotion, secrets and credentials, observability, and cost attribution

 - You have run dbt and an orchestrator (Airflow, Dagster or Temporal) in production on Kubernetes, and you’ve owned the deployment and reliability of both — not just the models.

 - Strong database fundamentals: SQL, data modeling, query optimization, and familiarity with OLAP or columnar databases

 - Outstanding written and verbal communication; comfortable collaborating across engineering functions and with open-source communities


BONUS POINTS
