At ClickUp, we're building the future of work: the first truly converged AI workspace unifying tasks, docs, chat, calendar, and enterprise search, all supercharged by context-driven AI. We are an AI-native company. Every team member is expected to leverage AI daily, and we evaluate AI fluency as part of our hiring process. Join us and help redefine what's possible. 🚀



Everything we build now runs through one question: how do we supercharge productivity with AI? 

ClickUp Brain and our agentic AI capabilities are the center of gravity for the company. We're not bolting AI onto a project management tool, we're building the platform where AI does real work: drafting, summarizing, routing, researching, and executing alongside the humans who use it. That focus is external and internal. We expect our customers to get radically more productive with AI, and we expect the same of ourselves. Every ClickUp employee is given the tools, the training, and the mandate to use AI in their daily workflow.

 

This is an AI-native role. You will use AI every day to research faster, personalize at scale, prep calls, and keep your pipeline clean. You will also be selling AI, so you need to speak about it credibly.

 


THE ROLE

As a Market Development Representative (MDR), you'll serve as the critical bridge between our marketing efforts and the sales team, playing a pivotal role in accelerating our revenue pipeline. You will be responsible for meticulously following up on, nurturing, and qualifying all inbound leads generated from our diverse marketing channels. This role is fundamental to ensuring our sales team engages only with the most promising and well-prepared prospects.

 

In this position, you'll act as the first point of contact and a trusted educator for potential customers. Your mission is to understand their initial interest, assess their business needs, and articulate the value of our platform, including how our AI capabilities change what their team is capable of. You will manage the crucial early stages of the buyer's journey, building rapport and filtering for high-potential opportunities before seamlessly transitioning them to an Account Executive.

 

This is a high-velocity motion: sub-30 day cycles, pipeline generation at scale, and relentless execution. MDRs don't win by out-strategizing over weeks. They win by out-hustling, out-qualifying, and out-persisting, turning every inbound signal into a qualified opportunity that sticks downstream.

 


HOW WE HIRE, COACH AND MEASURE: THE FOUR PILLARS

Every MDR is developed and evaluated against four behavioral pillars. They're not corporate values on a wall, they're the operating system of the team.

 

🔥 Ownership. The non-negotiable foundation. Extreme ownership of pipeline outcomes and no excuses when a lead goes cold because you didn't respond fast enough or log your work properly. Intellectual honesty: truth over ego. Going above and beyond for the team's collective success, not just your own number.

 

⭐️ Obsession. The refusal to plateau. This is a high-rejection motion, so you study objection patterns, perfect talk tracks, and learn from every no. You compound knowledge: every call makes the next one better because you document what works and share it.

 

⚡️ Effectiveness. Winning by design, not effort alone. Converting high volume into high quality through sharp qualification, deep discovery, and meetings that actually stick. Every touch is chosen for maximum conversion impact.

 

🤖 AI Native. Using AI to amplify your own output, and positioning ClickUp's AI credibly to prospects. The bar: you're leveraging AI across research, outreach, follow-up, and CRM hygiene, and you can articulate our agentic AI value proposition in every qualification conversation.

 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Respond promptly (Zoom, phone, email) to all inbound leads generated by marketing activities: handraisers, account signals, content, webinars, social campaigns, and events.

 - Qualify marketing-qualified leads (MQLs) using a consistent framework to determine sales readiness and fit, and distinguish buyers from browsers.

 - Nurture leads through in-depth conversations, acting as an educator and advisor rather than focusing solely on immediate conversions.

 - Uncover real business pain beneath surface-level inquiries, quantify its impact, and document it clearly for the AE.

 - Position ClickUp's platform and agentic AI capabilities credibly and specifically, mapping them to the prospect's actual workflow gaps.

 - Use AI tools across your entire workflow: account and persona research, personalization at scale, call prep, follow-up drafting, and CRM hygiene. Edit every output for authenticity, never ship raw.

 - Maintain accurate, real-time records of lead interactions and qualification status in CRM.

 - Deliver comprehensive AE handoffs with a qualification summary, roles identified, pain documented, and competitive context.

 - Provide detailed feedback to sales and marketing on lead quality, content effectiveness, and channel performance, helping refine messaging and targeting.

 - Occasionally perform cold outreach as needed, with a primary focus on inbound.

 - Share what works: talk tracks, AI workflows, and objection patterns. Individual wins are good, team adoption is better.

 


QUALIFICATIONS

This role is built for a highly motivated and tenacious individual who is eager to succeed and thrives on hard work. The most important qualifications are your personal drive and resilience, as you'll be connecting with a high volume of customers daily.

 - What's non-negotiable: a strong work ethic, the grit to overcome challenges, and the tenacity to consistently engage with customers.

 - Also non-negotiable: genuine curiosity about AI and a willingness to rebuild how you work around it. You don't need to be an expert. You need to be someone who reaches for AI first and figures it out.

 - 1-2 years of relevant experience in outbound sales and/or a demonstrated passion for sales as a primary career focus.

 - Strong communication and interpersonal skills, and the ability to quickly build rapport and trust.

 - Analytical mindset with real attention to detail.

 - Familiarity with CRM and marketing automation tools.

 - Collaborative team player with a proactive approach to problem-solving. AI adoption spreads through people who are approachable and generous with what they learn.


SUCCESS METRICS

 - Speed and quality of lead follow-up against SLA.

 - Conversion rate of MQLs to sales-qualified opportunities.

 - CRM data integrity and process adherence.

 - Quality and usefulness of feedback provided to marketing and sales.

 - Contribution to pipeline and revenue growth from marketing-generated leads.

 

The throughline for this role: speed, resilience, and conversion quality. You win by out-hustling, out-persisting, and out-qualifying every single day, and by using AI to make every one of those things easier than it was yesterday.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Data Integrations team owns the systems that move clinical and financial data between Commure and hundreds of external healthcare systems using FHIR, HL7, Flat files, RPA etc. The domain is EMRs and Portals like Availity, but the engineering problem is distributed systems at scale: durable orchestration on Temporal, strong delivery semantics against unreliable third parties, and a data and networking substrate that has to keep up as the business grows.

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to own multi-component projects on this platform end to end and help us scale as we move towards more enterprise customers.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own multi-component projects where requirements are incomplete or evolving: define the approach, sequence the work, and see them through design, implementation, migration, rollout, and running them in production.

 - Design and build robust systems across the orchestration layer, the pipelines, and the data stores, with strong boundaries and observability built in..

 - Set the bar for observability and operational readiness (monitoring, logging, distributed tracing, dashboards, alerting, SLOs, and safe production rollouts).

 - Work hand-in-hand with platform and product teams to keep sensitive customer data protected, tighten security boundaries, and stay on top of our regulatory and compliance obligations.

 - Make pragmatic calls that weigh security, correctness, reliability, performance, and simplicity against how fast we need to ship.

 - Mentor other junior and senior engineers on the team, lead team-level and cross-org design reviews, and help improve hiring and team processes.

 - Take real ownership in a fast-moving environment. Fix root causes instead of patching around them.




OUR TECH STACK

 - Backend: Python (FastAPI) monolith on Kubernetes; supporting services in Go (e.g. HL7/MLLP gateways)

 - Database: PostgreSQL (SQLAlchemy) · Redis

 - Cloud & orchestration: GCP (Cloud Tasks, Pub/Sub, GCS, Cloud Run / Knative), Temporal

 - Integrations: HL7 v2, FHIR R4, REST/OAuth (SMART), Selenium, SFTP

 - Monitoring: Prometheus + Grafana

 - Other tools: Linear, Notion, Slack




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent extensive experience.

 - 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, including leading multi-component projects with ambiguous requirements from design through production.

 - Deep experience building and operating distributed systems at scale, high-throughput pipelines, data-intensive services. You can talk about the non-obvious failure modes, not just the happy path.

 - Strong data-layer and concurrency judgment. You've made a relational database (Postgres or similar) do more than it wanted to, and you know when to reach for a DB lock, when Redis is the right tool, and when the right move is a design that doesn't need either.

 - Real depth in the boring-but-critical layers. Networking and egress (NAT, static IPs, connection lifecycle, DNS, TLS), the database, the container runtime. You're comfortable debugging when something below the application layer misbehaves.

 - Production experience with GCP and container orchestration (Kubernetes, Knative, or similar serverless-on-k8s), and fluency in a modern backend language (Python strongly preferred; Go or similar is a plus).

 - The ability to explain technical tradeoffs in language non-engineers can act on, and to coordinate dependencies across teams.

 - A history of leveling up the engineers around you.




BONUS

 - Healthcare integrations experience — HL7 v2, FHIR, and EHRs like Epic, Cerner, or Athenahealth. We can teach the domain; we're hiring for the systems judgment above.

 - Experience with the compliance envelope this work lives inside (HIPAA, SOC 2) and the security posture that comes with handling PHI.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Commure is hiring AR Specialists to handle end-to-end claim follow-up for our US healthcare provider clients. You will review unpaid claims, call payers to retrieve claim processing decisions, file appeals, post remittances, and complete every other activity needed to take a claim to payment or final resolution.


The job is to turn aging receivables into cash before claims hit timely-filing limits or get written off. It suits someone who is comfortable on the phone with US insurance representatives, asks good probing questions, and documents their work carefully.




WHAT YOU'LL DO



CLAIM FOLLOW-UP

 - Work assigned accounts from aging reports and work queues, prioritizing by age, balance, and filing deadline.

 - Review each unpaid claim before contacting the payer: claim history, prior notes, authorization, medical documentation, and the EOB or ERA.

 - Call payers, or use IVR and payer portals, to retrieve claim processing decisions: whether the claim is on file, in process, paid, denied, or pending, and why.

 - Get a clear next step on every contact (payment date, reference number, reason for non-payment).

 - Follow up on time so that claims are resolved before timely-filing and appeal deadlines pass.

 - Take the action each claim needs to reach resolution: send missing information or medical records, request reprocessing, correct and resubmit, appeal, or escalate.


DENIALS, UNDERPAYMENTS, AND APPEALS

 - Identify the denial or underpayment reason and decide the correct fix.

 - Correct and resubmit claims, including working billing scrubber edits and rejections.

 - File appeals and reconsiderations with the supporting documentation, and track each one to a decision.

 - Handle contractual adjustments and write-offs according to client policy and approval limits.

 - Escalate complex or stuck claims to the team lead, coding, billing, or the client as needed.


REMITTANCE POSTING

 - Post payer remittances from ERAs and EOBs to the correct claims and line items: payments, contractual adjustments, and denials.

 - Reconcile posted amounts against the remittance and fix unapplied or misapplied payments.

 - After posting, move any remaining balance to the next step: secondary payer billing, patient responsibility, or further follow-up.


DOCUMENTATION AND ANALYSIS

 - Record clear, complete call notes and actions taken in our practice management system, using the correct status and action codes, so there is an audit trail for the next person.

 - Spot patterns in denials and underpayments (by payer, provider, or code) and flag them to your lead so root causes can be fixed upstream.

 - Contribute to reporting on days in AR, top denial reasons, and resolution outcomes.


QUALITY AND COMPLIANCE

 - Meet daily productivity targets and quality standards.

 - Follow HIPAA requirements, client SOPs, and payer guidelines at all times when handling patient and claim information.




WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR




 - 2+ years of hands-on experience in AR follow-up and denial management for US healthcare clients.

 - Working knowledge of the US revenue cycle and insurance landscape: Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial payers.

 - Experience with a specific area: physician billing, Ambulatory Surgical Centers, or orthopaedic surgery.

 - Good understanding of denials: common reason codes, what causes them, and how to resolve them.

 - Ability to read and interpret an EOB and ERA.

 - Fluent spoken English and confident phone manner, with strong probing and listening skills.

 - Clear written English for call notes and appeals.

 - Basic proficiency with computers and MS Office, especially Excel.

 - Graduate in any discipline.

 - Willingness to work night shifts on an ongoing basis.

You will bring the agency’s requirements to Quality and help translate them into submittals that get approved. This is a full-time, individual contributor position.

 - Licensing Path and Predictability: Maintain approval date forecasts for each assigned state and program, flag schedule risk to Project Management before it reaches a ship date, and help maintain the 12-month licensing roadmap.

 - Market Access Support: Help assess new states ahead of contract and first shipment, including how each building structure (modular building, equipment enclosure, skid) is classified and which licensing path it triggers.

The Developer Platform team owns how Decagon builds and ships software: from the time an engineer/coding agent starts with an idea/spec/problem to the time the we have a released product in our customer’s hands. ABOUT THE ROLE

Every improvement you make for engineers also helps agents, and you'll design with both kinds of users in mind.

 - Developer productivity observability and evals: instrument the whole development lifecycle for both human and agent work, and use that to guide project selection and agent evals

OPERATING PRINCIPLES

Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:

 1. Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.

 2. Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.

 3. Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.

 4. Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.




AI-FIRST BY DEFAULT

We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.

That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:

 - Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.

 - Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.

 - Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.

 - Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.

The Director of Fraud Risk Management is a key member of the Flex Risk Management Leadership Team (reports to the Chief Risk Officer) who will have the opportunity to take the Fraud Risk Management function at Flex to a level that rivals the best in class.

Core Responsibilities

Own end-to-end fraud risk management for Flex's credit card and DDA product portfolio across consumer and small business segments; end-to-end meaning full lifecycle coverage, from pre-acquisition through post-disbursement:

 - Acquisition & onboarding fraud: analyze application fraud patterns by channel and source; assess identity signal quality, document authenticity rates, and synthetic identity indicators at the population level; monitor approval flow for anomalous approval rate shifts that may signal policy exploitation

 - Identity & entity verification performance: maintain analytical visibility into match rates, challenge rates, and step-up conversion across KYC and KYB verification layers in partnership with compliance; identify where the verification stack may be generating friction for good applicants or gaps for bad ones — and surface those findings as inputs to joint policy discussions

 - First-party fraud: monitor behavioral signals associated with intentional default — spend acceleration, balance build without payment intent, cash advance abuse, and bust-out patterns; distinguish first-party risk from credit deterioration analytically

 - Third-party fraud: track unauthorized transaction patterns, account takeover indicators, card-not-present abuse, and compromised credential signals; maintain segment-level views of dispute and chargeback rates by fraud type

 - Synthetic identity fraud: build and maintain detection frameworks for synthetic identities — thin-file manipulation, credit piggybacking, fabricated entity structures — with particular attention to SMB applicants where bureau data is sparse and entity verification is harder

 - DDA-specific fraud vectors: monitor ACH manipulation, payee substitution, unauthorized external transfer attempts, and check fraud patterns within the DDA product; maintain visibility into funds flow anomalies that may indicate account misuse or laundering behavior

 - Authorization & transaction monitoring: analyze real-time and near-real-time authorization patterns for velocity anomalies, geographic inconsistencies, merchant category abuse, and card testing signals

 - Dispute, chargeback & recovery: own the analytical view of dispute resolution patterns; identify chargeback abuse and friendly fraud at the segment and merchant level; track recovery rates by fraud type and loss emergence timing

Build and maintain fraud detection frameworks that surface emerging attack patterns before they scale — distinguishing signal from noise across high-volume transaction and behavioral data

 

Synthesize data across sources — device, IP, identity, bureau, transaction, and behavioral — to construct a layered fraud risk view; capable of identifying coordinated fraud rings and correlated anomalies that don't surface in single-signal models

 

Lead periodic fraud risk reviews: design the analytical narrative, own the underlying loss and dispute data, and present findings with clear exposure implications to risk committees and senior leadership

 

Develop fraud segmentation — by fraud type, acquisition channel, product, obligor type, and attack vector — to enable more precise detection tuning, policy intervention, and loss reserve calibration

 

Partner cross-functionally with credit, legal & compliance, financial crimes, operations, and product to ensure fraud risk visibility is embedded in product design and upstream decisioning, not bolted on reactively

 

Contribute to scenario analysis and stress testing for fraud loss: model exposure under elevated attack conditions and translate into concrete loss and operational cost estimates

 

Serve as the internal SME on fraud analytics — establishing detection standards, taxonomy, and measurement frameworks as the product portfolio scales

Qualifications

 - 

 - 

 - This role sits in the foundational build path of core risk management disciplines, and we expect significant upward potential for the right candidate.  - We're seeking an ambitious problem solver with a record of achievement on an exponential trajectory.

What You'll Do

 - 

 - Build and own the city’s dream list of 50 owners, prioritizing five North Star accounts and identifying the best path to each.

 - Curate rooms built around the people on your list: Plan and host events that bring the right people together, including intimate dinners, customer gatherings, and strategic brand activations.

 - Develop relationships with prospective customers and guide them from initial conversations through account opening, staying involved as their businesses grow with Flex.

 - Evaluate and negotiate sponsorships and memberships, and only say yes to the ones that put you in front of people on the list.

 - Develop a monthly market plan covering your priority accounts, upcoming initiatives, and progress toward customer acquisition.

 - Collaborate with internal teams to move opportunities forward, generate customer referrals, and share insights from your market.

 - Maintain an organized pipeline, track applications and referrals, coordinate events, and manage your local budget.

What Success Looks Like

 - First 90 days: Your 50 are written, your five are picked, your first rooms have happened and you’re in real conversations with your North Star accounts.
   
   First year: Your North Star accounts are on Flex, the customers you brought in are active and spending, and people around the city are sending you introductions without being asked.

 -

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to own the rails that move money into, out of and across Float: financial ledgering, financial accounts, payment rails (EFT, wires, ACH, cross-border and FX) and card infrastructure. You'll think about the whole life of a payment — how it starts, how its status is communicated, what happens when it fails or is returned, and how customers and our teams resolve exceptions. You'll work with a designer, eight engineers and a product operations specialist focused on analytics and go-to-market planning.

 - Make payment health measurable and keep improving it — success rate, processing speed, failure recovery and reconciliation.

 - Manage dependencies with banks, networks and processors that move on their own timelines. Escalate risks early, with options attached.

 - Partner closely with Engineering on APIs, data models, ledger interactions, controls and observability.

 - Make trade-off calls across customer experience, speed, reliability, risk, compliance, operational complexity and commercial impact.

 - Coordinate across our card, payments and banking products so infrastructure work supports the whole business.

 - Learn how finance leaders run payroll funding, tax remittance and multi-currency treasury, and work with Design to build accounts, treasury and FX into those workflows.

 - Work with Risk, Compliance, Operations, Finance and GTM from the start, not as approval steps at the end.

 - Keep leadership and partner teams clearly informed across many projects at once.

 - Use AI tools to speed up discovery, analysis, documentation and decision-making.

ABOUT GENESIS

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.




THE ROLE

Eno is going to work with its first customers, starting in industrial environments: manufacturing, logistics and laboratories. Our glove matches our robot hand one to one, so when a customer's team wears it while doing their regular work, that work becomes the data the robot learns from. Someone has to make that happen at the customer's site, and someone has to be next to the robot when it arrives. That is this role.

You will help customers collect data at their sites, teleoperate the robot on our floor and at the customer's, and help our deployment team bring Eno into the customer's workflow. You are the face of Genesis on the customer's floor.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Help customers collect at their sites. Set the customer's team up with our gloves and cameras, train them, and stay with them while they do their regular work, so the data clears our quality bar. Collect the task yourself when that is the faster way to get it right.

 - Teleoperate, on our floor or at the customer's. Operate Eno through the customer's tasks to collect data in the real environment and cover the cases the model has not seen yet.

 - Help integrate the robot. Work with our Deployment Solution Engineers on station set-up, fixtures, calibration, bring-up and shutdown, and run the checks that show a station is ready.

 - Run evaluations and acceptance runs. Take the robot through the agreed tasks, score each run, and log what happened so the team knows what works and what does not.

 - Be the first line when something stops. Do the basic troubleshooting, then send engineering a clear report with logs and video.

 - Work safely in someone else's building. Follow the customer's site rules, protective equipment and safety procedures, and ours.

Role highlights:

 

 - Senior Product Designer, Missions and Data

 - Location: Espoo, Finland 

 - Department:  Product Management

 - Reports to: Director of Product Design

 - Employment type: Permanent

WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS:

Our satellites can see through clouds. Our software should make things just as clear.

ICEYE operates the world's largest SAR satellite constellation. Our radar satellites can see any location on Earth, day or night, through cloud, smoke and darkness. That's the frontier part. Next up: giving the operators, mission planners and analysts who use them a software experience to match. We're hiring four product designers to make it happen.

The people using our software are experts, and they're short on time. Plans change late, imagery lands fast, and there's no room for a confusing screen.

Here's the tricky bit. These tools are dense for a reason: maps, timelines, big tables, imagery, live status. Strip that away and you lose the trust that comes from seeing the full picture. So the job is making complex software feel obvious, without making it feel thin. If that sentence made you want to start sketching, keep reading.

We won't pretend it's simple. Our products are powerful and complex, and shaping them around how users think means reworking what's there as much as building what's new. (We think that's the interesting part.)

 


WHO WE ARE


ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

 

ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.

 

ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.

 

Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.



YOUR DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES 

 

You'll own big parts of the product end to end, side by side with product and engineering. In practice, that looks like:

 - Designing the core workflows for fleet operations, tasking, and imagery and intelligence, from how operators run a constellation to how analysts turn radar data into decisions.

 - Staying close to users. Real time with operators, planners and analysts, and keeping them in the loop from first sketch to release, not just at kickoff.

 - Making dense feel calm. Maps, timelines, giant tables, live status: you make them readable at a glance, down to the last empty state and edge case.

 - Having a say in what we build, not just how it looks, together with your product and engineering partners.

 - Building things with AI. Tools, agents and workflows that generate, audit or migrate UI, so the whole team moves faster.

 - Making the team better through critique, hiring and shaping how we work as the team grows.

Six months from now, we'd love to see a core workflow you redesigned and shipped, with proof it helped (faster decisions, fewer errors, people actually using it), and at least one AI-powered tool the team now relies on.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Titles and years matter less to us than talent and judgment. The scope here is senior to lead. Took the scenic route to get here? Great. If the work holds up, apply.

Must haves:

 - Craft that stops people mid-scroll. Typography, spacing, hierarchy, motion, and every last state and edge case. In dense software, craft is what makes complexity readable.

 - Comfort in complex systems. You've designed data-dense, workflow-heavy tools: dashboards, maps, big tables, operational or enterprise software, multi-product platforms. The messier, the better.

 - You build with AI, not just chat with it. You've made skills, agents or workflows that generate, audit or migrate UI. Show us.

 - Customers in the room. Users shape your work throughout, not just at kickoff and a final test. You can tell us about the conversation that changed your mind.

 - Commercial impact, with receipts. You connect your work to business metrics and can show the evidence: delivery speed, defects avoided, engineering time saved, adoption. "The team loved it" is lovely, but it isn't proof. And you can tell us what changed for your customers because of it.

 - Speed without shortcuts. You've shipped at fast-moving, high-bar companies without letting quality slip, and you're comfortable making the call before every answer is in.

 - A real reason to be here. You can tell us, in your own words, why European defense capability matters to you. "Satellites are cool" is true, but it isn't a reason.



Nice to haves:

genuinely optional; we'll teach you the domain

 - Geospatial or mapping interfaces

 - Defense or government software

 - Front-end code

 - Hiring Manager Interview

 - Portfolio Review

 - Take home task + presentation

 - Final interview with CPO

ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.

WHAT YOU WILL BUILD:

 - Domain Services. Backend services handling task management and sensor planning. Event-driven workers that perform opportunity calculation and synchronise state asynchronously via NATS JetStream. PostgreSQL for persistence. Responsiveness and resilience at the service of the mission.

 - Customer-facing APIs. Stable, performant interfaces that can evolve but must not break users in doing so. The observability stack and troubleshooting capabilities needed to support our customers in production.

 - Geospatial Databases. Performant indexes able to resolve geospatial queries against large datasets and ingest new data often.

 - Tasking and Planning Engines. Orbit propagation, pass prediction, acquisition geometry, sensor configuration parameters, and coverage footprint computation. Applied science mathematics turned into operational capability via Software.

 - Whatever the future brings. Cross-sensor coordination, satellite autonomy, new collection strategies, and capabilities that will emerge from continuous learning and close collaboration with customers





WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Must haves:

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals. You design evolvable, resilient, performant systems. You can reason about concurrency and how transactions work. You are able to choose technologies and design data models that optimise for their data ingestion and access patterns. You understand the difference between “At most once”, “At least once” and how to design systems around those guarantees.

 - Production experience. You have designed, built, and operated services in production that served real customers and had real economic consequences attached to their availability. You know how to make your systems resilient and observable.

 - API design experience. You know how to design APIs that enable users, encapsulate unnecessary complexity, and expose opportunity. APIs that remain evolvable but don’t break users who don’t want to adopt the new features.

You can listen carefully, ask precise questions, and articulate technical trade-offs in terms that everybody can understand, and adjust to your audience accordingly.

 - Department:   Product Engineering, Solutions

 - Employment type:  Permanent

Why this role matters:

 

As a Senior Platform Engineer, you’ll work on the shared platform that sits behind ICEYE's natural catastrophe analysis products.

ICEYE's Product Engineering teams turn data from our own SAR satellite constellation into analysis of natural catastrophes such as floods, wildfires and storms. Insurers and other customers receive this analysis through products like the ICEYE Solutions Suite (ISS).

Every one of these products runs on a shared platform: the Kubernetes clusters, cloud infrastructure, GitOps pipelines and tooling that product and data science teams use to ship and run their services.

The demands on that platform are growing. Our products are moving from a delivery platform to a customer insights platform, where customers upload their own datasets and receive near real-time, drill-down results at global scale. This requires us to:

 - Run workloads across several cloud regions to meet data residency requirements;

 - Enforce tenant isolation and auditability at the infrastructure layer;

 - Give a growing number of teams a golden path, so they can deploy safely without a platform engineer in the loop.

We are a small, product-minded platform team inside the Product Engineering department. You will join while these foundations are being built, and you will have a direct say in how they take shape.

 - Abstract our AWS and Kubernetes infrastructure behind a small set of core services and interfaces, so product teams interact with a few well-designed building blocks instead of raw cloud resources.

 - Design and build the golden path: low-config, convention-over-configuration ways to create a new service and take it to production in hours, with security, compliance and observability included by default.

 - Build and maintain the reusable components behind it: including Helm charts, Terraform modules and shared CI workflows

 - Make observability a default: with metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, SLOs and alerting available out of the box

 - Embed security and compliance into the platform layer.

 - Mentor teammates and engineers in product teams.

 - Work closely with product, security and other engineering teams.

 

What we’re looking for

Must haves:

 

 - Proven experience building and operating AWS cloud infrastructure for customer-facing production system

 - Deep hands-on experience with Kubernetes in production, including cluster operations, networking, autoscaling, and a service mesh or similar.

 - Strong infrastructure-as-code and GitOps skills; you have run Terraform and a GitOps controller (FluxCD or Argo CD) at team or organisation scale, not just for a single service.

 - Experience designing tenant isolation, access control, and auditability into shared infrastructure.

 - Experience with observability and reliability practices: SLOs, alerting, incident response, and capacity and cost management.

 - Clear communication: you can explain technical trade-offs to engineers, product colleagues and auditors alike, and you document your work.

 - A product mindset toward internal platforms: you treat other engineers as your users and measure success by how easily they ship.

 

Nice to haves:

 - Experience with Istio or another service mesh, Karpenter, or Argo Workflows.

 - Hands-on use of AI coding assistants and agents in your daily work, with sound judgment about where they help.

 - Experience supporting data science or ML workloads (GPU scheduling, batch pipelines, notebook environments).

 - Familiarity with geospatial data pipelines or large raster/vector workloads.

 - Experience working within ISO 27001, SOC 2, or DORA-governed environments.

 - Strong attention to detail and comfort with large data sets in Excel or similar tools.

 - Clear written and verbal communication with suppliers and internal stakeholders.

 - Problem solving and root cause analysis

 - Service orientation and stakeholder management

 - Process discipline with an eye for automation

 - Ability to prioritize across a steady queue of requests

Founded in 2013, Ignition is the leading revenue and billing automation platform for firms and agencies. We automate proposals, invoicing, payments and workflows in a single AI-powered platform, empowering businesses to sell, bill and get paid faster.

Ignition automates proposals, engagement letters, invoicing, payments and workflows in a single AI-powered platform, empowering 8,500+ businesses to sell, bill and get paid for their services with ease. 

To date, Ignition customers have managed relationships with over 2.4 million clients and earned $13b in revenue via the platform. Ignition's global workforce spans Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the Philippines, US and the UK.




COMPANY VALUES:

 - We are better everyday

 - We work without ego

 - We are smarter together

 - We hero our customer


ABOUT THE ROLE

Ignition helps accounting firms price confidently, bill everything and get paid faster. Ignition runs the revenue side of 8,500+ accounting firms. We’re looking for the person who builds the digital engine that finds the next 10,000, in every region we sell. You will own the pipeline Ignition generates through digital channels, in every region we sell. You'll lead performance marketing (SEO, AEO (answer engine optimization), paid search, paid social), lifecycle and nurture, and the website, co-owning pipeline and revenue with our sales leaders in every region.

This is a hands-on, test-and-learn leadership role where AI is at the core of how marketing gets done: enabling you to run the work, build reporting, and quickly spot and fix issues. This role goes beyond channels and you’ll help shape how marketing and sales work together, along with working closely with RevOps, Product Marketing and regional marketing teams across AMER, APAC and the UK.




WHERE AND HOW WE WORK

We're a global team across Canada, the US, Australia and the UK. We work asynchronously where we can and offer flexible hours to make cross-time-zone collaboration work.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

Own and grow the global digital pipeline:

 - Co-own the digital pipeline and revenue targets for AMER, APAC and UK, with AMER as the largest market.

 - Set the global channel strategy and adapt it by region and segment, from SMB to mid-market and enterprise firms.

 - Grow self-serve trials and signups alongside sales-led pipeline initiatives

 - Manage and optimize the paid media budget across search, social and other CPC channels, quickly reallocating spend to the best-performing campaigns.

 - Partner with regional marketing and product marketing in every region so digital programs amplify launches, campaigns and events.

Co-own pipeline and revenue with Sales:

 - Build a true partnership with regional sales leaders; sharing digital funnel ownership and revenue accountability for joint success.

 - Shape how marketing and sales work together: lead definitions, routing, prioritization, follow-up and feedback loops, with RevOps.

 - Influence sales process and campaign builds so marketing demand converts to revenue.

 - Use sales and customer insight to decide where to invest and what to test next

Lead performance, lifecycle and the website:

 - Lead organic search, AEO, paid search and paid social via both in-house and through agencies.

 - Own lifecycle and nurture programs, moving leads to qualified pipeline and reengaging stalled or lost opportunities.

 - Own the website as our primary conversion asset. Use insights from sales calls, live chat and customer conversations to sharpen messaging, improve visibility in AI-driven search results, and deliver a consistent roadmap.

 - Launch an automated and consistent online review program on G2 and Capterra to drive positive online sentiment

Run marketing with AI:

 - Use AI and agents to do real work: content and ad variants, campaign builds, analysis, scenario planning and reporting.

 - Help the team adopt AI in their own workflows, so the team can experiment and ship faster.

 - Build reporting that lets you see quickly where the funnel is off track, by region, channel and segment, and act on it.

Lead, Build, and Mentor a High-Performing Team:

 - Lead a team covering paid and organic search, lifecycle marketing and website development, plus agency partners.

 - Foster a culture of experimentation with clear priorities, regular cadence, and transparent readouts.

 - Report weekly and quarterly to leadership on pipeline, channel performance, conversion and ROI.

 - Build, coach and grow a high-performing remote team.

What you need to succeed:

 - Experience: 10+ years in B2B growth or demand generation at a high-growth SaaS company, including 3+ years leading a team. You've owned pipeline targets across more than one region.

 - Performance marketing depth: Hands-on with SEO, paid search and paid social, and confident managing paid budgets and CPC economics. You know what AEO is and have a point of view on how to win in AI search.

 - Lifecycle and conversion: You've built nurture programs and improved website conversion through steady testing.

 - AI fluency: You use AI tools daily and can show how they changed your output. You're comfortable connecting tools like Claude or ChatGPT to your marketing stack, building agents or AI workflows, and teaching your team to do the same.

 - Analytical agility: You can pull your own data, find where the funnel broke, and make a call. HubSpot and a BI tool (Looker, Tableau or similar) are part of your day.

 - Global performance: Owned pipeline targets across more than one region

 - Leadership and partnership: You build strong remote teams. You have a track record of co-owning pipeline and revenue with sales leaders, earning their trust and influencing how the two teams work together. You communicate performance clearly to executives.

 - Mindset: You are both a leader and a builder – focused on outcomes, effective at rolling your sleeves up and enabling your team to deliver results.

 - Nice to have: Marketing to accounting firms or professional services; fintech or payments; hybrid self-serve and sales-led motions; ABM tools such as DemandBase; Amplitude.

KPIs and success metrics

 - Global digital pipeline: Qualified leads and pipeline from digital channels, against target, by region and segment.

 - Trial and self-serve: Growth in trial, PQL (product-qualified lead) and self-serve signup volume.

 - Revenue impact: New customers and ARR sourced from digital and lifecycle programs.

 - Conversion: Website conversion and stage conversion through nurture to qualified pipeline.

 - Efficiency: Paid media ROI / ROAS and cost per qualified opportunity.

 - AI search visibility: Share of presence for priority queries in AI answers and organic search.

 - Speed of learning: Experiments shipped per month and time from spotting an issue to a fix.

 - Team: Team growth, engagement and AI adoption in day-to-day work

WHO WE ARE

Imprint is on a mission to make every customer a regular.

You know how it feels when you walk into your favorite coffee shop and they know your name and start prepping your usual? Imprint makes it possible for the largest brands to create that experience at scale.

We bring payments, loyalty, and customer intelligence together in one platform, so brands can recognize and reward customers as individuals and keep them coming back. With the power of our technology and data, brands create financial products that their customers’ use everyday, earning more of their spend and increasing loyalty. Customers are rewarded with money and time saved, and surprised and delighted with a more unique, tailored experience.

We first proved our business in co-brand credit cards. For decades, the same few banks dominated the industry, building brands’ programs on mainframes older than the internet. We took a different approach, rebuilding the technology from the ground up. Today, Imprint has more than two million members, with partners like Shell, Kroger, H-E-B, and Booking.com http://Booking.com representing half a trillion dollars in total US consumer spend. Now, we’re growing our partnerships, bringing on more members, and expanding beyond credit cards so that brands offer more ways to pay and be rewarded to recognize their customers as individuals no matter their income or preferences.

Better yet, we’re doing it differently with a lean team of the most talented people on earth. Historically, companies scaled by adding people. Imprint is taking on our opportunity with a small team of exceptional people, with the best AI and technology dramatically amplifying what each person can accomplish. That means you’ll learn faster here than you could anywhere else. You’ll be one of the few people building an entirely new technology with the ownership and trust to shape what Imprint becomes. You’ll work alongside people who make you sharper everyday, armed with tools that turn your best ideas into reality faster than you thought possible. This is a rare chance to do the most important work of your career and to help prove that a small team can build what’s never been done before, inside industries that haven’t changed in decades.

Role Summary

As an AFC Operations Investigator, you will support our AFC (Anti-Financial Crimes) Operations team, which protects Imprint, our partner banks, and our cardholders by detecting, investigating, and reporting money laundering and other illicit activity in line with the Bank Secrecy Act and our BSA/AML program. You'll review transaction monitoring alerts, conduct thorough BSA/AML investigations, and make clear, well-documented case decisions, including preparing Unusual Activity Report (UAR) referrals to our partner banks.

We take an AI-native approach: questioning repetitive work, exploring better investigative methods, and finding practical ways to improve speed and quality, paired with sound investigative judgment, clear documentation, and accountability for every decision. As Imprint launches new products, you'll help us recognize emerging risks and strengthen how we investigate them.

This is a fully remote contract role, Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM in your local time zone, with flexibility as needed.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

 - Working the AFC Operations alert queue independently, meeting established service level agreements with consistently high-quality decisions

 - Writing case narratives and UAR referrals that meet partner bank expectations with minimal revisions

 - Handling sanctions (OFAC) screening reviews and FinCEN 314(a) requests end to end

 - Identified at least one recurring workflow issue and proposed a practical fix, including where AI tools can safely speed up the work

 - Earned trust as a sharp, reliable investigator who raises emerging risks early

Responsibilities

 - Review transaction monitoring alerts in the AFC Operations queue and document clear, well-supported decisions

 - Conduct in-depth BSA/AML investigations into escalated cases to identify potential money laundering and other suspicious activity

 - Write clear, concise, and well-supported case narratives and UAR referrals that meet regulatory and partner bank expectations

 - Support sanctions (OFAC) screening reviews, FinCEN 314(a) requests, and other ad hoc BSA/AML investigations as needed

 - Determine which activity warrants referral, and escalate potential high-risk activity and emerging trends to partner banks in a timely manner

 - Manage case volume effectively, balancing productivity and urgency with quality decisions and established service level agreements

 - Use approved AI tools to support research, analysis, and documentation, verifying material facts against source records and owning the final case assessment

 - Identify emerging patterns, gaps in available information, and recurring workflow issues, and communicate clear examples and recommended next steps

 - Adapt to new products, transaction patterns, and investigative procedures while maintaining consistent standards for evidence and documentation

Qualifications

Required

 - 3+ years of hands-on experience reviewing transaction monitoring alerts and conducting BSA/AML investigations, including writing SAR/UAR narratives

 - Working knowledge of BSA/AML regulations, OFAC sanctions, suspicious activity red flags, and SAR/UAR filing requirements

 - Familiarity with KYC and enhanced due diligence (EDD) practices

 - Sound investigative judgment: you can identify patterns in transaction data, distinguish suspicious activity from unusual but explainable behavior, weigh conflicting evidence, and recognize when further investigation or escalation is needed

 - Experience writing investigative narratives that clearly support a case decision

 - Ability to use or quickly learn AI-assisted workflows, recognize unsupported conclusions, verify outputs, and handle sensitive information in line with company requirements

 - Ability to work independently and resolve cases within service level agreements

 - Strong written and verbal communication, exceptional organization, and attention to detail

 - High school diploma, GED, or equivalent certification; Bachelor's degree preferred

 - CAMS, CFE, or other AML or financial crimes certification

 - Experience with sanctions and politically exposed person (PEP) screening reviews

 - Credit card or fintech industry experience

Job Description

Purified tap water, food and beverage production, massive data centers, and advanced manufacturing facilities all depend on industrial software that can't go down. As a Software Solutions Engineer I, you'll be the person customers call when something breaks, working through root causes with them in real time. Whether your background is in Computer Science or Electrical Engineering/Controls, you’ll help bridge Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT). 



You’ll like this job if: 

You love connecting the dots between a timestamp, a cryptic error message, and a weird software behavior. You see a complex failure as a puzzle, and you won't walk away until you find the root cause. You're also patient and warm with people, even when they're stressed.  You like working as part of a team with both colleagues and customers, in an environment where everyone steps up to help where needed. This is a full-time role that requires on-site work, Monday - Friday for first 90 days. 



Responsibilities:

 - Solving hard problems. Owning complex technical cases: writing and debugging different coding languages, tracking down root-cause architectural issues across platforms, and navigating issues spanning multiple layers and different technologies.

 - Working directly with customers. Helping customers and system integrators by phone and email, whether they're technical or not, and keeping them informed while you work. 

 - Getting very good at root-cause analysis. Building diagnostic skills that will serve you for your whole career. 

 - Documenting as you go. Keeping clear records of ticket progress, issue breakdowns, and resolutions. They become the knowledgebase articles of tomorrow. 

 - Leaving your fingerprints on Ignition. Proposing enhancements, advocating for fixes, and partnering with Software Engineering to shape future releases. The more you master Ignition, the more your ideas drive the roadmap. 

 - Growing with the work. Level I is the start of a path through the Senior Software Solutions Engineer role, where you'll take on the toughest cases and help train the next engineers in. 

 - Getting Ignition Certified. Completing Core and Gold Ignition certifications funded by Inductive Automation before touching a live customer system. 



Requirements:

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Mechatronics, or equivalent hands-on experience with SCADA systems, PLCs, or industrial control networks is required 

 - Comfort writing code (Java, Python, etc.) and SQL queries

 - Familiarity with relational databases (MS SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle, etc.) and how tables relate 

 - Experience with Windows, Linux, and macOS; command line skills are a plus 

 - Comfort troubleshooting live alongside customers 

 - Confidence learning unfamiliar subjects on the fly 

 - Strong written and verbal communication, and the ability to listen, acknowledge frustration, and steer a tense situation toward a solution 



Not required, but preferred:  

 - Customer Service experience 

 - Experience with PLCs (Rockwell/Allen-Bradley, Omron, Siemens, etc.), HMIs, or industrial networks 

 - Experience with Ignition or other SCADA/HMI platforms

 - Lead experiments in customized and cross-channel quoting experiences, setting the hypotheses, success metrics, and next steps based on the results

 - Build and scale AI-native workflows for the quoting experience

 - Professional growth: You build experience in project delivery, customer leadership, business process improvement, and professional services

The Cost Manager leads cost management for Lambda's portfolio of greenfield data center campuses and leased data center sites across the United States. The role reports to the Senior Director of Project Controls.

The Cost Manager owns how project cost is budgeted, committed, forecast, changed, and reported across the portfolio. The role sets the cost management procedures that every project follows, leads a team of cost analysts, and gives leadership an accurate and timely view of cost, forecast at completion, and contingency on every project.

The role brings recognized cost management practice, including AACE International Total Cost Management, earned value management, and owner-side commercial controls, to a fast-moving, capital-intensive AI infrastructure program. The successful candidate will make sure cost surprises are found early, change is controlled, and every dollar is coded the same way from budget through capitalization.

The Cost Manager partners closely with construction, engineering, procurement, finance, accounting, legal, and the other project controls disciplines. At Lambda, Project Controls is being built from first principles, so this role will build the cost management function to the level a multi-campus, multi-gigawatt capital program requires.


What You'll Do

Cost Management Framework

 - Establish and maintain cost management procedures, templates, and guidance for budgeting, commitments, forecasting, change control, and cost reporting, coordinated with the other project controls disciplines.

 - Align cost deliverables with the capital stage-gate process, so budgets and forecasts meet the maturity each gate requires.

 - Partner with cost engineering and Program Services on the code of accounts and WBS, so every project codes cost the same way and maps to capitalization categories.

 - Run periodic cost health reviews of each project, with findings tracked to closure.

Budgets & Forecasting

 - Own the control budget for each campus and lease site, from approved estimate through closeout.

 - Lead the monthly estimate-at-completion (EAC) forecast process with project managers, and challenge forecasts that are not supported by progress, commitments, or known risk.

 - Produce cash flow forecasts and spend curves for each project and the portfolio, in partnership with finance and treasury.

 - Apply earned value management to measure cost and schedule performance where it adds value.

 - Report contingency and management reserve usage against risk remaining, in partnership with Program Services.

Change Control & Commercial Management

 - Own the change control process, covering trends, potential change orders, change requests, and approved change orders, with clear approval thresholds.

 - Lead review and negotiation of contractor change orders, claims, and GMP adjustments with construction, procurement, and legal teams.

 - Review contractor pay applications, schedules of values, retainage, and allowances against contract terms.

 - Support contract strategy and the cost and payment terms in design-build, EPC, GMP, and trade contracts.

 - Lead cost audits of contractor billings and closeout reconciliations.

Reporting & Financial Integration

 - Deliver monthly cost reports for each project and the portfolio, including budget, commitments, actuals, EAC, variance, and contingency.

 - Provide cost data for portfolio dashboards, executive reporting, and board, lender, and partner reporting.

 - Work with accounting on month-end close, accruals, capitalization, and fixed-asset reporting.

 - Make sure cost data in the project controls and ERP systems is complete, accurate, and reconciled.

Leadership

 - Build, lead, and develop a team of cost analysts and cost engineers as the portfolio scales.

 - Provide functional leadership to cost staff and consultants on project teams.

 - Present cost status, forecast risks, and recommended actions clearly to senior leadership and investment decision-makers.

 - Partner with estimating, scheduling, and risk so cost, schedule, risk, and change information is integrated and reliable.

You

 - Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Quantity Surveying, Finance, Business, or a related discipline.

 - Professional credentials such as AACE CCP or EVP, RICS chartered status, or PMP strongly preferred.

 - Typically 8+ years of experience in project cost management on large construction or capital projects, including experience leading a cost team.

 - Owner-side experience setting up cost management procedures and reporting across a multi-project capital program.

 - Expert in budgeting, commitment tracking, EAC forecasting, cash flow forecasting, and change control.

 - Strong commercial skills, including change order and claims negotiation and contractor billing review.

 - Strong understanding of work breakdown structures, codes of accounts, earned value management, and capital accounting requirements.

 - Experience with cost management platforms (for example Oracle Unifier, EcoSys, Procore, or equivalent) and integration with ERP systems.

 - Experience on greenfield construction and MEP-intensive facilities; hyperscale or mission-critical data center experience strongly preferred.

 - Strong analytical and communication skills, with the ability to turn cost data into clear decisions for executives.

Nice to Have

 - Hyperscale, cloud, colocation, or mission-critical data center development.

 - Experience building a cost management function from the ground up.

 - Experience with multi-billion-dollar capital programs or portfolios.

 - Experience with stage-gate or Front-End Loading (FEL) capital governance.

 - Experience with EPC, design-build, GMP, or other major delivery models.

We believe change is constant and our team moves forward as one, with a culture of problem-solving where every employee is empowered and supported to challenge tradition and create solutions. Our mission is simple: to make self-custody accessible and give people the keys to their own financial futures. If you want to make a true impact, we want you to join us at Ledger.

At Ledger, we’re proud to be the global platform for digital assets and Web3, with over 20% of the world’s crypto assets secured through our Ledger devices. With our headquarters in Paris, and offices in Vierzon, Grenoble, Montpellier, London, Portland, Geneva, Zurich and Central Singapore, we have a team of around 600 professionals developing a variety of products and services to enable individuals and companies to securely buy, store, swap, grow and manage crypto assets – including the Ledger hardware wallets line with more than 7.5 millions units already sold in 200 countries.

 

The team:

Directly reporting to the Head of Physical Security, you'll own the security of Ledger's hardware manufacturing and supply chain, from components to finished devices, working with Operations, our contract manufacturers and specialist product-security teams

 

What you’ll be doing:

 - Define and maintain security requirements for manufacturing lines, suppliers and production changes.

 - Protect the exchange and integrity of sensitive manufacturing documentation, firmware and production artifacts, with strong supplier identity and authorisation.

 - Run component provenance checks, lot sampling and inspection, and the security gates of each production run.

 - Plan and run supplier and manufacturing-site assessments together with Physical Security.

 - Coordinate hardware tampering and supply-chain attack tests with Ledger's Donjon team and offensive-security specialists.

 - Set indicators and escalation thresholds, and coordinate investigations when something looks wrong.

 - Report progress and remaining exposure to security leadership.

 - Build and lead the manufacturing security team, and own its strategy, roadmap and budget.

 - Represent manufacturing security to Ledger's executives and to the leadership of our contract manufacturers and key suppliers.

 

What we’re looking for:

 - 10+ years in hardware, electronics or manufacturing security, including 5+ years leading a function or a supplier security programme.

 - Director-level management experience: you have built and led a security team, owned its budget and supplier relationships, and reported to executives.

 - Experience with hardware products built by contract manufacturers.

 - You have found or prevented a real tampering, counterfeit or manufacturing-integrity case.

 - You have run supplier and manufacturing-site assessments and worked directly with engineering and production teams.

 - Knowledge of supply-chain security frameworks such as NIST SP 800-161 and ISO 28000.

 - Fluent English.

The team

To sustain the company's growth, you'll join the Security Engineering team and will be the hands-on security architect for the applications and SaaS tools Ledger runs on: identity, collaboration, customer support, finance and the vendors behind them. You set the architecture standards, take on the hardest threat models yourself, and make sure data exposure through a vendor or an integration is found by us first.

 

What you’ll be doing

 - Lead threat modelling and risk assessment of enterprise applications, SaaS tools and their integrations, hands-on, starting with the most critical tools and suppliers.

 - Set the security architecture standards and reusable patterns for enterprise systems: identity and SSO, access and least privilege, endpoints, network access, logging, data protection and integration tokens.

 - Review new applications, SaaS purchases and major changes at design stage, and agree the conditions for going live.

 - Design data masking and least-privilege access for customer support and customer-data tools.

 - Use offensive security techniques to challenge every design the way an attacker would, and work with the Red Team and external testers to validate it.

 - Turn findings into owned, dated actions, with the GRC team for the risk register.

 - Mentor the security engineers and help them grow into architecture work.
   
    

 

What we’re looking for

 - 10+ years in security engineering or architecture, including 5+ years in architecture and threat modelling for enterprise and cloud environments, and still hands-on.

 - Solid knowledge across the security disciplines: AWS, networking, endpoints, identity and access management (SSO, OAuth, OIDC), application and API security, and SaaS security.

 - Knowledge of offensive security techniques: how attackers abuse identities, integrations, tokens and endpoints, and how they move once inside.

 - Ability to challenge engineering and IT leads, and to be heard.

 - Fluent English is a must; French is a plus.

ABOUT US

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

 - We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

 - We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

 - We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

What you’ll be doing
Let’s get the tricky part out of the way: this role doesn’t fit neatly into a traditional box. It’s part legal ops, part product specialist, part solutions architect, and part client whisperer. If you enjoy roles that stay static, this probably isn’t it. Your mission is to help our clients, some of the most respected legal teams in the world, get the absolute most out of our platform.

Some of what you’ll be up to:

 - Acting as a thought partner to clients - building trusted relationships, addressing tricky pain points, and identifying high-value opportunities for them to scale their use of Legora.

 - Working together with Customer Success in taking full ownership of client relationship - from running pilots in the early stages, to onboarding new users, and ultimately guiding full-firm adoption across major law firms and corporate legal departments.

 - Be the voice of the user inside Legora - sharing insights that directly inform product development, roadmap priorities, and strategic direction.

 - Delivering clear, confident product demos and training that bring the power of our platform to life.

 - Documenting best practices, contribute to the development of scalable playbooks, and help shape how we grow this function globally.

 - Confidently helping our clients navigate one of the biggest shifts in how the legal business operates - from evaluating the ROI and impact of AI to clearly mapping how AI will impact different practice areas



What you bring
You come from the world of law; but you’ve never been content with how things have always been done. You may have started out at a top-tier law firm. Maybe you’ve worked in a corporate legal team, seeing thorny operational problems from the inside. Perhaps you've even tried disrupting the status-quo through a legal tech company, or ventures of your own. Either way, you've had experience beyond the traditional legal career path. Either way, you know how legal teams think, work, and (sometimes) struggle and you're ready to help them level up with technology.



You’ll thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a background in law, with experience at a top-tier firm or in-house legal team.

 - Are tech-curious and product-savvy. Not necessarily a coder, but passionate navigating technical conversations, especially around things like generative AI, technology implementation, innovation and productivity .

 - Communicate clearly and confidently with diverse stakeholders, both lawyers and engineers. I.e. translating across disciplines is second nature to you.

 - Bring structure to ambiguity and energy to complexity; and enjoy being the calm, credible presence in a fast-moving environment.

 - Understand how to evaluate and improve existing processes as a direct result of new and emerging technologies

 - Are proactive, self-directed, and comfortable juggling multiple client relationships at once.

 - Care deeply about quality, but don’t get stuck in perfectionism - you get things done, and you make them better over time.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As an Engagement Director, Financial Services, you’ll own Legora’s partnerships with a focused portfolio of leading financial institutions and help build our approach to the sector. Working directly with General Counsel and senior legal leaders, you’ll shape how their departments put AI to work—and be accountable for turning that ambition into measurable value and long-term growth.

This is a senior, hands-on role combining direct account ownership with leadership of our financial services vertical within Engagement. You’ll lead the account team, develop approaches that work across institutions, and bring client priorities and insights directly into our product strategy, helping shape what Legora builds next.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the strategic partnerships. Set and lead the account strategy for a focused portfolio of financial institutions, connecting legal department priorities, adoption, and commercial growth in a multi-year plan.

 - Advise senior legal leaders. Earn the trust of General Counsel, legal leadership, and legal operations teams. Understand how each department supports the institution’s business and bring a clear perspective on where AI can create the greatest value.

 - Turn strategy into sustained adoption. Partner with Legal Engineering to embed Legora into legal workflows across teams, business lines, and jurisdictions. Build champions and work with client stakeholders to address the governance, security, and operational requirements that affect adoption.

 - Own the growth of the partnership. Be accountable for retention and expansion across your accounts. Lead renewal and growth strategy alongside commercial leadership, building executive support and a compelling business case for extending Legora into additional teams and use cases.

 - Lead the account team. Set priorities for Engagement Managers and Associates supporting your accounts, coach them through complex client situations, and coordinate execution across functions and regions. Keep clear accountability for decisions, commitments, and results.

 - Prove the value. Agree on success measures with each institution and demonstrate improvements in legal workflows, turnaround times, and team capacity. Lead executive reviews that connect those results to renewal and expansion decisions, and intervene early when adoption stalls.

 - Shape Legora’s direction in financial services. Translate insight from your accounts into recommendations for Product, Legal Engineering, and leadership, influencing our roadmap, investment priorities, and approach to the sector.

 - Build the financial services engagement approach. Turn successful use cases and lessons from client delivery into frameworks the wider team can use. Establish repeatable approaches to adoption and value measurement while adapting to each institution’s needs.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - 8+ years in strategic account management, consulting, professional services, or enterprise customer success, or equivalent customer-facing role, with a track record of leading complex relationships, advising senior stakeholders, and delivering measurable business outcomes.

 - Financial services experience. You’ve worked within or advised financial institutions and understand their priorities, operating environments, and decision-making. Experience supporting their in-house legal teams is preferred.

 - Credibility with senior leaders. You earn trust through preparation, judgment, and a clear point of view. You can challenge assumptions, navigate competing interests, and secure commitment from senior stakeholders.

 - Commercial ownership. You’ve translated client value into retention and expansion. You can lead complex renewal conversations, build compelling business cases, and develop a clear strategy for growing a major account.

 - A track record of turning strategy into action. You’ve helped complex organizations adopt new technology and change established ways of working. You know how to build champions and sustain momentum through demanding approval processes.

 - Experience leading teams. You’ve coached client-facing colleagues, set priorities, and held a team accountable for results while maintaining direct ownership of senior client relationships and commercial outcomes.

 - Strong analytical judgment and clear communication. You look beyond headline adoption numbers to understand what’s working, where momentum is stalling, and where an account can grow. You turn those insights into clear recommendations and challenge assumptions when the evidence calls for it.

 - A builder’s mindset. You thrive in ambiguity, take ownership without waiting for direction, and build solutions where no playbook exists. You use AI to automate workflows and turn what you learn into tools and approaches that make the whole team more effective.




WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU

 - Global collaboration: Partner with teams and clients across Europe, APAC, and North America.

 - Competitive package: Comprehensive salary, benefits, and tools for success.

 - Meaningful work: Your efforts shape how thousands of lawyers use AI daily.

 - In-person environment: NYC office designed for ambitious builders and company provided lunch daily.
