 - You ramp quickly. Within your first 30 days, you know our product, our customers and our ideal buyer well, and you're running outbound sequences of your own and booking meetings.

 - You build momentum fast. Within 90 days, you're consistently booking qualified meetings and running your first mid-market opportunities.

 - You grow into a closer. Within 6 to 12 months, you're closing mid-market deals, your outbound plays are used by the wider team, and you're on the path to a full-cycle AE role.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Research target accounts and the people who own support, operations and CX

 - Write and run outbound sequences across email, phone and LinkedIn, using AI tools to research and personalise at scale

 - Book qualified first meetings, and hit weekly activity and pipeline goals

 - Test new angles, segments and messages, and keep the ones that work

 - Share what's working in outbound with the team, and help turn it into a repeatable playbook for EMEA

 - Keep our CRM accurate so the team can see what's in flight

 - Run your own mid-market deals from first meeting to signed contract

 - Learn how a support team operates and show them what Lorikeet can take off their plate, in their own numbers

 - Work with our solutions and implementation teams so new customers get off to a strong start

 - Bring what you hear in the market back to our product and sales teams
   
   


YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU:

 - Have 1 to 3 years in a sales role, such as SDR, BDR or junior AE, ideally in B2B SaaS

 - Have a track record of creating pipeline through cold outbound, and enjoy picking up the phone

 - Have run or helped close deals, or are ready and keen to

 - Get genuinely curious about how a support team works and what's slowing it down

 - Write clearly and concisely, and build trust quickly on calls

 - Are excited about AI and already use AI tools in your own work

 

We care more about drive, curiosity and how fast you learn than about years of experience. If you've been the top performer on an SDR team and want to start closing, we'd like to hear from you.

 

Applicants must be based in the UK and have the right to work in the UK without sponsorship.




WHAT'S UNIQUE ABOUT THIS OPPORTUNITY?


A culture that's genuinely different. Low ego, high trust, no tolerance for talented jerks. We work efficiently, keep hours flexible, and actually mean it — because life outside work matters. We're committed to building a diverse team and actively encourage applicants from underrepresented backgrounds. We care far more about user obsession and eagerness to learn than traditional credentials.


A front-row seat to building something meaningful. We're Series A and moving fast. You'll have real scope to shape the product and the company — not just execute someone else's vision.


Performance recognized in real time, not on a calendar. Promotions happen when you're ready — leadership meets every six weeks specifically to identify and recognize strong performers, so you're never waiting for an arbitrary review window to move up.


We're AI-native, and we'll make you AI-native too. Every person at Lorikeet uses AI in their day-to-day work (current favourite: Claude Code), with unrestricted access and no usage limits. You'll leave with skills that matter for the next decade of work.


Twice a year, the whole company flies to Hawaii. Headquartered in Sydney, with teams spanning the US and UK — which means getting everyone in the same place is something we invest in seriously. We spend the time hacking on ideas, building things together that wouldn't otherwise exist, and making memories that remind you why you joined a startup in the first place.


A recruitment process built on respect, not hoops. We keep it simple: a couple of informal chats to share our story and hear yours, followed by a paid ~two-day work trial. The work trial is genuinely the best part — you'll work on real problems alongside the actual team, get a true feel for how we operate, and we'll both come out of it knowing whether this is the right fit. No trick questions, no take-homes that disappear into a void. Just real work, done together.



If you're from an underrepresented background and don't tick every box, please reach out anyway. We know firsthand that diverse teams perform better, and we're proud that our team reflects a broad spectrum of identities and lived experiences.
Mental Health Therapist - Telehealth (Unrestricted LCSW, LMFT, LPC - New Jersey)

About Lyra   Lyra Clinical Associates partners with Lyra Health, a leading provider of evidence-based mental health care, serving more than 20 million people globally in partnership with employers and more than 100 million through health plan and partner relationships. The company has delivered more than 15 million sessions of mental health care, published more than 35 peer-reviewed studies, and delivered unmatched outcomes in terms of access, clinical effectiveness, and cost efficiency. Lyra members have access to care in one day, and nine out of ten improve with the support of providers like you. Lyra is transforming access to life-changing mental health care through Lyra Empower, the only fully integrated, AI-powered platform combining the highest-quality care and technology solutions. You will be employed by Lyra Clinical Associates. About the Role Lyra developed an innovative video therapy program called Lyra Care Therapy: blending live video sessions with between-session digital psychoeducation and customizable skill building tools. With this program, you’ll have the resources and support you need to ensure that your clients get better—all while improving access to mental health care from your home or preferred setting.    Daily: As a Lyra Care Therapist, you’ll provide short-term, evidence-based treatment via live video, maintaining a caseload of diverse and varied clinical needs. You’ll assign digital lessons, videos, and assessments to your clients to enhance learnings and monitor outcomes between sessions. An important note: Lyra's clients come from a multitude of different backgrounds and experiences, and have varying needs and abilities. We strive to continue to meet their unique needs by delivering culturally responsive care—an approach that accounts for the impact of cultural backgrounds on each person’s care experience.   Regularly: Our therapists enjoy connecting with their peers, who share a passion for providing evidence-based care. You’ll attend one-on-one and peer group clinical consultation meetings, conduct peer-based quality assurance reviews, and attend robust training to enhance your clinical skills. You’ll always have access to expert consultation and support for your most complex clients. It’s like a safety net of resources to help plan the best options—from specialty consultations to culturally responsive care—you’re not alone, even while working remotely within the US.    This role is a great fit if you're a licensed clinician with excellent interpersonal skills, who wants continuous learning and development in their professional career, and thrives in a feedback rich environment. If you have experience with caseloads that include a comprehensive spectrum of mental health needs, from milder presentations to more complex and severe support, we encourage you to apply. If you're comfortable with evolving processes and excited by a rapidly growing business, then this role is for you!
  • Unrestricted LCSW, LMFT, LPC, PsyD, PhD, or equivalent license (i.e., able to work independently, without supervision from a licensed supervisor) without current, past, or pending disciplinary action
  • Master’s degree from a clinical track (e.g., MSW, MFT, MC, MMHC)
  • Experience and commitment to providing evidence-based treatments (e.g., ACT, CBT, CPT, DBT) and clinical best practices (e.g., measurement based care, promoting skills practice)
  • Experience managing risk and responding to clinical crises, as needed
  • Experience providing telehealth therapy services in a virtual environment (video and teletherapy) preferred but not required
  • Computer and live video tools literacy (e.g., Zoom, Google Meets, DoxyMe, Skype, etc.)
  • Experience maintaining a full clinical caseload of adult and/or adolescent clients/week (30 potential bookable calendar spots)
  • Ability to work full-time, approximately 40 hours per week
  • Authorized to work in the United States

Production Engineers at Mercor are software engineers who own the reliability, performance, and operability of the systems that run our business. We're looking for "generalist" engineers who can operate at a Staff level:

 - You're confident in building scalable, distributed systems across the full stack with particular depth on the back end and people usually come to you for technical guidance.

 - You own reliability, security, and networking end to end designing for 99.99%+ uptime, thinking like an attacker to harden your systems, and diving into the network layer yourself rather than treating it as someone else's domain.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

We ingest clinical data for millions of patients from external healthcare sources, with continuous updates for a growing subset of those patients. You'll co own the architecture and evolution of the platform that powers our product and ship it to customers fast.

Day to day, that looks like:

 - Setting the technical direction: defining patterns for low latency, highly scalable, event based systems integrations; being a champion for observability into every part of the platform; establishing patterns and best practices for maintainable code; and fostering effective use of AI in our product (evals, harnesses, observability).

 - Working across our back end heavy platform: our public API (the core product our customers build on), integrations with health information networks (Carequality, CommonWell, eHealth Exchange) and third parties (EHRs, data vendors, partner platforms), and the platform work that lets the rest of the team ship faster.

 - Driving projects end to end, from ideation to production rollout: writing Design Documents, shipping v0's quickly, and iterating to v1 and beyond.

 - Eventually, acting as Team Lead for a group of engineers: breaking down and delegating work, unblocking teammates, and owning your team's delivery while staying hands on in the code.

 - Multiplying the team: mentoring engineers, reviewing designs and PRs, judging when to invest in quality vs. ship fast, and improving our dev processes and tooling so quality and security are enforced by default.

 - Driving bi weekly sprint planning and retros, contributing to the engineering roadmap, joining our daily 30 min remote stand up at 7:30am PST (our only mandatory meeting), and taking part in the on call rotation.

Example projects you could own:

 - Refactoring our core data pipeline to process data 10x faster than originally designed.

 - Use AI/ML to turn freeform doctors' notes into structured data we can add to patients' medical records.

 - Identifying the biggest infra cost opportunities and shipping the changes saving money while increasing scalability.

 - Transforming incoming TCP messages from hospitals using a 90s era protocol into modern HTTP webhooks routed to our customers.

 - Leveling up developer experience: making systems easier to test, tightening CI/CD, and cutting the time from PR to production.




REQUIREMENTS

 - 8+ years as a full stack engineer, with a heavy lean towards back end, public APIs, distributed systems, and complex integrations with external systems.

 - Experience leading engineers, formally or informally with projects where you drove a team's technical direction and delivery, not just your own output.

 - Experience developing, maintaining, and scaling cloud based platforms to many millions or billions of transactions a day including optimizing architecture and code for scalability and cost.

 - You've made engineering teams faster, better developer experience, more testability, shorter release cycles and you can talk about the before/after.

 - You’re located in San Francisco or the Bay Area (or willing to relocate).

 - Bonus:
   
   - Experience processing large amounts of data, including moving it across different services, transforming/consolidating, and building services to query it.
   
   - Healthcare standards/technologies: FHIR, HIE, IHE, EHR/EMR, NPI, TEFCA, ADT, HL7, HEDIS, RAF, SNOMED, LOINC, ICD 10, etc.

As an Advisor Data Analyst, you will serve as a senior subject matter expert responsible for guiding data analysis, integration, conversion, and reporting activities throughout healthcare technology implementation and modernization projects. You will ensure that business and regulatory requirements are accurately translated into technical solutions, while maintaining data integrity, system alignment, and comprehensive project documentation.

  • Serve as a subject matter expert and advisor on Medicaid data, system interfaces, data conversions, reporting, system configuration, and cross-platform integration.

You will join an evolving finance function where analytical excellence, collaboration, and continuous process improvement are highly valued.

  • Develop, manage, and maintain annual budgets, financial forecasts, and multi-year financial plans.

  • Lead monthly and quarterly financial variance analysis, identifying key performance drivers and explaining discrepancies against budgets and forecasts.

  • Partner with business leaders and cross-functional teams to support headcount planning, operational spending, and investment decisions.

  • Build, maintain, and enhance financial models to support strategic planning, scenario analysis, and business performance evaluation.

  • Develop and improve financial dashboards, management reports, and performance tracking tools to provide clear and actionable insights.

  • Translate financial information into meaningful recommendations to support decision-making among senior stakeholders and non-finance teams.

  • Support month-end closing activities and contribute to accurate and timely financial reporting for leadership.

  • Identify opportunities to streamline financial planning processes, improve reporting efficiency, and enhance existing finance tools as the business scales.

  • Take ownership of key FP&A activities and contribute to the continuous development of financial planning and business partnering practices.

    • Requirements:

  • At least 7 years of professional experience in corporate finance, Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A), or finance business partnering, primarily in an in-house environment.

  • Previous experience within a technology company, high-growth business, or similarly dynamic organization is highly desirable.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage substantial financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, or reporting responsibilities.

  • Proven experience influencing senior stakeholders and supporting business decisions through financial analysis and strategic recommendations.

  • Strong financial modelling capabilities and advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets.

  • Experience with financial planning and analysis platforms such as Anaplan, Adaptive Planning, or Pigment is an advantage.

  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex financial information and identify business performance trends.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly when presenting financial insights to non-finance stakeholders.

  • Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and deliver high-quality financial analysis in a fast-paced environment.

  • A proactive, commercially minded approach, combined with strong attention to detail and a collaborative mindset.

  • A professional accounting or finance qualification such as ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CPA, or CFA is considered an advantage but is not mandatory.

  • Senior individual contributors with strong expertise are encouraged to apply; previous management experience or a formal managerial title is not required.

  • Candidates whose experience is exclusively in investment banking or private equity may not be suited to this operational, in-house finance position.

  • Professional fluency in English is required, as both the working environment and interview process are conducted in English.

  • Candidates must be based in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany, Spain, or Switzerland.

    • Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation of $70–$100 per hour, depending on location, experience, and qualifications.

  • Full-time engagement of approximately 40 hours per week.

  • Fully remote working arrangement, with flexibility to work from an eligible country.

  • Opportunity to work directly within the finance team of a leading AI-focused organization.

• Analyze utility billing data using Python and specialized analytical tools to identify billing errors, misapplied rates, overlooked credits, and other cost-saving opportunities.

  • Learn and interpret complex tariff schedules, demand charge calculations, rider provisions, tax codes, regulatory requirements, and jurisdiction-specific billing rules.

  • Conduct retrospective audits covering the full applicable statute of limitations, often six years or more, to maximize potential client recoveries.

  • Develop original, technically defensible claim theories by combining regulatory knowledge with pattern recognition across billing histories, meter data, and account classifications.

  • Prepare persuasive claim submissions, client summaries, and regulatory correspondence that explain complex billing issues clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Communicate with clients, utility providers, tax authorities, and regulatory agencies to pursue claims and secure identified savings.

  • Follow up on disputed or delayed claims and escalate matters through appropriate administrative and regulatory channels when necessary.

  • Coordinate with external legal specialists when claims require additional legal or regulatory support.

  • Maintain accurate documentation of claims, supporting evidence, correspondence, deadlines, and recovery outcomes from identification through payment.

  • Collaborate with technical and information systems teams to develop and improve analytical tools, automate anomaly detection, and strengthen account review processes.

  • Manage changing priorities across accounts, jurisdictions, and claim types while maintaining accuracy and meeting deadlines.

    • Requirements:

  • Approximately 1–3 years of relevant experience, or equivalent academic, internship, or project experience demonstrating the ability to master complex, rule-based systems and translate that knowledge into practical opportunities.

  • Completed undergraduate degree, or expected completion within six months. STEM, economics, finance, regulatory affairs, and pre-law backgrounds are preferred, although candidates from other disciplines are welcome.

  • Proficiency in Python is required, particularly for extracting, cleaning, analyzing, and interrogating large datasets and automating anomaly detection. Experience with additional programming languages is an advantage.

  • Strong analytical reasoning and the ability to absorb detailed regulatory codes, tariff schedules, tax rules, accounting standards, or comparable technical frameworks.

  • Intellectual curiosity and tenacity, with the determination to pursue well-supported claims through challenges and setbacks.

  • Creative problem-solving skills and the ability to develop original, technically sound approaches that can withstand regulatory scrutiny.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare persuasive reports and present findings confidently to clients, utility representatives, and regulators.

  • Comfort working with ambiguity, interpreting complex or inconsistent regulatory language, and identifying opportunities others may overlook.

  • Adaptability and strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple accounts, shifting priorities, and deadlines without sacrificing precision.

  • Experience working for a regulated public utility, particularly in rate billing analysis or customer-facing operations, is a significant advantage.

  • Must reside in the Eastern or Central Time Zone. Eligible Central Time locations include Missouri, Arkansas, Mississippi, and Alabama.

  • Must be a U.S. citizen or an active Green Card holder. Visa sponsorship is not available.

  • Availability for full-time remote work, with core working hours from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM Eastern Time.

    • Benefits:

  • Base salary: $40,000 annually, increasing to $45,000 upon successful completion of auditing skills benchmarks.

  • Performance bonuses: Monthly bonuses begin after onboarding and are directly linked to the refunds and savings claims generated. Established analysts regularly earn $1,000–$3,000 or more per month in bonuses.

  • Total earning potential: Strong performers can reach approximately $55,000–$76,000 or more annually, with further potential as expertise and claim results grow.

  • Paid training: Three-month intensive onboarding program designed to build expertise in utility auditing, regulatory billing, and forensic analysis.

  • Career progression: Opportunities to advance to Senior Analyst, Practice Lead, or Client Relationship Manager, with high performers potentially progressing within two to three years.

  • Healthcare coverage: Health, dental, and vision insurance.

  • Retirement: 401(k) plan with company matching.

  • Paid time off: Three weeks of PTO plus 11 paid holidays.

  • Work flexibility: Full-time remote position, subject to the specified Eastern or Central Time Zone residency requirements.

• Own financial forecasting for the Customer Experience organization, developing bottom-up projections for renewals bookings, gross and net revenue retention (GRR/NRR), Professional Services revenue, and Support revenue and costs.
  • Reconcile financial forecasts with CRM data, identify performance risks and growth opportunities, and communicate key findings and recommendations to leadership.
  • Lead quarterly financial reporting and performance reviews, preparing business commentary for Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and board materials while explaining variances against budgets and previous forecasts.
  • Drive renewals and customer retention analytics by monitoring churn, contraction, expansion, pricing uplift realization, and gross and net retention performance.
  • Partner with Customer Success and Renewals teams to assess at-risk customer accounts and develop actionable insights to improve retention outcomes.
  • Evaluate Customer Success performance through analysis of customer success manager productivity, account coverage, customer segmentation, and resource allocation models.
  • Monitor Professional Services and Support financial performance, including bookings, backlog, utilization, margins, staffing requirements, and cost-to-serve metrics.
  • Develop and maintain financial models for platform migration initiatives, tracking key performance indicators and progress against strategic objectives.
  • Lead strategic financial planning by identifying growth opportunities within the existing customer base and developing targets that support annual budgets and long-range business plans.
  • Partner with the Center of Excellence (CoE) to manage organizational spending, including headcount, travel and entertainment (T&E), and discretionary expenses.
  • Provide regular budget-versus-actual analysis and financial guidance to Customer Experience leadership to support informed operational decisions.

  • Collaborate with Sales Operations, Strategic Finance, and the broader FP&A team to ensure consistency across financial forecasts, reporting, and business planning.

Senior Digital Forensics or Incident Response Specialist Lead

The role focuses on leading cybersecurity incident response activities, conducting advanced digital forensic investigations, and coordinating vulnerability remediation efforts. You will ensure incidents are properly assessed, documented, escalated, and resolved while maintaining compliance with established federal security standards and operational procedures.

  • Lead incident intake, initial assessments, vulnerability evaluations, forensic scoping, and incident response planning.

  • Coordinate time-sensitive remediation activities for vulnerabilities listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, including three-calendar-day remediation requirements.

  • Collaborate with security teams and system owners to prioritize remediation activities and ensure timely resolution of critical vulnerabilities.

  • Conduct advanced digital forensic investigations across endpoints, networks, cloud environments, and security logging systems.

  • Analyze indicators of compromise (IOCs), malicious persistence mechanisms, unauthorized access, and potential data exfiltration activities.

  • Oversee digital evidence preservation, documentation, and chain-of-custody procedures to maintain forensic integrity.

  • Coordinate incident escalation and response activities with relevant technical and operational stakeholders.

  • Validate remediation actions and confirm that identified security issues have been effectively addressed.

  • Prepare detailed technical investigation findings, forensic triage reports, and executive-level summaries.

  • Communicate incident status, investigation outcomes, and remediation progress to relevant stakeholders.

  • Obtain required approvals before implementing operational changes or undertaking activities that exceed authorized labor hours.

  • Ensure incident response activities align with applicable federal security requirements, established procedures, and industry best practices.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate is an experienced cybersecurity professional with strong expertise in digital forensics, incident response, and security operations.   • Strong knowledge of NIST Special Publication 800-86 and its digital forensic investigation guidelines.

  • Familiarity with CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) processes and federal incident response practices.

  • Relevant professional certifications such as CISSP, GCFA, GCFE, or equivalent credentials.

  • Practical experience using digital forensic investigation tools, Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) platforms, and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solutions.

  • Experience analyzing security logs and investigating threats across endpoint, network, and cloud environments.

  • Strong understanding of incident investigation methodologies, evidence preservation, chain of custody, and remediation validation.

  • Ability to lead incident response activities, coordinate multiple stakeholders, and manage time-sensitive security priorities.

  • Excellent analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare technical reports and executive summaries.

THE ROLE

Special Projects is the business team inside the Office of the CEO. The team is composed of attorneys, strategy analysts, and other personnel whose objectives are to drive CEO priorities and execute on company decisions. Special Projects focuses primarily on work that serves the company’s growth by deciding what to prioritize, sizing the opportunity, building the plan, and driving it through to revenue. This work helps leadership decide where to invest, which offerings to develop, and how to turn promising ideas into businesses that scale.

As a Senior Strategy Associate, you will own initiatives from an initial question through research, a business plan, and execution. That could mean evaluating a new client segment, developing a new service offering, or determining whether a recurring client need warrants a product. You will build the financial model, speak with prospective customers, work through delivery requirements, and help secure the first clients. As an initiative develops, you will help establish the operating model and its long-term ownership.

You will bring your skillset and subject matter expertise from investment banking, VC, or similar fields–researching, financial modelling, valuation, diligence, and creation of client materials; however, your role within the OCEO will be much more expansive. You will rely on your problem-solving skills and quantitative background to build out plans, map out pricing, identify potential clients, and provide a clear path to executing on particular initiatives. This role suits someone who combines rigorous analytical training with hands-on experience building in an uncertain and intense environment. You enjoy figuring out what needs to happen, bringing the right people together, and taking responsibility for the result.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Identify and test new opportunities: Develop ideas from client conversations, market research, developments in AI, and company priorities. Assess the customer problem, competitive alternatives, willingness to pay, and why Norm is positioned to succeed.

 - Build a business plan: Define the target customer and offering, size the market, and work through cost to deliver, pricing structure, and revenue plan. Identify the people, technology, and milestones needed to execute, and present a clear recommendation on whether and how to proceed.

 - Translate results into strategy: Compare actual demand, delivery costs, and client feedback with the original plan. Recommend where to expand, change direction, build internally, work with a partner, or stop.

 - Build the tools and processes the work needs: Use AI to accelerate research, analysis, prototyping, and execution. Create practical workflows that improve how the team operates and measure whether they help.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Analytical training paired with operating experience: 4+ years in a relevant role. A strong candidate might have spent approximately two years in investment banking or consulting, followed by meaningful experience at a startup, in a founder’s office, or building a venture. We also welcome candidates with equivalent financial rigor and a demonstrated record of execution.

 - Ownership under ambiguity: You have taken responsibility for an initiative where the problem, approach, or operating process was not fully defined. You can explain what you decided, what you personally did, what changed, and what you learned.

 - Good with numbers: You can size a market from scratch, build a financial model, propose a price, and defend the arithmetic. You know which assumptions drive the answer, how to test them, and when the numbers suggest we should change direction.

 - Strong discretion: You will work on confidential and sensitive matters across the company.

 - Enjoy being held to a very high standard.

 - Strong customer and stakeholder skills: You can lead discovery conversations, uncover the need behind a request, and earn trust with clients, senior leaders, lawyers, and technical colleagues.

 - Clear writing and independent thinking: You turn incomplete information into concise recommendations, explain tradeoffs, and revise your view when the evidence changes.

 - AI fluency: You use AI regularly and can demonstrate tools, workflows, or automations you have built or materially improved.

 - Low ego, sound judgment, and follow-through: You seek input, work across disciplines, handle sensitive information carefully, and stay accountable through the details of execution.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience launching an offering, entering a new market, winning initial customers, or establishing a new operating process.

 - Exposure to financial institutions, asset managers, or professional services.

 - Experience with pricing, product development, customer discovery, or go-to-market execution.

About AIVista

NTT DATA AIVista, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of NTT DATA, is based in Silicon Valley. We develop AI products for enterprises operating in complex regulatory environments. The Role

The Applied Scientist will develop methods that turn natural-language intent into structured, machine-checkable artifacts and use those artifacts to make AI-driven software development more verifiable, traceable, and reliable. You will work from policies, regulations, standard operating procedures, requirements, process descriptions, application programming interfaces, and code to construct formal specifications, rule ontologies, process ontologies, contracts, tests, and proofs with complete source traceability.

The work addresses two distinct assurance problems. Validation asks whether a formal artifact faithfully captures authorized intent. Verification asks whether an implementation satisfies that artifact. You will build measurable validation methods for omissions and mistranslations, integrate independent checkers and proof systems, and carry the resulting evidence through the AI-driven software development life cycle. The objective is a practical development workflow in which models may propose requirements, designs, code, tests, or proofs, while deterministic checkers, versioned evidence, and human authority determine what is accepted.

Responsibilities

 - Develop autoformalization methods that translate policies, procedures, regulations, requirements, and process descriptions into typed rules, process models, contracts, and formal specifications.

 - Design restricted domain-specific languages and formal semantics that domain experts and engineers can review together, with clause-level provenance and versioned change histories.

 - Build validation stacks using controlled source language, concretization, counterexamples, back-translation, cross-representation consistency, independent dual translation, and expert adjudication.

 - Create specification-mutation, non-vacuity, and seeded-defect benchmarks that measure detection rates for omissions, weakenings, exception errors, and mistranslations.

 - Integrate satisfiability modulo theories solvers, model checkers, theorem provers, static analyzers, type systems, and property-based or fuzz testing into independent verification harnesses.

 - Develop verifier-guided generation and repair methods for specifications, code, tests, invariants, proofs, and counterexamples while keeping the checker outside the generative model's trusted path.

 - Apply formal methods across the AI-driven software development life cycle, from requirements and architecture through model-generated implementation, continuous integration, release evidence, monitoring, and change-impact analysis.

 - Study composition at system scale, proof and specification maintenance under change, and methods for preserving evidence across tool, model, dependency, and compiler versions.

 - Connect formal artifacts to AIVista's data, rule, action, and process ontologies so runtime decisions can be traced to governing sources, versions, evaluated values, and accepted checks.

 - Define assurance claims with explicit scope, assumptions, trusted components, checker versions, and acceptance boundaries; prevent stronger claims than the evidence supports.

 - Partner with product and engineering teams to transition successful methods into production authoring, verification, and AI-driven software development workflows.

 - Lead publications, patents, open-source contributions, and research partnerships in formal methods, programming languages, software engineering, knowledge representation, and AI-driven software development.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Optical Mechanical Engineer to design, prototype, and validate high-density fiber interconnects for our AI infrastructure. You’ll work across MT ferrule–based connectors and adapters, optical transceiver mechanical designs, tray-level optical assemblies, and fiber shuffle solutions, translating optical and system requirements into reliable, manufacturable hardware.

This is a hands-on role spanning detailed mechanical design, lab testing, and integration. You’ll partner with optical, mechanical, networking, manufacturing, and data center teams to make fiber connections practical to assemble, route, test, and service—from within a tray or rack to the cabling infrastructure connecting racks.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and test MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters, addressing alignment, tolerances, retention, mating repeatability, and serviceability.

 - Develop mechanical designs for optical transceivers and tray-level optical solutions, balancing packaging density, thermal interfaces, assembly access, and fiber management.

 - Design and validate high-density fiber shuffle assemblies, including shuffle cassettes, with clear connectivity maps, controlled routing, and accessible test interfaces.

 - Define and execute optical-mechanical validation plans, including optical loss measurements, connector inspection, mating cycles, and relevant environmental and mechanical testing.

 - Develop fiber routing within and between racks, accounting for bend radius, strain relief, cable management, labeling, installation, and maintenance access.

 - Partner with data center and network teams to translate fiber layouts and cabling infrastructure requirements into hardware interfaces and integration plans.

 - Work with suppliers and manufacturing partners to build prototypes, resolve failures, improve assembly consistency, and transition validated designs into production.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - You have hands-on experience designing and testing MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters.

 - You have developed and tested fiber interconnects, including high-density fiber solutions, and can connect mechanical design decisions to optical performance.

 - You have experience with the mechanical design and integration of optical transceivers and tray-level optical assemblies.

 - You have designed and validated fiber shuffle solutions, such as shuffle cassettes, including connectivity, routing, assembly, and test considerations.

 - You understand fiber routing within and between racks, including bend-radius constraints, strain relief, connector access, and serviceability.

 - You are familiar with data center fiber layouts and the cabling infrastructure that supports installation, expansion, and operation.

 - You can move between detailed design and hands-on debugging, use measurements to identify root causes, and work with engineering and manufacturing partners to implement practical improvements.

About the role

We’re looking for a Startup Ecosystem Account Director to help more startups across Asia Pacific build and grow with OpenAI. You’ll focus on the broad base of startups beyond our sales team’s 1:1 coverage, creating engagement approaches that help founders and developers discover our products, get started, and deepen their adoption over time.

This role combines growth marketing, field marketing, online events, content, and ecosystem partnerships. You’ll connect these activities into a coherent journey from a startup’s first interaction with OpenAI to sustained product usage and revenue growth.

You’ll join the APAC Startups team and work closely with sales, technical, marketing, developer relations, and partnerships colleagues. This is a hands-on role for someone who is comfortable owning a revenue target and can set strategy, run experiments, and build repeatable programs across diverse markets.

In this role, you’ll:

 - Own growth across startups beyond active sales coverage. Develop and execute a regional strategy to increase revenue by driving engagement, with a particular focus on API and ChatGPT adoption.

 - Build scalable startup journeys. Create programs that move founders and developers from initial interest to their first working use case, production deployment, and broader adoption.

 - Run field and online programs. Design founder gatherings, technical workshops, hackathons, webinars, and other formats with clear audiences, follow-up journeys, and measurable outcomes.

 - Collaborate with Marketing to create useful content. Work with technical experts, marketers, and customers to produce practical guides, demos, startup stories, and campaigns that help teams solve problems and build with OpenAI.

 - Develop lifecycle campaigns. Use email, digital channels, and product and engagement signals to deliver relevant guidance at key moments in a startup’s journey.

 - Extend our reach through partners. Collaborate with venture capital firms, accelerators, startup communities, and other ecosystem partners to reach and support founders at scale.

 - Prioritize across APAC. Segment audiences by market, stage, use case, and adoption maturity, adapting programs to local needs while building formats that can be reused across the region.

 - Connect growth programs to sales. Establish clear signals and handoffs for startups that would benefit from direct commercial or technical support.

 - Measure and improve performance. Own a dashboard spanning activation, sustained usage, revenue growth, retention, and program efficiency. Use experiments and cohort analysis to identify what works and where to invest.

 - Own execution. Manage the program calendar, budget, agencies, and vendors, balancing ambitious goals with disciplined delivery.



We’re seeking someone with:

 - 6+ years of experience in growth, lifecycle, developer, or field marketing for a technology business, ideally serving startups or developers.

 - A track record of turning campaigns and programs into measurable product adoption and revenue growth.

 - Experience combining events, content, digital channels, and lifecycle marketing into an integrated growth motion.

 - Strong analytical judgment: you can define success, interpret funnel and cohort data, and distinguish activity from business impact.

 - Strong writing and storytelling skills, with the ability to make technical topics useful and accessible to founders and builders.

 - Experience working across APAC, with an understanding of how startup ecosystems, languages, and routes to market vary across the region.

 - The ability to work effectively with sales, technical teams, marketing, and ecosystem partners.

 - An ownership mindset and the willingness to move between strategy and hands-on execution.



You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Enjoy helping startups turn promising ideas into products customers use.

 - Are curious about AI and willing to learn about APIs and developer workflows, with support from technical colleagues.

 - Think about the full customer journey, including what happens after an event, content download, or first API call.

 - Know when to tailor a program to a local market and when to build a repeatable regional approach.

 - Bring structure to ambiguity, test ideas quickly, and use evidence to decide what to scale.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Contents Property Claims Adjuster is an individual contributor role within Openly's Property Claims organization, responsible for managing high-value homeowner personal property claims from first notice of loss through resolution. This position demands a rare combination of deep technical content claims expertise, exceptional communication skills, and the confidence to make difficult, independent decisions on moderate to large personal property losses. The right candidate can write and critically review large, intricate estimates; navigate sophisticated coverage questions; and deliver a superior policyholder experience at every touchpoint.



The ideal candidate is a consummate professional who commands every file with proactive ownership and unwavering integrity. They bring urgency and genuine empathy to every interaction, and they thrive in an environment that demands both independent judgment and close collaboration.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Claim Investigation & Coverage Analysis

 - Manage end-to-end moderate to large personal property claim handling from FNOL through closure, including supplements, ensuring timely and accurate resolution.

 - Conduct thorough investigations including review of policy terms, coverage analysis, and determination of liability.

 - Examine claims for potential subrogation opportunities and identify potential fraudulent issues.

 - Determine the appropriate method of inspection (virtual, field, or third-party) based on claim complexity and circumstances.

 - Conduct virtual inspections using video, AI-assisted tools, and other emerging technology platforms.



Estimating & File Documentation

 - Write and critically review large personal property damage estimates using Cotality along with other types of estimating software, adhering to established best practices and applying independent technical judgment to scope and methodology.

 - Prepare and maintain thorough file documentation, including coverage letters, estimates, activity notes, and settlement documentation.

 - Adhere to reserving best practices and update reserves accurately throughout the life of the claim.



Customer Service & Communication

 - Provide superior customer service to policyholders, claimants, and agents throughout the claims process, serving as the primary point of contact and ensuring every party has clarity, confidence, and timely communication at every stage.

 - Communicate and coordinate effectively with a wide range of stakeholders — including public adjusters (PAs), contractors, building consultants, engineers and technical experts, and attorneys — maintaining clear, professional, and proactive communication throughout the life of the claim.

 - Negotiate settlement of claims with insureds, claimants, public adjusters, and vendors with fairness, professionalism, and confidence — asking tough questions, challenging unsupported positions, and working through complex or convoluted situations to reach well-reasoned resolutions.

 - Maintain absolute, proactive control of every file — anticipating next steps, setting clear action plans, and driving claims forward without waiting for external prompts.

 - Conduct and lead virtual inspections with public adjusters, contractors, customers, and building consultants as a core tool for proactively managing claims, gathering accurate information, and making the right method-of-inspection (MOI) decisions — balancing thoroughness with expense management.
   
   

Negotiation & Independent Decision-Making

 - Apply strong negotiation skills to work through complex, high-stakes, and often convoluted claim situations — asking tough questions, identifying gaps in logic or documentation, and securing fair outcomes for all parties.

 - Make difficult, independent decisions with confidence and sound judgment, taking ownership of outcomes and escalating appropriately when the situation warrants.



Vendor & Partner Collaboration

 - Manage and coordinate with vendor partners — including contractors, independent adjusters (PAs), building consultants, engineers, and other service providers — to drive accurate, efficient, and aligned claim outcomes.

 - Collaborate closely with structure adjusters on dual-handled claims, working in a coordinated and seamless manner to deliver a unified, stress-free experience for the customer.

 - Partner with internal functions — including SIU, Subrogation, Legal, and Catastrophe — to drive aligned claim outcomes, and actively contribute to team roundtable discussions, bringing insights and collaboration that elevate the performance of the entire team.

 - Experience writing estimates in Cotality, Xactimate, Claimtouch or a comparable platform

 - Proven ability to independently write and critically review estimates — not merely reviewing estimates prepared by others, but authoring them with technical precision and scope accuracy

 - Active adjuster license(s) or eligibility to obtain licenses in all required states; must maintain licensure as a condition of continued employment

 - Experience in a remote or hybrid claims environment

 - Proficiency in Microsoft and Google productivity tools

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and persuasively across diverse audiences including policyholders, public adjusters, contractors, experts, and legal counsel

 - Strong organization, time management, and multi-tasking abilities

 - Demonstrated negotiation skills with a track record of successfully resolving complex, disputed, and high-stakes claims through persistence, preparation, and professional confidence

 - Ability to work from home without distraction

The Revenue Operations Manager is building the forecasting and pipeline infrastructure that Openly's leadership depends on. Your first priority is establishing a clean, reliable system and a support function the GTM team trusts and uses.



Salesforce: Shape how our GTM tech stack evolves, with Salesforce at its core. You are the first responder when something breaks and the person accountable for keeping it clean. Working with the Revenue Operations Manager, you decide how requests get built, test every change in a sandbox before it reaches production, and document what you ship so the system stays understandable as we grow. You make sure what we build is still the right answer six months from now.

Integrations: You support how HubSpot, Outreach, and Zendesk connect to Salesforce, and you keep data moving between them. When a sync breaks or data goes missing, you find the root cause and fix it there. Along the way, you learn how these tools fit together.

Reports & Dashboards: Build and maintain reports and dashboards that give leadership and field teams visibility into the pipeline. You are building what the Revenue Operations Manager designs, accuracy and reliability are your accountability.

User Support & Training: Be the first point of contact for data issues, access problems, and workflow questions from the BizDev team. Data & Process Integrity: Support the data quality program in partnership with the Revenue Operations Manager, auditing records, identifying data gaps, and enforcing entry standards before problems show up in reporting. Documentation: Create and maintain documentation for system configurations, processes, and SOPs. When something changes, the docs change with it. The goal is a team that is never dependent on tribal knowledge.

Tech Stack Partnership: Partner with the Revenue Operations Manager on evaluation and implementation of new tools. You are not setting the strategy for what gets added, but you are a critical voice in whether something can be operationalized and you own the configuration work when it does.

 - Comfortable supporting HubSpot and sales engagement tools (Outreach or similar), especially the integrations that connect them to Salesforce.

 - Detail-oriented and process driven. You catch data quality issues before they become reporting problems.

 - A clear communicator who can explain CRM concepts to non-technical users without condescension and escalate issues clearly.

 - You run an intake process, ask the questions that uncover the real problem, and push back when a request would create a one-off configuration or technical debt.

 - Proactive about documentation. You write things down so the next person can succeed without asking you every question.

About Persona

Persona https://withpersona.com/ is the configurable identity platform built for businesses in a digital-first world. Verifying individuals and organizations is harder — but more important — than ever, with AI enabling fraudsters to launch sophisticated accounts at scale and regulations evolving rapidly.

We’ve built Persona to support practically every use case and industry — that’s why we’re able to serve a wide range of leading companies. For example, Reddit relies on Persona for age assurance and verification to comply with online safety regulations, protecting younger users while maintaining a seamless experience. Meanwhile, OpenAI relies on Persona to keep bad actors out, protecting one of the world’s most powerful AI platforms from large-scale abuse in a time when AI is reshaping the way we work and live.

We’re growing rapidly and looking for exceptional people to join us!




ABOUT THE ROLE

Persona is building its first dedicated commercial presence in APAC. This opportunity has a main focus in Australia & New Zealand but would be an integral part of the broader APAC team. The person who stands up ANZ sales arm should also be able to support strategic deals, regulatory groundwork, and partnerships across the wider region as we expand as well as attend conferences for lead generation and brand awareness in the region. This is a first-AE, build-from-scratch seat with lots of ownership. It's deliberately broader than a pure sales quota. We're looking for someone who can sell, but who can also be our in-region regulatory partner, lead major tender responses, and build the ecosystem of relationships that a new market requires. If ANZ ramps more slowly than we'd like, this role still delivers regional value through APAC deal support, accreditation groundwork, and partnerships.




WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT

You'll be Persona's first dedicated seller in the region and define the ICP, the partnerships, and the regulatory playbook from first principles. You'll be the person we lean on for the Australian digital identity regulatory regime, for leading complex public-sector and enterprise tenders, and for representing Persona in industry and regulatory forums. You'll operate cross functionally - one week you might be running a strategic enterprise deal; the next, coordinating Product, Legal, Compliance and Security into a government tender, or partnering with our Compliance team on an accreditation path.




WHAT YOU'LL DO AT PERSONA:

 - Stand up and own the ANZ sales motion as Persona's first dedicated in-region seller. Build the ICP for ANZ. Today we segment between companies founded in Australia expanding globally vs. companies founded internationally with an Australian arm; how we work with each differs.

 - Contribute to strategic and enterprise deals across APAC, partnering with the AE team and APAC leads on relevant accounts, so the role delivers regional value beyond ANZ.

 - Contribute to Persona's regulatory accreditation strategy across ANZ. Based on prospect feedback, proactively identify where an accreditation or certification would unlock the market, build the internal case for it (the why, backed by concrete deal and buyer examples), and then lead the process end-to-end, in partnership with Compliance and Legal, to secure it.

 - Lead ANZ tender responses (RFP / RFI / RFT) end-to-end from qualification and win-strategy through to coordinating Product, Legal, Compliance and Security inputs into a polished submission. These are major, time-intensive efforts and are often the primary route into government and large regulated buyers across the region.

 - Represent Persona at regional and global identity, fraud, and RegTech conferences, nurturing an existing network into qualified pipeline.

 - Act as the in-region competitive subject-matter expert for opportunities across APAC.

 - Establish relationships with industry, compliance and regulatory bodies to generate leads, identify key stakeholders, secure certifications, advocate for Persona's interests, and help shape regulation.

 - Identify and develop alternative sales channels and strategic partnerships (resellers, distributors, system integrators) to grow regional market presence.





WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

 - Proven enterprise / strategic sales experience in identity verification, RegTech, fintech, compliance technology, or an adjacent regulated space — ideally selling into APAC/ANZ.

 - Deep familiarity with the Australian regulatory and compliance landscape (KYC/AML, digital identity, AUSTRAC direction).

 - Experience owning complex, multi-stakeholder deals and coordinating cross-functional inputs (Product, Legal, Compliance, Security) to drive a specific outcome.

 - A genuine networker who is comfortable representing a company on stage and at industry events, and turning that presence into pipeline.

 - Comfort operating in ambiguity and building processes, playbooks, and ICPs where none exist yet.

 - Strong written communication with ability to explain complex technical and regulatory topics clearly.

ABOUT PLANE

Plane's mission is to build the infrastructure the world's work runs on. Every organization runs on three things: the projects it's driving, the knowledge it keeps, and the requests it fields. Plane brings all three into one open, adaptable platform: simple enough for any team to adopt, dependable enough for organizations to build on. And we are building it for a future where humans and AI agents do that work together.

 

Plane began in public on GitHub at the end of 2022. Since then it has grown into a work management platform used by teams around the world: 63,000+ stars, 6,500+ forks, and a contributor community that reads our code and files our issues. Organizations run Plane as a managed Cloud service, on their own infrastructure, or inside fully isolated environments. Building in the open keeps us close to users and raises the standard for everything we ship.

 

Plane is the #1 work infrastructure in aerospace, defense, financial services, and other regulated industries: organizations whose requirements for control, auditability, and data residency rule most software out. When the strictest buyers pick a system of record, that choice means something. Adoption is growing fastest on Plane Cloud and in sovereign clouds, deployments that keep everything inside a country's own borders and rules.

 

Plane is backed by top investors and built across San Francisco, London, and Hyderabad. We work in tightly knit teams, stay close to users, and care about the visible product as much as the unglamorous details that make software dependable. People own problems end to end, and we add process only when it helps the work.

 


HUMANS AND AGENTS

We believe the next decade of work will be done by humans and AI agents together. Not agents replacing people, and not a chat window bolted onto software built for humans clicking around, but both working in one system of action, where an agent's work is as visible and as accountable as a person's. 

 

Most software treats AI as a feature. We treat agents as a kind of worker, and that changes what the system underneath has to be. Agents are only as good as the context they can see and the state they are allowed to change, so shared context, explicit state, durable history, and accountable action are not items on our roadmap. They are the product. Plane is built so that when an agent acts, the humans responsible can see what happened, why, and on whose authority, and the record survives.

 

This is what the infrastructure is for: making the future where humans and agents work together useful, legible, and fully within the organization's control. Every role at Plane is some part of building that.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

Plane gets evaluated in public. Our docs, our issue tracker, and comparison pages written by competitors are all evidence a buyer collects before they talk to anyone here. You will own the content that meets them there, which means the roadmap of what we publish, the standard every page is held to, and most of the drafts. This is a writing job first. You will work with product managers on what shipped rather than what was announced, with Sales on the objections that stall enterprise evaluations, and with the community team, whose forum threads are a steady supply of real questions.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the content roadmap across discovery and evaluation: what gets written, refreshed, consolidated, or killed. You defend those calls with signups, product qualified leads, and assisted conversions rather than pageviews.

 - Own the comparison and migration surfaces for Jira, Asana, Monday.com, and ClickUp. These pages get read mid-evaluation with a competitor's sales team in the other tab, so they have to be accurate enough to survive that reader.

 - Write for two audiences without patronizing either. A self-hoster debugging a container upgrade and a VP of engineering justifying a migration budget both have to reach the end of the page.

 - Turn releases into content that says what changed and who it is for, built from the pull requests and the product manager rather than from the announcement blurb.

 - Build the proof that shortens an enterprise evaluation: deployment stories, customer evidence, and content on security, governance, and data residency. Much of this means asking regulated customers for permission we will sometimes not get, and writing without it when we do not.

 - Work daily with product managers, design, and community, and put every technical draft in front of the engineer who built the thing before it goes live.

 - Do the maintenance: auditing pages that rank for the wrong query, rewriting posts that aged badly after a release, fixing internal links across the site, and consolidating pages that compete with each other.

 


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - You ship final drafts You write long form that goes live with light editing, and you can point to three pieces you would still defend a year later.

 - You have grown organic traffic that converted Keyword strategy, internal linking, refreshes, and topical authority are things you have run end to end, with signups or pipeline at the other end of them.

 - You write about technical products without distorting them You have covered software you did not build, checked claims against the product, and been corrected by an engineer without it becoming a problem.

 - You have written competitive content Comparison, migration, or alternatives pages in a category where the other side had a bigger budget than you.

 - You have editorial judgment about other people's work You can brief a writer, cut a draft in half, and explain why, because part of this job is improving writing you did not do.

 


NICE TO HAVES

 - You have used Plane, run it self-hosted, or written for an open project whose community will correct you in public.

 - You have written security, compliance, and deployment content: SSO, audit logs, data residency, air-gapped installs.

 - You have built templates, docs-adjacent content, or product education that people still use.

 - You have opinions about what AI search is doing to content strategy, and you have tested them.

 


WHY PLANE?

Every company says it is different. We will try evidence instead.

 

The scope is real. We are a passion team serving companies of every size, including some of the largest in the world. Something you ship this month will run inside a Fortune 500 company and a 50-person startup in the same week, and you will hear from both.

 

The constraints make you better. Plane runs in our cloud, in customers' clouds, and on machines that will never touch the internet. Much of the work happens in the open, where the issues, the fixes, and the roadmap conversations are public. Building software that survives all of that is harder than building an ordinary SaaS product, and it is a better education than most companies can offer.

 

The people-and-agents future is being built here, in production. We think humans and AI agents will share one system of action for work. We are building that system now, for customers who already depend on it, and you will work on that problem directly whatever your role.

 

Your name is on the work. The teams are deeply connected enough that credit and responsibility both find you fast. That is some pressure. Mostly it is the fun part.

If that sounds like your kind of place, we would like to meet you.

Position Summary:

15+ years of progressive software engineering experience, including significant leadership experience within complex technology organizations.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.
Demonstrated success partnering with Product Management and executive stakeholders to define strategy, prioritize investments, and deliver business outcomes.
Experience defining and implementing software engineering best practices across the full software development lifecycle.
Strong track record of organizational leadership, including coaching leaders, driving change, and building high-performing teams.
Experience delivering large-scale cloud-based solutions using Azure, AWS, and/or Google Cloud Platform.
Familiarity with modern AI technologies, with preference given to candidates who have successfully built and scaled AI-enabled products or platforms.
Strong technical architecture background with the ability to evaluate trade-offs and guide strategic technology decisions.
Demonstrated ability to influence across engineering, product, sales, customer success, and executive teams.
Excellent communication, problem-solving, organizational, and stakeholder management skills.
Strong sense of ownership, urgency, accountability, and commitment to delivering results.

ABOUT POSH

We are all social creatures, but the dominant “social” companies today have evolved into digital loneliness machines, driving isolation, anxiety, and mental health challenges around the world.

Human connection is lost. Posh is a beacon guiding us back.

Posh enables anyone to build an IRL community based on shared interests, while connecting consumers with the communities of people just like them. Founded by event organizers who were frustrated with the growing loneliness epidemic and the tools available to build their own event brand, we’ve built the ultimate platform for launching, monetizing, and finding IRL communities of people just like you. In just 6 years, Posh has grown to a team of 70, expanded to 10M+ users, secured $70m in venture funding, and facilitated over $400M in transactions.





ABOUT THE ROLE

Posh's Affiliate Program is made up of organizers, promoters and campus directors who refer other organizers to Posh and earn on what those organizers go on to sell. Thousands of affiliates have signed up, and hundreds more join every month.

As Junior Affiliate Manager, you'll be their main point of contact. You'll welcome new affiliates, stay in touch with the ones already in the program, connect their referrals with our sales team (we call it Partnerships), bring people to our events, and find new affiliates and organizers to bring onto Posh.

You'll report to Ty Scearce, Affiliate Manager, and work in person at our SoHo office five days a week, with some evening events. It's a role for someone who'd rather pick up the phone than send another email, with room to grow into an Affiliate Manager or Account Executive role as the program scales.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Talk to affiliates every day. Work a daily call list by phone, text and DM.

 - Onboard new affiliates. Welcome new affiliates, walk them through the program, and host our affiliate webinar once you're ready.

 - Stay in touch. Check in with affiliates already in the program and help them keep referring.

 - Connect referrals with Partnerships. Make introductions, book demos with our Account Executives, and keep affiliates updated.

 - Find new people. Prospect new affiliates and organizers through Instagram DMs, research and cold outreach, and pass qualified organizers to Partnerships.

 - Fill the room. Drive RSVPs for our city events and webinars, work the door in NYC, and follow up with attendees.

 - Keep the CRM clean. Log every conversation in HubSpot the same day and share what you're hearing with the team.


ABOUT YOU

 - 1-2 years in a role measured on conversations: SDR/BDR, inside sales, recruiting, campus rep, promoter, or you sold tickets and ran events in college.

 - Comfortable on the phone. A "no" doesn't slow you down, and you can get a stranger talking in 30 seconds.

 - Fluent in texts, WhatsApp and Instagram DMs, where organizers and promoters actually live.

 - Competitive and coachable. You want a scoreboard and feedback on your calls.

 - Organized enough to manage hundreds of relationships. We'll teach you the tools.

 - Comfortable with data and AI tools. You'll pull your own numbers and prep your calls with Claude.

 - Connected to nightlife, culture, campus or creator communities.


NICE TO HAVES

 - You've thrown, promoted or worked events, or run a campus org.

 - Experience with HubSpot or another CRM.

 - Startup experience.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We’re hiring a Data Scientist for Sales and CS at PostHog to join a small team that works out which accounts are about to grow, before the growth shows up on an invoice. The holy grail is the cold start: patterns that carry over to companies who aren't using PostHog yet, where we have no usage signals at all.

This is a greenfield, quantitative role at PostHog - you’ll need engineering chops, statistical judgment, but also a keen commercial sense and an interest in working with usage time-series data. Perhaps you’re a former technical founder who did a lot of sales calls and knows how annoying it is to not have the right data at your fingertips. Or maybe a quantitative data scientist who has worked closely with sales teams, and likes to see a direct correlation between their work and making the line go up. Or a software engineer who has built data pipelines or internal tools for go-to-market teams, and wants to own the models as well as the systems that feed them. We’re happy to consider a range of profiles for this role!




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Own and maintain the pipelines behind our daily account snapshots, and use them to find leading indicators of growth: what an account looks like 30, 60, and 90 days before it expands.

 - Engineer signals from usage, engagement, and firmographic time series, then stack them into scores that Sales, CS, and Onboarding act on.

 - Backtest everything point-in-time, so we know a signal would have worked before anyone acts on it.

 - Build systems that proactively flag expansion opportunities (free → paid, cross-sell, upsell), and get them in front of reps inside the tools they already use.

 - Train, ship, and monitor models that predict growth, so we stop finding out after the fact.

 - Measure whether acting on a signal changed the outcome, and kill the signals that don’t work.

Decide what to snapshot next, flag where the history can't be trusted, and document religiously so others can build on your work.

Example projects:

 - Growth benchmarks by cohort: what a normal trajectory looks like for an account of a given size, segment, and product mix, so the outliers stand out.

 - Signal stacking: measure each new signal's lift over the ones we already have.

 - Account-level usage and revenue forecasts, with uncertainty we can trust.

 - Smarter segmentation for cross-sell and retention plays (resurface leads and accounts when their trajectory changes).

 - A lookalike model for prospects, trained on what our best customers looked like from the outside before they signed up.

 - Holdout tests that separate "this signal predicts growth" from "acting on this signal causes growth".




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Strong data analysis skills. You've turned messy, real-world business data into findings people acted on.

 - You have hands-on experience with time-series data and forecasting: panels across many accounts, sparse and irregular series, seasonality. You know the ways the data lies, and you can tell a good forecast from a lucky one.

 - You write production-quality Python and SQL.

 - You've taken a model or analysis out of the notebook and into something people use every day, including the pipelines and services around it.

 - Strong commercial focus - you really care about having an impact on revenue.

 - You have started a project from scratch. You might have led a project, been a founder previously, or built an impressive side project.

Nice to have

 - Prior experience with scoring or forecasting for revenue teams: lead scoring, propensity, churn, or expansion models, ideally at a product-led or usage-based company.

 - Experience with causal inference or experiment design.

 - Data engineering experience: you've built and run scheduled pipelines and warehouse models that other teams depend on.

 - Full-stack engineering experience, so you can build the tool that puts your signal in front of a salesperson.

 - You don’t have to be a Salesforce developer, but experience coding in Salesforce would definitely help.

Company Overview:

We are building Protege to solve the biggest unmet need in AI — getting access to the right training data. The process today is time intensive, incredibly expensive, and often ends in failure. The Protege platform facilitates the secure, efficient, and privacy-centric exchange of AI training data.

Solving AI’s data problem is a generational opportunity. We’re backed by world-class investors and already powering partnerships with some of the most ambitious teams in AI. The company that succeeds will be one of the largest in AI — and in tech.

We’re a lean, fast-moving, high-trust team of builders who are obsessed with velocity and impact. Our culture is built for people who thrive on ambiguity, own outcomes, and want to shape the future of data and AI.



The role

AI in healthcare advances safely if people can trust it. Right now, it’s being deployed faster than anyone can check how well it actually works. We’re solving that problem by building out our Assessments team, which runs independent evaluations on real patient records. Those records go beyond text and includes scans, pathology slides, and audio. We’re looking for the Founding Evaluation Engineer to join that team.

Working with our researchers, engineers, and customers, you’ll build the evals which include the tasks, the graders, and the auditors for the graders. In healthcare, the right answer isn’t always clear and can be hard to verify. Doctors disagree, a diagnosis can take months to confirm, and models are starting to match the experts we’d ask to grade them. If you care deeply about how to score a model when the answer is hard to verify, or when the model may be better than the people grading it, you’re the right fit.

What you'll do

 - Build the eval platform. You’ll build the platform so that our researchers’ tasks, graders, and auditors can plug in once and run against any model.

 - Build the graders. Our researchers design the graders but you own the implementation and the tooling to make eval design easier.

 - Stand up each new customer’s eval. Their models or AI applications are scored on tasks that fit their product.

 - Score what is hard to verify. Partner with our researchers to build scoring for cases where doctors disagree or the answer only shows up later.

 - Audit the grader. Work with our researchers to find cases where the graders were wrong and build guardrails against that.

What success looks like

 - 30 days: Learned how our assessments run end to end, met our researchers and first customers, shipped first improvements to our graders and a first customer evaluation run.

 - 60 days: Owning the harness and graders end to end for every active customer, ensuring that every grader is tested before it scores.

 - 90 days: A new benchmark goes from researcher design to first scored run in 2 days, and every score ships with a measured grader error rate.

What you'll bring

 - You’ve built evals end to end: dataset, harness, grader and report.

 - You’ve evaluated models on tasks with no single right answer.

 - You’ve caught a misleading result, such as leaked answers, a bad answer key, or a metric that hid a failure.

 - You’ve built an eval harness that other people ran.

 - Nice to have: you’ve built an automated grader and measured how often it was wrong.

 - Nice to have: you’ve worked with doctors or other experts to write rubrics or labels.

 - Nice to have: you’ve built evals with multi-modal data.
