The role

Protege is hiring a Staff Software Engineer to build and operate the transformation layer of our data platform — the pipelines that take ingested, sensitive source data and turn it into de-identified, delivery-ready datasets. This is a hands-on, data-engineering-oriented software role with end-to-end ownership of the jobs that transform, protect, and package data at scale.

Protege connects organizations that hold high-value data with the AI builders who need it. Much of that data is regulated healthcare data. Before any of it reaches a customer, it passes through a transformation pipeline that de-identifies it to a defensible standard, preserves its analytical value, and packages it for delivery. The quality, correctness, and auditability of that pipeline is what makes the exchange possible.

You’ll work on a small team alongside a senior engineer who owns much of today’s transform logic, and you’ll partner closely with privacy, solutions, and ingestion teams. The work spans distributed Spark jobs, configuration-driven transform frameworks, free-text processing, and the operational discipline required when the input is privacy-protected. This role is ideal for engineers who like precise, high-stakes data work, want deep ownership of a critical system, and enjoy turning one-off requests into reusable, well-tested capabilities.

What you'll do

 - Build and extend the de-identification transform framework. Extend Protege’s capabilities by building composable transform chains, and developing multi-modal processes.

 - Maintain the boundary between protected and de-identified data. You own the guards between protected and de-identified data, extend them as new workflows need to cross the boundary, and make sure every crossing stays validated and auditable.

 - Develop agentic workflows in the pipeline. You bring ideas for where agents and models fit in our transformation layer and build them into production with the evaluation and guardrails PHI requires.

 - Make jobs self-serve for solutions engineers. Clear interfaces, sensible defaults, and runbooks let non-owners run transforms correctly without escalating to the team.

 - Turn recurring one-off requests into reusable capabilities. Deal-specific transform or packaging work becomes a job mode, shared utility, or config option rather than a fork.

What success looks like

 - 30 days: Mapped the flow from ingestion through de-identification to delivery, met the privacy, solutions, ingestion, and catalog partners, and shipped an update to the transform pipeline that adds a capability or makes an existing job easier to run.

 - 60 days: Created a new transform from a privacy or solutions request, including its config, tests, documentation, and a measured quality check, and seen it run on real provider data.

 - 90 days: Owning the transform pipeline end to end, including its configs, operations, and support; proposing and developing improvements to its reliability, usability, or development speed, with at least one in production.

What you'll bring

 - You have written Python libraries or frameworks that other engineers depend on, with tests and documentation.

 - You have shipped data pipelines on AWS and made the storage, compute, and access-control decisions yourself.

 - You have turned a vague data request into a precise, tested implementation.

 - You have built internal tools that serve a range of end-users.

 - Nice to have: hands-on Databricks experience (Delta tables, Unity Catalog or a comparable governance layer).

 - Nice to have: text processing at scale (regex or NLP pipelines), workflow orchestration (Dagster, Airflow), or config-driven data frameworks.

 2. Conversation with the hiring manager (45 min)

 3. Technical Interview (60 min)

 4. Work Trial (4 hrs)

Reap is a global financial technology company headquartered in Hong Kong with employees across multiple countries. We enable financial connectivity and access for businesses worldwide by combining traditional finance with stablecoins for efficient money movement.



Through our stablecoin-powered corporate cards, payments, and expense management tools, we streamline financial operations and help businesses scale. Our APIs enable businesses to integrate stablecoin-enabled finance into their own products and services—from issuing Visa cards to facilitating cross-border payments.



Backed by leading investors including Acorn Pacific, Index Ventures and HashKey Capital, Reap is building the future of borderless, stablecoin-enabled finance.

Reap is building financial infrastructure for modern businesses. Our products help companies issue cards, move money, manage payments, and scale financial operations across markets.



As our products and client base grow, the journey from sales to activation is becoming more technical and more important. We are looking for a Senior Solution Engineer who can help clients go from “interested” to “live and successful” faster, with the right technical guidance along the way.






THE TEAM

The Financial Crime Operations (FCO) team protects customers and the platform by preventing, detecting, and responding to financial crime across fiat and crypto rails. As Reap deepens its card network integrations and scales its Web3 infrastructure, FCO is moving from manual workflows towards automated, rules-based monitoring. The team works closely with Compliance (FCC), Product, Engineering, and Payment Operations to meet regulatory and scheme obligations while protecting the client experience.

Reap values ownership, speaking up, starting with the customer, and moving quickly without cutting corners. It offers an inclusive global team, annual leave and public holidays, a health insurance budget, flexible remote work options, a home office equipment budget, and a Corporate Reap Card for work expenses without out-of-pocket spending.




 


THE OPPORTUNITY

Every client relationship at Reap runs through Operations, from first application to final exit. Reporting to the Head of Operations, you’ll own that journey end to end and make onboarding and client lifecycle operations fast, consistent, and scalable across regions.

This is a leadership role beyond managing a queue. You’ll lead the onboarding team, run the compliance services Reap sells to clients, shape the tools the team uses, and set global operating standards.

 - Own KYB and onboarding outcomes across product lines, balancing speed, quality, risk, and client experience. Work with commercial teams to get the right clients live sooner.

 - Run and scale client-facing compliance services as reliable, well-defined products, adapting them as Reap enters new products, markets, and partnerships.

 - Represent the business in decisions about onboarding technology, setting requirements for tools and vendors. Use automation and AI so the team can focus on judgment rather than manual checks.

 - Set consistent onboarding and lifecycle standards across regions. Build the quality, measurement, and governance processes needed to scale and remain audit-ready.

 - Lead and grow the team directly, and set standards for regional operations leads through a dotted-line relationship. Compliance sets the policy guardrails; you decide how Operations meets them.


Success means first-line quality assurance is operating across the highest-risk workflows; regional teams follow one playbook and keep backlogs within SLA; client-facing compliance services have published SLAs, triage models, and capacity plans; and every workflow has an SOP and a named backup. The team should be able to run without depending on you for every decision.

 
 


WHAT YOU BRING

 - At least eight years in client or merchant onboarding, KYB, or client lifecycle operations at a payments company, card issuer, EMI, SaaS platform, or crypto business.

 - At least two years leading a team against SLAs, ideally across more than one region.

 - Deep KYB expertise, including complex ownership structures and platform or B2B2B models, such as sub-client onboarding and reliance versus non-reliance.

 - A record of building operations from scratch, including playbooks, SLAs, capacity models, and quality assurance frameworks that stood up to audit.

 - Experience defining requirements for internal tools, such as identity verification or case management, with Product and Engineering.

 - The ability to lead through influence and get regional teams to adopt standards without managing them directly.

 - Commercial judgment: you recognise onboarding speed as a growth lever and know how to say yes safely.


You take ownership of outcomes, speak up, and work well in ambiguity. You enjoy turning messy processes into scalable operations while keeping the customer in view.

 
 


NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience running a compliance service sold to clients.

 - Exposure to card scheme requirements.

 - Hands-on experience with automation or AI tools in operations workflows.

 3. Get them fully onboarded. Make sure they actually switch banks and start using everything Rho can do, not just open an account.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are hiring one Head of Product who is personally accountable for the quality, monetization and retention of a consumer product in the Utility niche, used by millions of people and monetized through a web-to-web subscription trial.

This is a hands-on builder role, not a coordination role. You will use Claude and Claude Code daily to research, prototype, spec, test and sometimes ship product yourself. You will own the roadmap, the standard of what reaches production, and the team that delivers it.

We are resetting how we build. The goal is fewer things shipped properly, not more things shipped fast: every funnel works, every release is tested, and every feature earns its place with data. Quality is the first job; ARPU and retention growth follow from it.



Key responsibilities



Quality and delivery (the first accountability)

• Own the quality bar for everything in production. If a funnel is broken or a release regresses, it is your problem and you fix the process, not only the bug.

• Run the delivery rhythm: daily stand-ups with engineering and QA, sprint planning, release go/no-go. Limit work in progress. No new feature starts while a critical bug is open.

• Write specs engineers can build from without guessing: user story, edge cases, analytics events, acceptance criteria and test cases. Review what ships against them.

• Work with QA to build regression coverage for the revenue-critical journeys and to monitor them in production.

• Define what “done” means: tested, instrumented, flagged, rolled out in stages and watched after release.



Hands-on building with AI

• Use Claude and Claude Code every day to research, analyze data, prototype flows, write specs and reproduce bugs. You can build a working prototype or a small fix yourself instead of waiting for a ticket.

• Judge AI output critically. You know the difference between a demo and something good enough to be number one in the niche, and you hold the team to it.

• Set the AI-first working standards for the product team: shared prompts, Claude Code conventions, review practices and design-to-code workflow.



Team building

• Hire and lead the product team around you, for example product managers, QA and design, as the scope requires. Every hire must work fluently with AI tools.

• Define roles, hiring bar and onboarding. Coach people, give direct feedback and remove people-process blockers.



Product strategy and roadmap

• Own one prioritized roadmap, built from user research, funnel data and competitor analysis. Say no to things that do not move quality, conversion or retention.

• Keep a living competitor teardown (flows, pricing, paywalls, onboarding, features) and use it to set the quality benchmark.

• Partner with the Managing Director on priorities and trade-offs, and report progress on a fixed cadence.



Monetization and ARPU

• Own D7 and D30 ARPU and trial-to-paid conversion. Run pricing, packaging and paywall experiments end to end: hypothesis, design, sample size, rollout, read-out.

• Find untapped revenue (plans, upsells, add-ons, cross-tool usage) and rank by impact.



Retention and engagement

• Own retention and churn targets. Use cohort analysis to find drop-off and friction, then fix them with onboarding, engagement loops and a clean cancellation and support experience.



Research and data

• Run continuous discovery with real users: interviews, session replays, support tickets, reviews.

• Define product metrics, keep the tracking plan accurate and make decisions from data, not opinion.



Growth collaboration

• Work with CRO and marketing so landing pages, messaging and onboarding match what the product delivers, and plan launches together.



Must-have experience



• Product leadership: 5+ years in product for D2C subscription products (web-to-web, web-to-app), including 2+ years as a senior or lead PM, ideally as the single accountable owner of one product.

• Quality track record: You can show a product you took from buggy or unstable to reliable. You can explain the release process, QA setup and metrics you introduced, and what changed.

• Builder skills: You build things yourself. Show us a prototype, internal tool or shipped feature made with Claude Code or similar, and explain how you directed the AI and checked its output.

• Daily AI workflow: Claude or an equivalent is part of how you research, analyze, spec and prototype every day, not an occasional helper.

• Technical fluency: You write precise requirements, join architecture and trade-off discussions, read code well enough to review a pull request and reproduce a bug.

• Monetization and retention: Measurable growth in ARPU and retention, including pricing, paywall or packaging experiments you ran end to end.

• Funnels and UX: Deep understanding of high-converting consumer journeys (onboarding, paywall, checkout, cancel) and the discipline to test every step.

• Analytics and experimentation: Hands-on with Mixpanel (or similar) and SQL or BI tools. You design and read A/B tests and manage feature flags and staged rollouts.

• Research and competitor analysis: A repeatable method for user discovery and for benchmarking competitors, with examples of decisions it changed.

• Team building: Experience hiring and leading product, QA or design people, ideally in an AI-first way of working.



Nice to have

• Experience with utility or productivity consumer products, or with high-traffic SEO-driven products.

• Exposure to paid acquisition (Meta Ads, Google Ads) and how traffic quality affects trial conversion and retention.

• Experience with payments, billing, trials and cancellation flows, including refund and chargeback reduction.

• Hands-on experience with test automation (Playwright, Cypress) or session-replay and error-monitoring tools.

• Experience with Claude Design or similar AI design tools for fast UI iteration.



Leadership attributes

• Radical ownership: You treat the product as your own. A bug in production or a broken funnel bothers you more than a missed feature date.

• Quality obsession: You care about the details of UX, specs and outcomes, and you push back,

including on leadership, when something is not good enough to ship.

• Disciplined pace: You know speed without quality is slower. You limit work in progress, say no, and sequence work so it lands finished.

• Structured and analytical: You turn ambiguous problems into hypotheses and tests, and your

conclusions rest on data.

• Builder mindset: You prefer to prototype, test and show over writing long documents.

• Clear communicator: You explain complex ideas simply to non-technical stakeholders and give engineers precise technical context.

• Talent magnet: You attract and grow strong people, and you set a bar others rise to.



This role is not for you if

• You prefer to manage a backlog and hand work to others rather than get hands-on with the product and the AI tools.

• You measure yourself by features shipped rather than by funnels that work and revenue retained.

• You need a large team of project managers, researchers and designers around you to function from day one.

• You are not comfortable owning a production problem and its root cause in public.

About the role:

Browsers are steadily closing the door on how device identity has worked on the web. Sardine's Device Intelligence & Behavior Biometrics team builds the signals that tell genuine users apart from fraudsters, bots, and AI agents, and we need an engineer to own how our Web SDK identifies devices reliably across Safari, Firefox, Chrome, Brave, and in-app WebViews, and how it reaches the browser as a true first party.

You will own the Web SDK, its client-side identity storage, and the CDN reverse proxy integrations that sit in our customers' traffic. This is a production engineering role with a strong investigative side: much of the work starts with understanding exactly how a browser treats a cookie, a request, or a domain, and ends with shipping a change that keeps working for thousands of end users.



What You Will Do

 - Lead our move to privacy-resilient first-party integrations: opt-in CHIPS partitioned cookies, true first-party cookie flows, and in-band CDN reverse proxy integrations.

 - Build and extend reverse proxy integrations across CDNs and origin setups (Cloudflare, AWS Lambda@Edge / CloudFront, Fastly, Akamai, F5, NGINX), including per-customer randomized paths for SDK loading and event ingestion.

 - Modernize the SDK's client-side identity storage layer, and design graceful degradation when persistence is limited.

 - Design device identity handoff between our native mobile SDKs and in-app WebViews, resistant to spoofing and abuse.

 - Instrument and measure device identifier longevity and churn by browser, version, and integration mode, and alert on regressions.

 - Track browser privacy changes (ITP, ETP / dFPI, CHIPS, Storage Access API, tracker lists) ahead of release, and turn them into SDK and integration decisions.

 - Own the performance, bundle size, and reliability of an SDK that runs on login, signup, and payment flows of fintechs and enterprises.

 - Work with backend (Go), mobile, dashboard, and customer success teams to roll out changes across existing customers without breaking installs.



What We're Looking For

 - 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with at least 3 years building production JavaScript / TypeScript that runs in the browser.

 - Strong TypeScript / JavaScript and deep knowledge of browser APIs, cross-browser differences, and WebView behavior.

 - Deep, practical knowledge of cookie and storage behavior across browsers: SameSite, partitioning, CHIPS, ITP / ETP, CNAME cloaking detection, and eviction rules.

 - Experience shipping and maintaining a third-party JavaScript SDK or library that runs on other companies' sites.

 - Experience building or operating reverse proxies or edge functions in production.

 - Solid web networking fundamentals: HTTP, CORS, cookies, DNS, TLS, caching, CDNs.

 - Good judgment on effort, risk, and migration paths in systems with many external integrators.

 - Clear written and verbal communication of trade-offs to engineering, product, and customer-facing teams.

 - Experience with at least one popular web framework or library, such as React, Angular, Vue.js, Next.js, or Svelte. Experience with multiple frameworks is a plus.

 - Experience with modern JavaScript development tools and build systems, including Node.js, npm, Babel, and bundlers such as Webpack, Vite, or Rollup. Familiarity with one or more of these tools is preferred.



Nice to Have

 - Background in fraud prevention, bot detection, device fingerprinting, or web security.

 - Go experience.

 - Experience with JavaScript obfuscation, anti-tampering, or reverse engineering minified code.

 - Familiarity with automation frameworks (Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium) and how they differ from real browsers.

This is primarily a regulatory and operations liaison role, with a meaningful credentialing and training component. You will partner closely with our Maritime Operations leadership, our Head of Regulatory & Litigation, our General Counsel, and our government affairs and policy teams to shape the regulatory and operational environment in which Saronic's uncrewed vessels are built, tested, and deployed.

This is not a legal or traditional compliance role. 📌 About the Role

Static ads are driving a bigger share of Scribe’s growth every month, and we’re looking for the person to lead that charge.

As our first Performance Creative Designer, you'll own every static ad Scribe runs: how it looks, how it's built and how it performs. You’ll take briefs from our creative strategists and demand generation team and level them up with your own taste and point of view, using AI to ship at a pace most teams can’t touch. An idea you have on Thursday can be in market by Monday.

You won’t be a ticket-taker who ships ads into the void and never finds out how they performed. You’ll sit in a closed loop with the media buyers who spend the money and the analysts who measure it, so you’ll know within days which of your ads became top performers and what revenue they drove. You'll have the freedom to build the system behind it all and make our static ads ridiculously good, directly driving business outcomes.

You’ll be working alongside one of the best performance creative teams anywhere, with the resources and the room to raise the bar on what world-class static creative looks like.



✨ You could be a great fit if:

 - You keep a swipe file of ads that stopped your scroll, and you have an opinion on why each one works.

 - You've watched an "ugly" ad beat the pretty one and felt vindicated (or humbled, both count).

 - You get a little too excited about CTR and the ads that take all the spend.

 - You're no order-taker. You get handed a brief and you make it better.

 - You're a tastemaker. You have a strong point of view on what “great” looks like, and you hold the bar there. You use AI every day to make you faster not to replace your taste.

 - When someone says "can you just resize this?", you've already built the AI-powered workflow that churns out six sizes and three variations worth testing.

If you read any of those ☝️ and said "that's me", we'd love to hear from you!



⚒️ What you'll do:

 - Own Scribe's performance statics end to end. Turn briefs into ads for Meta, LinkedIn and whatever channel we test next, for self-serve and enterprise audiences, in 24-48 hours.

 - Turn briefs into winners. Partner with our creative strategists and Demand Generation team to sharpen briefs and push back when something won’t work. Then make them better: bring your own taste and vision, and use what the data says works to level up every creative you ship.

 - Build the system, not just the assets. Create Figma-native templates, variation frameworks and an AI-powered production workflow so volume scales without quality dropping.

 - Run the external bench. Brief, QA and direct contractors and agencies as an extension of your hands, and decide when to burst up or down. You hold the bar.

 - Know what wins, and why. Dig into creative performance with the team, figure out what made the winners win, and bake those learnings into the next round. You own static win rate and velocity.
   
   

🔍 What we're looking for:

 - 4-6+ years designing performance or paid social creative (statics especially) at a D2C, consumer or high-growth B2B/PLG company, with a portfolio that shows off that work.

 - Deep fluency in the anatomy of paid ad creative: hooks, hierarchy, formats, variations, and how to explain a win in performance terms.

 - Expert-level at Figma. You build templates and variation systems that let you ship at volume without losing quality.

 - You have a tastemaker’s eye for AI output. You know the tools inside out, what they’re great at, where they produce slop, and when your own hands and eye need to take over.

 - You thrive at high pace — it energizes you. 24-48 hour turnarounds, competing requests from multiple teams, and quality that never slips.

 - You love spending a week perfecting one beautiful piece. At Scribe, five testable ads beat one perfect one, and we learn from every result.

 - Your passion is brand identity or product UI. This seat is performance design, and that's a different craft.

 - You'd prefer to hand off the "did it work?" conversation. You'll be in the numbers with us.

About Sesame

Sesame believes in a future where computers are lifelike - with the ability to see, hear, and collaborate with us in ways that feel natural and human. With this vision, we're designing a new kind of computer, focused on making voice agents part of our daily lives. Our team brings together founders from Oculus and Ubiquity6, alongside proven leaders from Meta, Google, and Apple, with deep expertise spanning hardware and software. Join us in shaping a future where computers truly come alive.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Sesame trains and serves its own speech and conversational models. Our goal for ML infrastructure is to keep pushing back the limits on what the ML team can do: train what they want at the scale they want, and get it into production, without the platform getting in the way. GPUs are always in high demand, our data keeps growing, and the models we serve have to respond in real time, so getting there will take a lot of clever engineering. We also want the tools to be world class. When someone uses the platform, we want them to notice how well it was built.

We're looking for an infrastructure engineer to design and build the systems that make that possible, from the clusters we train on to the platform we serve from. Most of the hard problems today are on the training side, so that's where you'd start, but the role covers serving too. Some of our capacity comes with a managed platform around it. The rest is plain Kubernetes, where we have to create that platform layer ourselves. We want someone with strong opinions about how to do that and the ability to do it. It's a broad role, and you'd have a lot of say in the direction we take.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Drive the strategy for our GPU infrastructure across training and serving: clusters, scheduling, storage, and the tooling the ML team uses every day

 - Design and build the platform the ML team runs on. You decide the architecture and you write the software

 - Get more out of scarce GPUs. Build the scheduling policy that decides which jobs run when there isn't room for all of them, and make interrupted jobs pick up where they left off

 - Decide where training data and checkpoints are stored and how they get to the GPUs. Our datasets are large enough that moving them around can get very expensive

 - Pick the right technology and stand behind it. If self-hosting a parallel filesystem is the best answer because the cloud's built-in storage isn't fast enough, make that case with numbers and carry it through

 - Automate everything you can, especially with agents. Build closed-loop solutions that cut off toil at the source

 - Find the bottleneck in a slow training run, whichever layer it's in: checkpoint writes, data loading, the network, one bad node. Fix it with data

 - Go where the problem is. One quarter that's the training scheduler, the next it's storage, data, or serving

 - Work with the ML team every day. You're the link between what researchers need and what the software and infrastructure teams build
   
   


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Infrastructure is what you do. You care about scale, reliability, and performance, and you judge your work by how fast the ML team can move

 - 8+ years of software engineering experience, with significant time in infrastructure, platform, or ML systems roles.

 - You've designed and built infrastructure other engineers ran their work on: a scheduler, a compute or storage platform, a cluster control plane. You made the design decisions and wrote the code, and you can name a decision you'd undo if you built it again

 - You're really good at Kubernetes or a similar compute platform, past the point of using it. You've written controllers or operators, extended a scheduler, or debugged your way into the internals

 - You've worked hands-on with GPUs. You can debug them, and you can explain why GPU infrastructure is different from everything else you've run. That experience can come from training, serving, or somewhere else

 - You know how large-scale multi-node training jobs behave, how they fail, and what preemption does to them

 - You have strong storage fundamentals. You can walk through a real decision where you chose block, object, or a parallel filesystem for a workload, with the throughput and cost numbers behind it

 - You can say when Kubernetes, Ray, or Slurm is the right base for training and for serving, from having used them

 - You explain complicated things clearly to people who don't share your background
   
   


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Model serving infrastructure at scale (vLLM, Triton, KServe, or similar)

 - You've built or run a shared training cluster with a batch scheduler (Volcano, Kueue, Slurm, or similar)

 - You've built or worked on a GPU cloud or an internal training platform at a company that trains its own models

 - You've run a parallel filesystem in production (Weka, Lustre, VAST, GPFS)

 - High-performance networking for training: RDMA over InfiniBand or RoCE, and NCCL

 - Enough PyTorch distributed training to debug a job alongside the researcher who wrote it

 - GCP and GKE

 - You've been a tech lead and still write code every day

 - You've gone all in on agentic coding and it shows in how you work

What you'll do:

 - Maintain the aircraft electrical power budget, load analysis, and power distribution, and assess the impact of every change on margins and endurance.

 - Design new PCBAs and update existing avionics, power, and ground support electronics: schematic capture, layout review, simulation, analysis, verification, and release to production.

 - Own component selection and BOM health, balancing performance, reliability, derating, cost, lead time, lifecycle, and compliance.

 - Lead root cause analysis and corrective action for electrical reliability, production, and field issues that cross board and subsystem boundaries.

 - Support manufacturing with DFM/DFT, first article inspection, line bring-up, and production transfers to new sites or suppliers.

 - Wear multiple hats—integrator, board designer, component engineer, test engineer, and problem solver—depending on what the project needs.

 - Work cross-functionally with mechanical, firmware, software, flight test, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and program teams to move fast without dropping rigor.

 - Travel to manufacturing sites, suppliers, test ranges, and customer locations (domestic and international) of up to 20%.

 - Present work in design reviews and communicate trade-offs and whole-aircraft impacts clearly to engineering and program leadership.

What Success Looks Like:

 - Every proposed change comes with a clear, fast assessment of its electrical impact on the whole aircraft.

 - Power, thermal, and EMI/EMC margins are known, tracked, and protected.

 - PCBAs and BOMs are compliant, buildable, and documented, and release to production on aggressive timelines.

 - Measurably reduce electrical production and field issues.

 - Make design decisions that hold up downstream and know when to escalate technical risk.

Required qualifications:

 - Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering; or equivalent work experience.

 - 5+ years of electrical engineering experience spanning PCBA design, component selection, integration, and test, including ownership of hardware through production release.

 - Experience integrating electrical subsystems at the vehicle or platform level, including power distribution, harnessing, grounding, and EMI/EMC.

 - Strong working knowledge of hardware compliance requirements (e.g., material restrictions, EMC, environmental qualification, export controls) and how to document and demonstrate compliance.

 - Solid understanding of component derating, reliability, lifecycle, and how part choices affect manufacturing and supply.

 - Experience planning and executing electrical and environmental qualification testing and interpreting the results.

 - Hands-on manufacturing experience, including DFM/DFT, working with contract manufacturers, and supporting production builds.

 - Experience with both new product development and modifying or improving fielded products.

 - Proficiency with a production ECAD tool such as Altium, Cadence/OrCAD/Allegro, or Mentor/Xpedition.

 - Comfortable working in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment with shifting priorities and a small team.

 - Strong understanding of how engineering decisions impact manufacturing, test, supply chain, cost, and field support downstream.

 - Ability and willingness to travel up to 20%, including international travel.

 - Demonstrated track record of extreme ownership, working hard, and delivering outstanding outcomes.

Preferred qualifications:

 - Prior experience on a special projects, rapid prototyping, skunkworks, or startup-style hardware team.

 - Experience integrating payloads, radios, or modifications on UAS, airborne, aerospace, space, or defense platforms.

 - Familiarity with test standards such as MIL-STD-810, MIL-STD-461, MIL-STD-704, or RTCA DO-160.

 - Familiarity with workmanship standards such as IPC-A-610 and J-STD-001 (Class 3).

 - Experience with component data and lifecycle tools such as SiliconExpert, Z2Data, or Accuris (IHS).

 - Experience with power systems, embedded systems, or RF interfaces.

 - Experience with configuration management, engineering change processes, and AS9100 quality systems.

JOB DESCRIPTION

Shield AI is seeking a Staff Platform Engineer to help design and implement the internal technology platforms that power our engineering, autonomy, and enterprise operations environments.

In this highly technical individual contributor role, you will serve as a senior technical expert responsible for designing and evolving scalable, secure, and highly automated platform infrastructure spanning cloud, on-premise, and hybrid environments. You will work closely with engineering, security, and infrastructure teams to establish platform architecture, develop paved paths for developers, and implement automation that improves reliability, security, and development productivity across engineering teams.

This role is ideal for an experienced platform engineer who thrives at the intersection of systems architecture, automation, and developer enablement, and who enjoys building the foundational systems that allow engineering organizations to move quickly and safely.

This position may be based in San Diego, CA; Dallas, TX; Washington, D.C.; or other Shield AI locations.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

Platform Architecture & Engineering

 - Build and evolve scalable internal platform infrastructure supporting engineering workloads across public cloud, private cloud, and on-prem environments.

 - Design and implement platform capabilities that enable standardized, secure, and repeatable application deployment of applications and services.

 - Develop and maintain infrastructure-as-code frameworks and reusable platform modules to accelerate engineering productivity.

 - Establish and evolve “paved path” platform patterns that simplify secure software delivery for engineering teams.

Automation & Developer Enablement

 - Build automation and developer tooling that improves software delivery and engineering productivity.

 - Contribute to and improve CI/CD pipelines, artifact management, and developer platform tooling.

 - Collaborate with engineering teams to reduce operational friction and improve system observability, resilience, and reliability.

 - Develop internal tools, platform integrations, and automation frameworks that streamline engineering workflows across the organization.

Infrastructure & Systems Engineering

 - Design, implement, and operate highly available infrastructure platforms supporting mission-critical engineering systems.

 - Implement scalable platform solutions across cloud and on-prem environments including compute, networking, identity, and storage.

 - Partner with security teams to embed strong security controls, auditability, and compliance requirements into platform architectures.

 - Evaluate and introduce new technologies that improve system scalability, security, and operational efficiency.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - 8+ years of experience in platform engineering, DevOps, infrastructure engineering, or site reliability engineering roles supporting large-scale systems.

 - Deep hands-on experience designing, building and operating cloud or hybrid infrastructure platforms, including networking, identity, compute, and storage systems.

 - Strong expertise with Infrastructure as Code and automation frameworks (e.g., Terraform, Ansible, or similar).

 - Experience building or improving CI/CD pipelines, developer platform tooling, and automated deployment workflows.

 - Strong systems engineering background across Linux-based environments, distributed systems, and infrastructure automation using scripting or programming languages (Python, Go, Bash, PowerShell, etc.).

 - Demonstrated ability to understand, build, and own complex platform initiatives and collaborate across engineering and infrastructure teams.

 - Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence technical direction across multiple engineering teams.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience building or operating internal developer platforms (IDP) or engineering productivity platforms that support large-scale development environments.

 - Experience with Kubernetes and modern container platforms.

 - Experience deploying infrastructure across commercial and government cloud environments, including AWS and Azure.

 - Familiarity with DevSecOps practices and integrating security controls into automated infrastructure and CI/CD pipelines.

 - Experience implementing observability platforms, including centralized logging, monitoring, and distributed tracing for large-scale systems.

 - Experience working within defense, aerospace, or other regulated industries, including familiarity with frameworks such as NIST or FedRAMP.

About the role:

Shield AI is seeking a Staff Manufacturing Infrastructure Engineer to own the systems infrastructure for our new 400,000 sq ft manufacturing facility in the Seattle-Tacoma area, home to our newest flagship product. You will design, build, and operate the compute, virtualization, storage, and backup and recovery platforms that run the factory, support the site’s Active Directory services as part of Shield AI’s enterprise environment, and own the infrastructure behind manufacturing systems such as MES, ERP, PLM, quality, and test, from build-out and commissioning through ramp to high-rate production.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will set the systems architecture and standards for the site and partner with the Manufacturing Infrastructure team, including the manufacturing network team, as well as Manufacturing Engineering, Operations, Facilities, Cybersecurity, and Cloud Platform, to keep production running.

This position is based on site in the Seattle, Tacoma, or surrounding SeaTac, WA area.

What You’ll Do:

Architecture and Build

 - Own the end-to-end systems architecture for the facility: compute, virtualization, storage, and backup and recovery, plus site identity services integrated with the enterprise, sized for build-out, commissioning, and production ramp.

 - Support and operate site Active Directory services, including domain controllers, DNS, Group Policy, authentication, and replication, as an extension of Shield AI’s enterprise Active Directory and Entra ID environment, in partnership with the enterprise teams that own them.

 - Design and operate virtualization and Windows and Linux server platforms (for example VMware, Hyper-V, or equivalent) for production, engineering, and test workloads.

 - Design, administer, and optimize enterprise storage platforms (for example NetApp, Pure Storage, or Dell EMC), including capacity, performance, availability, replication, and lifecycle management.

 - Plan capacity and size infrastructure for the production ramp, new lines, and future site expansion.

 - Select vendors, develop BOMs, and drive procurement and delivery timelines for compute, storage, and backup platforms.

 - Manage infrastructure as code, with builds and configuration in Git and repeatable deployment patterns using Terraform, Ansible, PowerShell, Python, or similar tools.

 - Automate provisioning, patching, and compliance checks from day 0 through day 2 so the site can be rebuilt and replicated consistently for future lines and facilities.

Manufacturing Systems and Facility Readiness

 - Lead systems technology readiness from design through construction, commissioning, and production ramp, including cutover plans, acceptance testing, and handoff to operations.

 - Build and host the infrastructure for manufacturing systems such as MES, ERP and PLM integrations (including Teamcenter), quality, and test systems, in partnership with Manufacturing Engineering, controls teams, and equipment vendors.

 - Support servers and systems that sit alongside production, such as equipment-vendor and test-station servers, historians, and imaging, including patching and lifecycle rules for vendor-controlled systems, with Manufacturing Engineering and controls teams.

 - Design and deliver shop-floor and edge compute for production lines and test and inspection stations, including VDI and GPU-accelerated workloads where needed.

 - Lead the systems side of server room, MDF/IDF, and data center design reviews, including racks, power and cooling, capacity, hardware lifecycle management, and documentation, and coordinate with Facilities and contractors through construction and commissioning.

Operations, Security and Reliability

 - Operate site systems infrastructure to production-grade availability targets, and define uptime targets, change governance, and maintenance windows with Manufacturing Operations that fit production schedules.

 - Design, document, and test backup, replication, and disaster recovery for production systems, including RTO/RPO planning and DR exercises, in an environment where downtime affects output.

 - Build observability for servers, storage, backup, and capacity so issues are found before they affect production.

 - Serve as tier-3 escalation for production-impacting systems incidents; lead root-cause analysis and drive corrective actions.

 - Participate in on-call rotations, maintenance windows, and change management, supporting 24/7 production schedules.

 - Partner with Cybersecurity on hardening, patching, vulnerability management, and access controls aligned with NIST 800-171, CMMC, and ITAR requirements.

 - Work with the manufacturing network team on connectivity, segmentation, and dependencies, with the network team owning network architecture and devices and this role owning the systems that attach to them.

Leadership

 - Set systems standards, reference designs, and runbooks that can be reused for future lines and facilities.

 - Mentor engineers and technicians, review designs, and influence the roadmap across Manufacturing Infrastructure.

Required Qualifications:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

 - 8+ years of experience engineering and supporting enterprise infrastructure in production environments, with direct experience supporting a manufacturing or production environment.

 - Hands-on experience deploying and operating on-premises data center or server room infrastructure, including rack-level deployments, power and cooling, and hardware lifecycle management.

 - Strong experience supporting Microsoft Active Directory in an enterprise environment, including AD DS, Group Policy, DNS, authentication, and replication.

 - Strong experience with enterprise compute, virtualization, and storage platforms, such as VMware, Hyper-V, KVM, NetApp, Pure Storage, Dell EMC, or equivalent.

 - Strong Windows Server administration experience and working proficiency with Linux systems such as RHEL or Ubuntu.

 - Experience designing and implementing backup, replication, disaster recovery, and business continuity solutions, including RTO/RPO planning and testing.

 - Experience with infrastructure automation and configuration management using tools such as Terraform, Ansible, PowerShell, Python, or Bash.

 - Experience supporting hybrid infrastructure across on-premises environments and AWS and/or Azure.

 - Familiarity with manufacturing systems such as MES, ERP, PLM, or quality platforms, and with how production equipment and infrastructure connect.

 - Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical initiatives, establish engineering standards, troubleshoot ambiguous problems, and mentor other engineers.

 - Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work with technical and non-technical audiences.

 - Ability to travel occasionally to other Shield AI locations.

 - This position may require access to export-controlled information, and employment may be contingent on U.S. person status or export authorization.

Preferred Qualifications:

 - Experience building or commissioning a greenfield manufacturing, data center, or large campus facility, including supporting a site through production ramp.

 - Experience in aerospace, defense, or other regulated manufacturing, including ITAR and CUI environments.

 - Experience with Siemens Teamcenter or other MES and PLM platforms.

 - Deep experience with enterprise storage and data protection ecosystems such as NetApp, Pure Storage, Dell EMC, or Cohesity.

 - Experience with Entra ID, VDI platforms (VMware Horizon, Citrix, or Azure Virtual Desktop), and GPU or high-performance compute for engineering workloads.

 - Experience with Kubernetes or containerized workloads and the underlying compute and storage requirements.

 - Familiarity with OT security guidance such as IEC 62443 and NIST 800-82, and industrial protocols such as OPC UA.

 - Relevant technical certifications such as VMware VCP, Microsoft, NetApp, AWS, Azure, CISSP, or ITIL.

 - Customer Obsession: Our entire business is designed to ensure every agent built on Sierra succeeds, and that we are accountable to our customers and their success. We do whatever it takes to make our customers successful, and we go the extra mile in how we show up as a partner with unreasonable hospitality.

 - Craftsmanship: A great company is the aggregation of thousands of things done well. As they say, “how you do anything is how you do everything”. Most important is craftsmanship in building agents that are so great that people thank them at the end of a call. That’s the standard.

 - Intensity: We operate with urgency, and we want to win. We are never complacent. We fight to win every deal, big or small, using the full force of the company. And when we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

 - Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We work hard, and turn on the afterburners when needed. But we pick up our parents at the airport when they’re visiting from out of town. We go to our kids’ events. And we show up for one another, in moments of celebration and hardship.

ABOUT US

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Sierra was co-founded by Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/ who first met while working together at Google over 20 years ago. Bret currently serves as Chairman of the Board of Open AI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce and CTO of Facebook. Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design and deliver production-grade AI agents https://sierra.ai/blog/meet-the-ai-agent-engineer: You'll build and ship highly performant, reliable, and intuitive AI agents that are central, mission-critical and drive revenue directly to Sierra's growth. These aren't prototypes—they are powerful, scalable systems running in production environments across industries like finance, healthcare, and commerce.

 - Drive the Agent Development Life Cycle https://sierra.ai/blog/agent-development-life-cycle (ADLC): You'll have complete ownership and autonomy from initial pilot through deployment and continuous iteration. You'll be responsible for building, tuning, and evolving AI agents in production environments, defining the standard for ADLC best practices along the way.

 - Partner with large enterprises and cutting-edge startups: You’ll work directly with leaders at some of the world’s largest enterprises to understand their most pressing business challenges, and build AI agents that transform how they operate at scale. You'll also partner with the most cutting-edge startups, embedding AI agents across their entire business stack to drive innovation and efficiency.

 - Build the future of the platform: Your direct work with customers will guide the evolution of Sierra's core platform. You'll surface unmet needs, prototype new tools and features, and collaborate with research, product, and platform to shape the future of AI agent development and Sierra's product.


EXAMPLE PROJECTS

These are some examples of projects that engineers on our team have worked on recently:

 - Design and build AI agents for large telecommunications and media companies that consistently outperform human agents in managing subscription churn

 - Develop and refine AI agents capable of navigating complex customer interactions, like troubleshooting a broken device and personalising product recommendations

 - Create generalisable AI agent frameworks tailored for industry-specific use cases. See some examples in our financial services blog https://sierra.ai/blog/five-ways-to-use-ai-agents-financial-services!

 - Facilitate design partnerships for new product initiatives, such as new agent architectures, self-service capabilities, and generative agent development

 - Experiment with the latest voice models and figure out how to integrate them at scale to enterprise-grade customers


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Experience building and scaling end-to-end production systems

 - Strong technical problem-solving skills, especially in fast-changing, ambiguous environments

 - A builder and tinkerer’s mindset with high agency - you find creative ways to overcome obstacles and ship

 - Comfort working directly with customers to understand their needs and solve real-world problems

 - Excellent communication skills - clear, direct, and persuasive across technical and non-technical audiences


EVEN BETTER...

 - Experience building or deploying AI/LLM systems in production

 - Have been a founder or founding engineer - you know what it means to balance craft, ownership, and speed

 - Familiarity with tools that power today's AI agents: eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG pipelines, and prompt engineering

 - Prior experience with React, TypeScript, and/or Go

 - Previous roles where you interfaced with customers or led technical projects with external stakeholders

WHAT YOU'LL DO

As an Agent Strategist https://sierra.ai/blog/agent-strategist-your-phd-in-applied-ai, you own how Sierra's AI agents come to life for our customers — from first pilot to a production agent handling thousands of conversations a day. You sit at the intersection of product, building agents and customer-facing work, and stay just as close to the technology as you are to the people you build for. You transform a customer's thorniest, highest-stakes problems into agents that measurably move their business.

 - Own the Agent Development Life Cycle https://sierra.ai/blog/agent-development-life-cycle. Take agents from initial scope through conversation design, tooling, and evaluation, to launch and continuous iteration in production — translating business goals into an agent that outperforms, and tuning relentlessly until it's the best version of itself in the real world. You'll have real ownership and autonomy over the outcome.

 - Be the trusted strategic advisor to enterprise leaders. Sit shoulder-to-shoulder with our customers' executives, understand what success actually means to their business, and shape the AI strategy that gets them there.

 - Partner with the customer's working teams day to day. Run working sessions, troubleshoot the agent as issues come up, and make the calls that keep the build on track for launch.

 - Directly impact product. Surface unmet needs from your customer work, and feed them back to research and platform to shape where Sierra goes next.


EXAMPLE PROJECTS

These are the kinds of projects that strategists on our team have worked on recently:

 - Scope and launch a subscription-retention agent for a large telecommunications or media company that consistently outperforms human agents at saving at-risk customers.

 - Stand up an agent for a commerce customer that troubleshoots a broken device end-to-end and personalizes product recommendations in the same conversation.

 - Redesign the conversation flows for a financial services agent so it can handle complex, regulated interactions — and convert a pilot into a multi-team production deployment. See our financial services blog https://sierra.ai/blog/five-ways-to-use-ai-agents-financial-services for examples.

 - Partner with product on a net-new capability — a new agent architecture or self-service tooling — using a live customer as the design partner.

 - Define the evaluation and quality bar for a new agent, then use those metrics to drive a measurable lift in outcome https://sierra.ai/blog/outcome-based-pricing-for-ai-agents week over week.


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Customer obsession. Genuine energy being in front of customers — understanding their business and needs, thriving in complex organizations, and building trusted relationships.

 - Communication. Clear, direct, and persuasive across technical and non-technical audiences.

 - Strategic problem-solving in ambiguity. Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills to break down complex problems, spot risks early, and adapt as things change fast.

 - Technical aptitude. Comfortable engaging directly with technical concepts - reading API documentation, understanding data models and system architecture, and following engineering tradeoffs in a design discussion.

 - Ownership and delivery. A track record of running multiple complex, high-visibility projects at once and driving them to outcomes.


EVEN BETTER...

 - Experience building or deploying AI/LLM agents in production — hands-on with the tools behind them (eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG, prompt engineering) — working closely with technical counterparts.

 - You've been a founder, founding team member, or operator — you know how to balance craft, ownership, and speed.

 - A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience — and/or an MBA or comparable experience at the intersection of technology and business.

ABOUT US

Sieve is a multimodal data lab building high-quality training datasets and evaluation environments for frontier AI across audiovisual modeling, robotics, and multimodal interaction. We pair exabyte-scale data infrastructure and global data collection operations with multimodal research to help machines learn how the world looks, sounds, moves, and responds. Currently, the leave management process is painful and inefficient for everyone. Company leaders struggle to keep up with regulations and processes that change frequently, and the employees going on leave are overwhelmed by bureaucracy at an exceptionally important juncture in their career. Sparrow transforms this ordinarily tedious, error-prone, complex to remain compliant, and time-consuming process into a 30-minute end-to-end experience saving teams time (20 - 40 hours per leave) and money (up to $30K per leave).

Sparrow is headquartered in San Francisco but all employees work remotely across the country. Sparrow is a diverse, highly talented, and supportive team. Together, we are hardworking, collaborative, smart, and humble—after all, we’re solving real problems.

As an early member of the engineering leadership team, you will have a significant opportunity to play a pivotal role in Sparrow’s growth and setting the direction and culture of the engineering team.

 - Nurture and develop a team culture that values collaboration, engineering excellence, psychological safety, and pragmatic execution.

ABOUT US

Our mission is to reinvent the way people learn, starting with language.

Learning a language can change a life by opening doors to new cultures, careers, and communities. Two billion people around the world are actively trying to learn a language, but the best way to learn (one-on-one tutoring) is hard to access at scale and hasn’t been meaningfully improved in decades. Speak is building a human-level, AI-powered tutor in your pocket: a conversation-first experience that lets learners actually speak, get instant feedback, and progress through carefully designed lessons. The result is a complete path from beginner to confident speaker across multiple languages.

Speak first launched in South Korea in 2019, where Speak has now become the number one language learning app, and we now serve learners across many markets and 15+ languages. Speak is one of the world’s leading AI companies, with over $150m raised in venture investment from OpenAI, Accel, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and more, with a distributed team across San Francisco, Seoul, Tokyo, Taipei, and Ljubljana.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

We're looking for an engineer to join Speak's Infra Platform team at a pivotal moment: software development is undergoing a fundamental shift toward agentic workflows, and we're embracing it.

Your team's mission is to help every engineering team at Speak own and operate its infrastructure. You'll provide reliable foundations, self-serve tooling, sensible guardrails, and hands-on guidance so teams can ship high-quality features quickly while delivering a state-of-the-art customer experience.

The scope is broad and consequential: you'll drive velocity, reliability, and performance across our client apps, web, API, and infrastructure, while improving developer productivity. When Speak is fast and stable for millions of learners—and engineers can ship without friction—that's your team's impact.

You'll also help lead Speak's agentic engineering transformation: moving beyond using AI to code faster and toward designing the systems, environments, and feedback loops that enable agents to work with increasing autonomy and quality. Platform is where that leverage compounds. The tools, environments, and guardrails you build will shape how effectively agents can work across the organization. We believe this shift is widening the gap between teams that fully embrace it and those that don't, and we're building for the former.

We're looking for engineers who are excited to use coding agents to build faster, stay deep in the details, and lead by example.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Designing, building, and shipping the platform and infrastructure that other engineering teams rely on, using coding agents to move faster than was previously possible

 - Driving velocity and reliability across client apps, web, API, and infrastructure, and setting a high quality bar through your own work and your reviews

 - Leading the agentic engineering transformation from the front: constantly asking what's still being done manually, identifying slowdowns and roadblocks, and building the tooling, environments, and feedback loops that close the gap

 - Improving the agent environment so coding agents can do increasingly autonomous, high-quality work across the org

 - Collaborating closely with partner functions like Product and Design to execute effectively in the AI era

 - Proactively pushing for changes to shared infrastructure, tooling, and systems that help the broader engineering org become more agentic
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 8+ years of software engineering experience on fast-paced, high performance teams

 - Strong backend, systems, platform/infra, or performance background

 - Deeply technical and building faster than ever with coding agents

 - Track record of technical leadership: setting direction, driving projects across teams, and influencing without formal authority

 - Strong conviction that 10x engineering output is possible with agentic tools and practices

 - Proven ability to drive velocity, hold a high quality bar, and give direct, constructive feedback

 - Excited about working in-person in San Francisco at least 3-4 days per week




AI-NATIVE SOFTWARE ENGINEER

You won't necessarily be working on "core AI" features, but we expect you to be AI-native in how you work: using AI tools every day to design, build, test, and debug, and always looking for ways to ship faster and better with them.




WHY WORK AT SPEAK

ABOUT US


Every 10 minutes, 18 million conversations happen between businesses and consumers around the world.


For decades, the consumer side of those conversations sucked: long queues, robotic menus, repeated explanations, and advice that is often unhelpful. Most people today still cannot simply say what their problem is in natural language when communicating with businesses.


AI changes that. For the first time, companies can have natural conversations with customers at massive scale. Every B2C company - from energy providers to telcos to insurers - will use AI agents to interact with their customers. The number of conversations businesses will handle is going to explode in the coming years.


At telli, we are solving the challenges that come with that shift. Today, leading B2C companies like Sky are already using telli to deploy thousands of agents to provide their customers with a new experience. But building a first agent is easy, getting it to drive real outcomes for customers and businesses is the hard part. telli helps companies build, deploy, and improve consumer-facing AI agents at scale. This will become one of the most important software categories of the next decade, and we intend to win it.


We are a small, AI-pilled team that likes to solve hard problems. Be it engineering, product, or GTM - we build, experiment, and move fast, while heavily leveraging the capabilities of AI models. ROLE SUMMARY

Temporal is rapidly scaling its field organization, and setting up every seller to succeed, from day one and well beyond, is critical to meeting and exceeding our most ambitious goals.

As a GTM Enablement Manager, Field Training & Readiness, you’ll be the face of enablement in front of our sales teams. You’ll lead the live sessions where new hires and tenured sellers build the skills and confidence to have great customer conversations: bootcamp modules, workshops, role plays, and ongoing skills sessions. You’ll work from a defined track and a curriculum built with the enablement team, and you’ll bring it to life with your stories, your energy, and your read of the room.

If you’re energized by being in front of a room, believe training should be memorable and behavior-changing rather than a slide-reading exercise, and want to partner closely with the sales and BDR teams on the ground, this role is for you.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Deliver training that sticks. Lead a regular cadence of live, interactive sessions for Account Executives and BDRs and other customer-facing roles, including new hire cohorts, skills workshops, and role plays. Your sessions are built around practice, not presentation.

 - Own your delivery track. Take ownership of a defined slate of programs and a delivery calendar. You’ll work from a curriculum built with the broader enablement team and make it your own through storytelling, real examples, and adapting on the fly. You’ll also flag what’s working and what isn’t so the content keeps getting better.

 - Partner with the field. Stay close to the sales and BDR teams in Atlanta and beyond. Show up in team meetings, run role-play and call-practice reinforcement with managers, and bring what you hear (what’s resonating, where reps are stuck) back to the enablement team.

 - Bring in the experts. You won’t be the expert on everything, and you don’t need to be. You’ll deliver the fundamentals with confidence and know when to pull in an AE, SA, or product expert to take a session deeper.

 - Close the loop. Gather feedback and simple leading indicators (participation, skill demonstration, manager input) after every session and use them to iterate.

 - Pitch in on the work behind the work. Scheduling, session prep, LMS updates, and content upkeep are shared across the team. You’ll own your share.

 - Flex where the impact is. The core of this role is training delivery. As the team and the field grow, there will be room to expand into onboarding, BDR enablement, and broader field readiness.


WHO YOU ARE (NEED TO HAVES)

 - Location: Atlanta metro area, or willingness to relocate. This role involves in-person collaboration with our sales and BDR teams, with a strong preference for 1-2 days a week in the office. In-person attendance is required for biweekly bootcamp delivery.

 - You’re a natural facilitator. You come alive in front of a room. You’re outgoing, personable, and engaging; you use stories to make concepts real, and you can hold a room’s attention for hours. Your strength is how you facilitate, not just how you present: you read the audience, draw people in, and adapt on the fly. People leave your sessions feeling equipped, not talked at.

 - You have a credible foundation in sales or enablement. You come from one of two places: you’ve spent 2+ years in a sales role (AE or BDR/SDR management) and want to move into enablement, or you’ve spent 5+ years delivering sales training or enablement at a comparable company or level. Either way, sellers listen to you because you understand their reality and speak their language.

 - You earn credibility with humility. You know you aren’t the expert in our product or our customers. You build trust by being curious, prepared, and honest about what you know, and by bringing the right people into the room when it matters.

 - You’re coachable and a team player. You take feedback well, you ask for it, and you improve fast. Enablement touches every part of the business, and you’re as comfortable collaborating as you are owning your own work.

 - You’re a builder who executes. You thrive where things aren’t fully figured out yet. You move fast, hold a high bar for quality, and run through walls to get things delivered, including the logistics.

 - You’re AI-forward and always raising the bar. The way enablement gets done has fundamentally shifted. You’re already using AI, whether to prep and personalize sessions or to focus on the highest-leverage work, and you don’t settle for how it’s always been done.


YOU’LL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF

 - You have a deep passion for Temporal’s mission and what we’re building for developers.

 - You’ve enabled or sold into teams working with highly technical or infrastructure products, sold to developers, and/or navigated bottoms-up OSS/PLG and tops-down sales motions.

 - You have experience enabling BDR/SDR teams, or you’ve led one.

 - You’re familiar with Command of the Message and MEDDPICC, or you’ve facilitated a comparable sales methodology.

 - You’ve enabled multiple audiences (e.g. AEs, BDRs, SAs, Managers).

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are hiring our first dedicated BDR Manager to lead a team of high-performing BDRs at different stages of ramp. Reporting to the Director of Sales, you will own that team: who we hire, how fast they ramp, how well they sell, and how many of them are ready for the next role. We want a manager who builds reps up by coaching them on real calls, not one who watches a dashboard. You will work every day with the AE manager and the account executives who take the meetings your team books. This role carries no personal quota.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Coach every BDR every week: review recorded calls against one shared rubric and give specific feedback the same week.

 - Run weekly one-to-ones and a weekly lost-call review, and join call blocks so the team hears what good sounds like.

 - Set monthly targets by rep and by stage of ramp, hold the team to them, and manage sustained underperformance early and fairly.

 - Run the promotion path from ramp to BDR to Senior BDR to AE, tell every rep where they stand, and bring the next account executives out of this team.

 - Own hiring for the team: source, interview and select BDRs.

 - Run onboarding from our BDR playbook, with certification, a 30-60-90 ramp and clear milestones, and shorten the time from start date to first meeting booked and to full targets.

 - Report weekly, by rep and for the team, on dials, connect rate, meetings booked, meetings held and pipeline created

 - Find where the funnel leaks and fix it with coaching, list changes, messaging or process

 - Work cross-functionally on ICP, lead routing, inbound follow-up and attribution.

 - Own the BDR playbook: target lists, sequences, talk tracks, objection handling and competitor responses.

 - Keep HubSpot and dialer data clean enough to trust.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - Previous experience managing BDRs or SDRs, on a team of five or more, in B2B SaaS or fintech, with a record of hitting meeting and pipeline targets.

THE ROLE

We're hiring a B2B Sales Manager to drive enterprise and API adoption of Viggle's four product lines — Viggle Video, 3D Character, Mocap, and Text-to-Motion — within the gaming and interactive entertainment industry.

WHO YOU ARE


REQUIRED EXPERIENCE

 - Experience running the full sales cycle independently — prospecting, demoing, negotiating, and closing — without heavy hand-holding or inbound support.

 - Excellent communication and presentation skills; comfortable presenting to executives, product leaders, and technical stakeholders.

 - A demonstrated ability to learn a new, technical product or unfamiliar industry quickly and become credible in it.

 - Self-starter who thrives in a fast-moving startup environment with minimal supervision.

 - Based in our Toronto office and able to travel occasionally in the United States; authorized to work in Canada.


STRONG SIGNALS

 - You've operated in a high-accountability, high-rejection environment before — commission-only sales, door-to-door or B2C canvassing, competitive athletics at a high level, structured military or first-responder service, or another pursuit that required daily discipline and the ability to keep showing up after being told no.

 - Familiarity with AI-powered video and motion generation tools and the emerging AI + gaming landscape.

 - Experience at an early-stage startup, building sales processes and playbooks from scratch.

 - A personal system for staying disciplined and consistent — whatever that looks like for you.


YOU ARE

 - A hunter — you generate your own pipeline and don't wait for leads to come to you.

 - Resilient — rejection doesn't slow you down; you've built habits that keep you consistent under pressure.

 - Consultative — you sell by understanding the client's production challenges, not by pushing features.

 - A fast learner — you can walk into an unfamiliar domain and earn credibility quickly.

 - Organized and data-driven — you run a disciplined pipeline and forecast accurately.

 - Low ego, high output — you care about results more than recognition.


WHY THIS ROLE

 - Sell AI video and motion APIs at the frontier of AI and gaming — a market moving faster than any in entertainment technology.

 - Own a market: you'll be the founding sales presence for Viggle in the US, with direct access to leadership.

 - Shape go-to-market strategy, pricing, and playbooks from the ground up.


COMPENSATION & CAREER DEVELOPMENT

 - Base Salary 80K to 120k + 15% on sales up to your $1M annual quota, with an accelerated 15–20% rate on anything closed beyond quota.

 - Group benefits, including dental, massage therapy, and physiotherapy coverage.

 - Two weeks of paid vacation to start.

 - A real path into sales leadership as we scale the US team — join early and help build it from the ground up, not slot into an existing structure.

 - Clear & Empathetic Communication: Ability to communicate transparently and confidently in plain language, escalating issues early and explaining complex payroll matters to non-technical stakeholders.

 - Resourceful Ownership & Agility: A roll-up-your-sleeves, self-directed mindset with the ability to navigate ambiguity, simplify complex workflows, and continuously improve operational processes.

The Role We are looking for an exceptional Product Marketing Manager to own the product marketing plan and drive market adoption for Veeva Ostro, the leading conversational AI platform for life sciences brands. Operating with the speed and autonomy of a startup inside Veeva, you will translate AI capabilities into clear, compelling value that resonates with buyers. You will collaborate closely with strategy, product management, sales, and customer success to shape messaging, build practical sales enablement, drive content marketing, capture customer case studies, and prepare thought leadership presentations for industry events. This role is ideal for a strong writer who works independently, moves fast with high quality, and knows how to market AI software based on real business value.
  • Own the Product Marketing Plan: Build and execute the end-to-end marketing plan for Ostro, collaborating closely with strategy, product management, sales, and customer success to drive awareness and adoption.
  • Shape & Apply Messaging: Partner on core positioning and translate it into clear, differentiated product messaging across all sales and marketing channels.
  • Build Sales Enablement & Collateral: Create and maintain a library of practical sales tools, including pitch decks, product briefs, demo scripts, and competitive battlecards, that empower our sales team to win.
  • Drive Content Marketing: Write and produce high-impact content, such as thought leadership articles, website copy, blog posts, and product videos, that clearly articulates the benefits of Ostro.
  • Capture Customer Case Studies: Work directly with customers to turn their real-world results into case studies, testimonials, and customer advocacy assets.
  • Event Thought Leadership: Partner with customers and Ostro leadership to build compelling presentations for industry conferences and events.
  • B2B Product Marketing Experience: 5+ years in B2B SaaS product marketing, ideally at a hypergrowth startup or within a fast-moving business unit.
  • AI Product Marketing Experience: Proven experience marketing AI-powered software, specifically translating capabilities into concrete customer outcomes rather than buzzwords.
  • Authentic, Clear Writing: Demonstrated ability to turn positioning into crisp, compelling messaging and write strong product content (decks, datasheets, blogs, and speeches).
  • High Ownership & Startup Speed: Able to own a plan end-to-end, work independently with little oversight, ship quickly, and adapt as priorities shift.
  • Cross-Functional & Customer Presence: Experienced partnering with strategy, product, sales, and customer success, and comfortable working directly with customers and executives on conference presentations.
  • Experience in life sciences, healthcare technology, patient engagement, or commercial pharma software.
  • Proven success bringing innovative B2B cloud or AI offerings to market.
