Vultr is seeking a Manager of DC Commercial Diligence to support commercial due diligence across our data center acquisition pipeline. This is a hands-on underwriting role: for every site Vultr pursues, whether an operator colocation lease, a powered shell, a lease-to-own structure, or a powered land purchase, you will work the data room directly, build out findings, and bring a well-supported point of view to the Senior Manager on whether the deal is what it claims to be. You will build fluency across power availability and energy commercial terms, counterparty and lease economics, and the deal model, and your work will directly inform the Go/No-Go recommendations and negotiating positions the Senior Manager brings to investment gates on transactions worth tens to hundreds of millions of dollars. Your job is to be constructively adversarial to every deal: the diligence function exists to find what the seller's materials do not say.



Key Responsibilities

 - Support commercial due diligence end to end for active acquisitions: review documents in the data room, maintain the findings register, and prepare evidence-based materials for investment gates alongside the Senior Manager

 - Diligence power under guidance: interconnection queue position versus contracted capacity, utility and ESA terms, tariff structure, curtailment provisions, demand charge pass-throughs, and power-on forecast credibility, flagging where bankable capacity and marketing figures diverge

 - Diligence counterparties: operator financial health and credit, guarantor structure, lease terms including minimum power obligations, escalations, expansion rights, termination provisions, and service level commitments

 - Build and maintain components of the deal model: total development cost, fit-out and NRC comparisons, yield, tax and incentive assumptions, and sensitivity to power cost and ramp scenarios, under the Senior Manager's review

 - Verify seller claims against primary sources: utility confirmations, interconnection studies, executed versus draft agreements, title and site control instruments

 - Draft Go/No-Go packages, risk registers, and challenge questions for operators; run day-to-day RFI cycles through resolution

 - Support the Senior Manager, Director, and Acquisitions Managers with diligence-derived data and analysis; do not carry deal negotiation

 - Escalate findings transparently through the Senior Manager, including adverse findings that may be unwelcome to the deal team

 - Coordinate with external counsel and consultants on legal, environmental, and specialty workstreams under the Senior Manager's direction

 - Help pre-qualify pipeline sites toward proposal-ready status so sales never offers an unvetted site

 - Apply and help refine repeatable diligence frameworks, checklists, and data room standards across deal types

 - Track diligence performance metrics: cycle time per deal, findings volume and severity, and post-close issue rate
   
   

Qualifications

 - 3-6 years in data center, energy, or infrastructure transactions with hands-on exposure to due diligence: you have worked in data rooms and contributed to investment views, even if final sign-off sat with others

 - Working familiarity with power markets: interconnection processes and queue mechanics, utility tariffs, energy services agreements, and power purchase agreement structures as applied to data centers

 - Solid understanding of data center lease structures, operator economics, and mission-critical delivery commitments

 - Strong financial modeling ability in Excel: comfortable building and maintaining components of a development cost, returns, and scenario model

 - Demonstrated attention to detail in finding discrepancies in deal materials: capacity claims that did not hold, unexecuted agreements presented as commitments, terms with hidden exposure

 - Able to synthesize a large document set into clear, evidence-cited findings for review by senior stakeholders

 - Comfortable managing multiple concurrent diligences in a fast-moving deal environment, with guidance from the Senior Manager

 - Bachelor's degree required; coursework or certification in finance, engineering, or energy valued



Preferred Experience

 - Infrastructure private equity, investment banking, or project finance deal teams; hyperscaler energy or site acquisition; IPP or utility origination; data center operator corporate development

 - Exposure to behind-the-meter generation and natural gas supply arrangements (firm transport, MDCQ, balancing)

Senior / Staff Software Engineer, Camera Integration
San Francisco, CA | San Francisco, CA | Toronto, ON | Pittsburgh, PA

Waabi, founded by AI visionary Raquel Urtasun, is the leader in Physical AI. With a world-class team, we're unlocking the next era of autonomous transportation with technology that's powering commercial autonomous trucks and robotaxis. Waabi is backed by and partners with world leaders in AI, automotive, logistics, and deep tech.
 
With offices in Toronto, San Francisco, Dallas, and Pittsburgh, Waabi is growing quickly and looking for diverse, innovative and collaborative candidates who want to impact the world in a positive way. To learn more visit: www.waabi.ai


Robots need to see the world they live in to make informed decisions. The Onboard Sensors Team brings that sight to our robot autonomous vehicles, and cameras are the richest and most demanding sensors on the vehicles. We are looking for an engineer who knows cameras end to end: from the image sensor and serializer, over the GMSL link, through the driver and ISP, to frames arriving on time in our autonomy stack.
 
You will own the camera side of our sensor platform, work with live vehicles every day, and help shape how our camera systems scale from today's fleet to production. Our team is small and hands-on, so you will also set the bar for camera knowledge and mentor engineers who are newer to the domain. 
 
You will…
Own camera integration on the Waabi Driver: bring-up, configuration, drivers and the path from the image sensor to GMSL link to the autonomy stack.
Debug camera issues on real vehicles operating in the field daily — dropped or corrupted frames, link errors, flicker, exposure problems — and trace them to the cable, serializer, deserializer, driver or application.
Make camera data trustworthy in time: hardware triggering, frame timestamping and synchronization with the rest of the sensor suite.
Tune and validate image quality with our perception and science partners: ISP settings, exposure and HDR control, and performance in hard lighting such as night, glare and tunnels.
Evaluate new cameras and vendors, and integrate them into existing and future onboard platforms.
Build the diagnostics and observability that tell us which component dropped a frame, and why.
Work closely with operations and hardware teams to understand live system behavior and mature our camera platform toward production.
 
Qualifications:
6+ years of industry experience, including hands-on work integrating cameras into fielded systems (automotive, AV, robotics, drones or similar).
Deep understanding of the camera hardware pipeline: image sensors, SerDes links (ADI/Maxim GMSL or TI FPD-Link), triggering, and how pixels get from the sensor over the wire into memory.
Hands-on SerDes experience: configuring and debugging ADI/Maxim GMSL2/GMSL3 or TI FPD-Link III/IV serializers and deserializers (e.g. MAX9295/MAX9296/MAX96712, DS90UB953/DS90UB960), including link training, I2C passthrough and link-error diagnostics.
Experience with Linux camera stacks below the application level: V4L2, kernel drivers, device tree, DMA and buffer management.
Proficiency in Rust or C/C++ in real-time, resource-constrained environments (we use Rust).
A track record of independently debugging hard camera problems on real hardware, not only in simulation or offline data.
Collaborating with large teams that span engineering, hardware and operations.
 
Bonus:
Experience with NVIDIA Jetson/DRIVE camera frameworks or similar automotive SoCs.
ISP and image-quality tuning: exposure, HDR, white balance, color.
Time synchronization in multi-sensor systems (PTP, hardware triggers, frame timestamping).
Electronics experience: reading schematics, signal integrity, and using an oscilloscope or protocol analyzer.
Experience evaluating camera vendors or working closely with camera suppliers.
Familiarity with other sensor modalities (lidar, radar, GNSS/IMU).
Passionate about self-driving technology and about efficient, readable, testable code.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

🛠️ About our Technical Operations Teams

 

Wayve’s Technical Operations function is the critical bridge between Product, Engineering, and Operations. We thrive in dynamic, high-growth environments, turning complex technical strategies into actionable field operations that set the standard for autonomy at scale.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

 

You’ll stand up and run technical operations in new markets—planning data collection campaigns, preparing vehicles and operators for launch, and running live robotaxi services with our ridehail partners. Your work will build the feedback loops that convert on-road data, operator insights, and service metrics into continuous product enhancements, demonstrating improvements through live operations. You’ll drive the pace and reliability required to deliver commercial services where customer experience and operational reliability are measured daily.

 

🧩 What you’ll be working on

 

 - Market launch readiness: Turn program plans into clear, actionable launch plans by market, covering vehicle commissioning, operator readiness, route and ODD validation, and safety sign-offs. Lead go/no-go reviews across multiple regions.

 - Third-party operator performance: Manage operating relationships with subcontracted partners, set and review SLAs and performance standards, run audit cycles, and drive corrective actions.

 - Operator standards and train-the-trainer: Partner with Training to ensure trainers are certified, curricula keep pace with releases, and operator competence is consistently assessed in every market.

 - Release and change management: Coordinate how software and model releases reach the road, from operator briefings and in-car checks to staged rollouts and structured field feedback.

 - Performance reporting: Own weekly product performance reporting—including autonomy time, pickups/drop-offs, km driven, and safety events—and turn trends into priority actions for Operations, Engineering, and Product.

 - Field-to-model feedback loops: Be the link between on-road operations and model, product, and research teams. Triage on-road events, route insights, and design targeted testing to close data gaps.

 - Scaling the playbook: Improve processes, SOPs, and tooling so each new market launches faster and more safely.

 

🙌 You should apply if

 

Essential:

 - Experience in technical program management or operations roles at the intersection of R&D, product development, and field testing in high-complexity environments (e.g., autonomous systems, robotics, aerospace, advanced mobility).

 - Proven track record of managing programs, demonstrations, or operations that require close coordination between technical development teams and field execution.

 - Experience managing third-party vendors or subcontractors against SLAs, including performance audits and corrective action plans.

 - Deep experience with test planning, operational readiness frameworks, and structured field-to-technical feedback loops.

 - Ability to influence across teams and geographies in fast-moving technology environments.

 - Strong facilitation and stakeholder management skills, with experience leading cross-functional workshops and coordinating across Engineering, Science, Product, and Operations.

 - Proficiency with operational data: defining metrics, creating/interpreting dashboards, and using them to identify bottlenecks.

 - Clear written communication, including SOPs, launch checklists, and executive updates.

 - Comfort with ambiguity and competing priorities.

 - Willing to travel up to 30% across launch markets.

 

Desirable:

 - Experience in autonomous vehicles, advanced driver assistance systems, or rideshare/mobility marketplace operations.

 - Background in safety management systems, incident investigation or operator competence frameworks.

 - Experience with AV permitting or deployment in one or more markets.

 - Comfortable with project management tools (e.g., Confluence, Asana/Jira) and implementing operational tracking systems.

 - Knowledge of process improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) or operational excellence frameworks.

 - Familiarity with vehicle commissioning, fleet management systems, or automotive safety protocols.

 

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

 

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

 

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

 

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.
